## 7. Reel motion, input and settle logic

### 7.1 State

- `pos` (current reel coordinate, tiles), `tgt` (target), `cur` (active project index), `mode` ∈ {`home`, `opening`, `case`, `closing`, `index`}, `lastIn` (timestamp of the last wheel/drag input), `ref` (reel centre of the project the current gesture started from, or null).
- Initial: `pos = tgt = 0.5` (project 0 centred), `cur = 0`, mode `home`.
- **wrapNear(c, ref)** = `c + round((ref − c)/16)·16` — the copy of reel coordinate c closest to ref.
- **Per frame smoothing**: `dt = min(0.05, frameDelta seconds)`; `pos += (tgt − pos) · (1 − e^(−5.5·dt))` (critically-damped-feeling exponential ease, frame-rate independent).
- **Active project**: tile `floor(pos)` mod 16 → its project. When it differs from `cur`: direction = +1 if `((a − cur) mod 6) ≤ 3` else −1; set `cur = a`; call setRoll(a, dir) and setNext(a). So titles update as soon as the boundary tile crosses the centre, mid-scroll.

### 7.2 Gestures and settle (home mode only)

- **startGesture()**: if `ref` is null, set `ref = wrapNear(PSTART[cur] + .5, pos)`.
- **Wheel** (window listener, passive): in home, startGesture(), then add the dominant-axis delta (deltaX if |deltaX| > |deltaY|, else deltaY) × **0.0032** tiles to `tgt`; set `lastIn = now`. In case mode (and Read more card closed) route to the gallery wheel. In index mode add `deltaY × 0.006` to the index target.
- **Drag** (pointer events on the canvas, home only): on pointerdown capture the pointer, reset `ref = null` then startGesture(), record start x, start `tgt`, `moved = 0`, last x/time, velocity 0, add `body.grab`.
  - One tile in pixels for dragging: `tilePx = H · 0.49 · 16/9` (the centre tile width).
  - pointermove: `dx` = clientX − start x; `moved = max(moved, |dx|)`; instantaneous velocity = Δx/Δt (px per ms, Δt ≥ 1); smoothed `v = v·0.6 + inst·0.4`. `tgt = startTgt − dx / tilePx` (drag left → reel advances); additionally `pos += (tgt − pos)·0.65` so the reel tracks the finger tightly; `lastIn = now`.
  - pointerup / pointercancel: remove `grab`. If `moved < 6px` it is a **click**: reset ref; if in home and the pointer is in the **central hit zone** (|x − W/2| < 0.3W and 0.18H < y < 0.78H) open the case for `cur`. Otherwise it is a **fling**: `tgt −= v · 260 / tilePx`, then `tgt = settle(tgt)`, `ref = null`, `lastIn = 0`.
- **Idle settle for wheel**: every frame, in home, not dragging, and **more than 380ms** since the last input: if `ref` is not null, `tgt = settle(tgt)` and `ref = null`.
- **settle(x)**: let `r = ref` (or x if null), `d = x − r`.
  - If `|d| < 0.18` tiles → return r (snap back to the project you started on; gesture threshold **0.18 tile**).
  - Otherwise, among all six project centres wrapped near x, consider only those strictly in the gesture direction from r (`(c − r)·d > 0.01`) and return the one **closest to x**. Result: any gesture beyond the threshold lands on the **next or previous project in the gesture direction** (a big fling can travel further — it lands on whichever centre in that direction is nearest to where the fling ended), never back on the start.
- **goP(i)**: `ref = null`; i wrapped to 0–5; `tgt = wrapNear(PSTART[i] + .5, pos)`. Next button → goP(cur + 1); Prev → goP(cur − 1).

### 9.5 Gallery behaviour (vertical filmstrip)

- Frame height `fh = innerWidth · 0.46 · 9/16`; gap `= innerHeight · 0.07` (**7vh**).
- Each frame j: `margin-top: −fh/2` px (centred on the 50% line) and `transform: translateY((j − gi)·(fh + gap) px)`. The active frame sits in the vertical centre; others stack above/below with 7vh gaps (neighbours partly visible at top and bottom of the viewport).
- Non-active frames have class `off`: **`filter: blur(16px) brightness(.42)`** (dark theme). In light theme: `blur(16px) brightness(1.05) saturate(.6) opacity(.55)`. Active frame has no filter. Filter and transform both transition 1s `--ease`.
- Night Harbour frame 0 contains a `<video>` (muted, loop, playsinline, crossorigin anonymous, src = VIDEO, autoplay via play()) absolutely filling the frame with `object-fit:cover`, on top of its poster crop, plus the **player bar** (9.6).
- **Wheel in case** (only when the card is closed): ignore if |deltaY| < 4 or if within the **750ms lock** after the last accepted step; otherwise lock for 750ms and step by sign(deltaY).
- **caseStep(d)**: `gi = clamp(gi + d, 0, 7)`; if unchanged do nothing; else re-layout. No wrap.
- Clicking a non-active frame jumps to it; clicking a rail thumbnail jumps to it.

### 9.6 Player bar (`#player.ui`, only inside the video frame)

- Absolute, left 0, right 0, **bottom −30px** (sits just below the frame), flex, align centre, gap 8px.
- Children in order: `❚❚`, `Pause`, a `.bar` (flex 1, height 1px, background `var(--line)`, position relative, containing an `<i>` absolutely positioned left/top/bottom 0 with background `var(--fg)` and no width set — i.e. an empty progress fill), then `⤢`. Non-functional.
- Layout sets the player's inline opacity to 1 when gi = 0 and 0 otherwise.

### 9.7 Rolling counter and thumbnail rail

- **Counter**: `.d` is a window of height **2.5vw** with `overflow:hidden`, containing a column of spans `01`…`08` (each block, height 2.5vw). The column translates `translateY(−gi·2.5vw)` with `transition: transform .9s var(--ease)` — digits roll vertically. Below it `.tot` shows the total `08` in `var(--mute)` with margin-top **.35vw**.
- **Rail**: 8 thumbnails `<i>`, each block, width **5.2vw**, `aspect-ratio:16/9`, cropped from the sheet with the crop helper, `filter: brightness(.4)`, `transition: filter .5s, transform .5s var(--out)`. Active thumb `on`: no filter and `translateX(−.8vw)` (pops left). Thumb step `th = innerWidth·0.052·9/16 + 6` px; the rail's transform is `translateY(−gi·th − th/2)` px so the active thumb is centred on the 50% line (transform .9s `--ease`).

## 10. Open / close transitions (exact timeline)

All "ease" below = `cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)`; "out" = `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`.

### 10.1 openCase(i) — only from home

| t (ms) | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | `mode = 'opening'`. `tgt = wrapNear(PSTART[i] + .5, pos)` (finish centring the project). buildCase(i). Add **`body.out`**: the title roller hides all non-current lines and the slide drops **8.4vw** down over **.5s ease**; the `#nx` controls drop by `100% + 4vh` over **.5s ease**. |
| 330 | Add **`body.case`**: case layer clip-path animates `inset(0 0 100% 0)` → `inset(0 0 0 0)` over **.8s ease** — the page **wipes down from the top**. The WebGL reel keeps rendering curved beneath it. |
| 330 + staggers (delays measured from adding `case`) | **Gallery** `#gal`: from `translateY(22vh)` to none over **1.25s out**, delay **.1s** (slides up). **Title lines**: inner spans from `translateY(105%)` to none over **.8s out**, line 1 delay **.62s**, line 2 delay **.72s** (roll up out of their masks). **Counter**: clip-path `inset(100% 0 0 0)` → `inset(0)` over **.8s out**, delay **.7s** (reveals bottom-up). **Back**: opacity 0 → **.6**, .5s, delay **.85s**. **Film, Read more, Rail**: opacity 0 → 1, .5s, delay **.95s** (rail transform keeps its .9s ease). **Player**: opacity → 1, .5s, delay **1s**. |
| 1250 | `mode = 'case'` (input enabled for the case). |

### 10.2 closeCase() — only from case

| t (ms) | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | Remove `body.read` (card slides out). `mode = 'closing'`. Remove **`body.case`**: clip-path animates back to `inset(0 0 100% 0)` over .8s ease — the case **wipes up** to the top revealing the curved reel. All inner case elements keep their entered state during the wipe because their un-case transitions are `0s` duration with **.8s delay**: after .8s (fully covered) gallery jumps back to `translateY(22vh)`, title spans to `translateY(105%)`, counter to clipped, back/film/more/rail/player to opacity 0 — ready for the next open. |
| 620 | Remove **`body.out`**: title slide returns to 0 with **.55s ease, .1s delay** and the `#nx` controls rise back with the same .55s/.1s; non-current title lines become visible again. |
| 1150 | `mode = 'home'`. |

- Fixed inset 0, z-index **40**, background **#121212**, colour **#f4f2ee** (always dark, regardless of theme). `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` → `body.index`: `inset(0 0 0 0)`, `transition: clip-path .9s var(--ease)` (wipes down from the top; covers the top bar).
- **Open** from the top-bar index button or the `Works` nav (allowed in home or case mode): remove `body.read`, remember the previous mode, `mode = 'index'`, set index target and value to `cur`, add `body.index`. Home overlay fades to opacity 0 (.4s).
- **Close button** `#xclose`: absolute, left 1.6vw, top 20px, z 2; contains a **3×3** `.dots` grid (`grid-template-columns: 3px 3px 3px`) rotated **45°** (reads as an ×/diamond of dots).
- **Red hairline** `#hair`: absolute, full width, top 50%, height 1px, background **rgba(255,43,43,.55)**.
- **Thumbnail** `#ithumb`: absolute, left 1.6vw, top 50%, width **10.5vw**, aspect 16/9, `translateY(-50%)`, cropped from the sheet to the **first cell of the highlighted project** (crop helper), no transition.
- **Meta** `#imeta`: absolute, left **29vw**, top 50%, `translateY(-120%)` (sits just above the hairline), **7px**, line-height 1.4, opacity .55, uppercase, letter-spacing .1em. Content: first segment of the category (text before the first ` · `, e.g. `Documentary`) + line break + year.
- **List** `#ilist.big`: absolute, left **33vw**, top 0, bottom 0, right 0. Contains **18 items** (three copies of the six titles), each a `div[data-i]` absolutely positioned at left 0, font-size **4.3vw**, line-height 1, height **4.6vw**, nowrap, colour **#3a3a3a**, `transform-origin: 0 50%`, `transition: color .35s`. Each title is in an inline-block span skewed **skewX(-11deg)** with `transition: transform .5s var(--out)`.
- **Highlighted item** (`on`): colour **#f4f2ee**; its span becomes `skewX(-11deg) translateX(2.2vw)` (slides right).
- **Infinite positioning, every frame while the index is open**: line step `lh = innerWidth·0.046`; ease `idxV += (idxT − idxV)·0.12`; for item k (0–17), `y = k − idxV − 6`, wrapped into the range [−9, 9) (total 18); `transform: translateY(H/2 + y·lh − lh/2 px)`. The item at y≈0 sits centred on the red hairline; the list scrolls endlessly in both directions.

- **Input**: wheel adds `deltaY·0.006` to idxT; ArrowDown/Up ±1; hovering (pointermove over) an item nudges idxT by `((itemCentreY − H/2) / (H·0.046))·0.08` per move event (drifts the hovered item toward the hairline).
- **Selecting** (click an item, or Enter on the highlighted one): remove `body.index`, restore the previous mode; if that was the case view, instantly remove `case` and `out` and set mode home; then goP(selected) on the reel. Escape or the close button just closes (returns to the previous mode).

## 13. Render loop summary (every requestAnimationFrame)

1. `dt = min(.05, Δt)`.
2. Home idle settle (not dragging, >380ms since input, ref set) → settle.
3. Ease `pos` toward `tgt` with factor `1 − e^(−5.5·dt)`.
4. Detect active project change → title roll + Next label roll.
5. Ease the (always-zero) flat factor with `1 − e^(−6.5·dt)`.
6. Ease shader background toward the theme colour by `min(1, dt·5)`.
7. Compute hh = 0.245H, cy = 0.455H, tile width = 2·hh·16/9 (times backing ratio).
8. Upload the current video frame if `readyState >= 2`.
9. Set uniforms (theta .95, k 1, video-on flag, background) and draw the triangle.
10. If the index is open, run the index positioning step.

On load: size the canvas, setRoll(0, +1), start the loop. (Optional debugging handle on `window.__nr` exposing goP, openCase, closeCase, openIndex, closeIndex, caseStep, a `more()` that opens the card, and getters for cur and mode.)

# HERO PROMPT — "Dune Play" by Grovekit (interactive pixel-art plant playground)

Build a single self-contained `index.html` (inline CSS + inline vanilla JS, no frameworks, no build step) that recreates the page described below **exactly**. The page is a full-viewport, non-scrolling toy: three pixel-art desert plants (a coconut palm, a barrel cactus with a pink flower, and a jacaranda tree) stand on small sand mounds over a flat warm-sand background. You can click or brush them to shake their leaves and petals loose, turn on weather so the wind bends them and strips foliage off, watch leaves fall and pile up as litter, have everything "grow back", flip to an x-ray "skeleton" view, toggle sound, switch to a single-plant carousel and toggle dark mode.

Everything visual on the plants is made of square "cells" (fat pixels) drawn on one full-screen `<canvas>`. All UI chrome is HTML floating above the canvas.

Document title: **`Dune Play · Grovekit`** (with a middle dot). `lang="en"`, UTF-8, `width=device-width,initial-scale=1` viewport.

## 4. The canvas

- `<canvas id="scene">` fixed, `inset:0`, 100%×100%, `image-rendering: pixelated`, `touch-action:none`. It sits below all UI.
- Backing size = `round(innerWidth·DPR) × round(innerHeight·DPR)` where **DPR = min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2)**.
- All drawing is axis-aligned filled squares of side **C** device pixels (one "cell"). No antialiasing, no images drawn to the main canvas — every sprite pixel is its own `fillRect`.

---

## 5. Sprite-to-grid pipeline (run once per plant at load)

Each plant definition:

| key | target rows | flex (bendiness) | default foliage kind | wood rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| palm | **96** | **1.15** | `frond` | hue 12–48° (inclusive), saturation > .30, value < .82 |
| cactus | **58** | **0.12** | `flesh` | special (below) |
| jac | **86** | **0.60** | `petal` | hue 8–50° (inclusive), saturation > .22, value < .72 |

Steps:
1. **Decode** the PNG, draw it to an offscreen canvas at native size, read pixels.
2. **Crop to alpha bounding box**: the bbox of all pixels with alpha **> 60**.
3. **Downsample**: target rows = per plant (above); cols = `round(rows · bboxWidth / bboxHeight)`. Draw the cropped region into a `cols × rows` canvas with `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` and `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'` and read it back.
4. **Alpha threshold**: skip any cell with alpha **< 120** (everything kept is drawn fully opaque).
5. **Posterise**: each R, G, B channel → `round(c/8)·8` (multiples of 8), clamped to ≤ 255 when building the colour string `rgb(r,g,b)`.
6. **Classify** using HSV of the posterised colour (h in degrees 0–360, s = (max−min)/max, v = max, all from 0–1 channels; standard hue formula, negative hue + 360):
   - **Palm / Jacaranda**: `wood = rule(h,s,v)` from the table — brown trunks/branches are wood; everything else is foliage of the plant's default kind (`frond` for palm, `petal` for jacaranda — the whole jacaranda canopy behaves like petals).
   - **Cactus** (evaluated in this order):
     - `green` = 60 < h < 170.
     - If green **and v < .36** → **wood** (the dark rib lines) with a **bare colour `#b2875a`** (see §9).
     - else if **flower** → kind `petal`. Flower = (h > 300 or h < 18) with s > .35 (pink petals), **or** (38 ≤ h ≤ 62 with s > .6 and the cell is in the top 30 % of rows, y < rows·0.3) (the yellow flower centre).
     - else if **spine** = s < .38 and v > .55 (pale, low-saturation light pixels) → kind `spine`.
     - else → kind `flesh` (the green body).
7. **Looseness**: build an occupancy grid of kept cells. For each cell count occupied cells `n` in its **7×7 neighbourhood** (offsets −3…+3 both axes, the cell itself included, out-of-bounds ignored). `loose = clamp((1 − n/49)·1.8 + random·0.25, 0, 1)`. Edge/outer cells are loose (≈1), interior cells are tight (≈0).
8. **Seed**: each cell gets `seed = random · 6.28`.

Each cell record stores: home column `hx`, home row `hy`, colour, `wood` flag, optional `bare` colour, `kind` (`frond` | `petal` | `flesh` | `spine`), `loose`, `seed`, and runtime state. Each plant record also stores `cols`, a spring position `k = 0` and velocity `kv = 0`.

## 6. World layout (on load and on every window resize / view change)

- **Cell size**: `C = max(2, round(innerHeight · DPR · 0.0054))` device pixels in the three-plant view; factor **0.0068** in single view (plants appear ~26 % larger).
- Grid width `cols = ceil(canvasWidth / C) + 2`.
- **Ground row** `GY = round(canvasHeight · 0.68 / C)` — the ground line is at 68 % of the viewport height.
- Allocate a **litter height map** `hm` (one int per column, all 0) and a **floor mask** `floor` (one flag per column, all 0).
- Plant centre fractions of width: palm **0.20**, cactus **0.48**, jacaranda **0.77**. In single view all are at **0.50** and only the selected plant is visible (`one` index; default **1 = cactus**).
- Per plant: centre column `cx = round(canvasWidth · fx / C)`; origin `ox = cx − round(cols/2)`; `oy = GY − rows` (the sprite's bottom row sits on row GY−1).
- **Sand mound** per plant: width `w = round(max(plantCols · 1.05, 40))` cells, starting at column `cx − round(w/2)`. For each x = 0…w−1 with `t = x/(w−1)`, mound height `hgt = round( sin(t·π)^0.6 · 3 )` (0–3 cells, a flat-topped dome). Fill cells from row `GY+1` up to row `GY+1−hgt` (y = 0…hgt, row = GY − y + 1). Each cell's tone = `tones[(x·7 + y·3) mod 4]` with tones `['#e4cfa6', '#d9c094', '#cdb282', '#efdcb8']` — a dithered sandy texture. The mound is drawn before the plant every frame (the plant base overlaps its top).
- **Litter floor**: only under visible plants, columns `cx − (W>>1)` to `cx + (W>>1)` (exclusive) where `W = round(max(plantCols·1.05, 40) · 1.25)` — i.e. **1.25× the mound width**. Falling foliage can only land where `floor` is set; elsewhere it falls through and off the bottom of the screen.
- Update the single-view dots (active = selected index).
- **Reset**: every cell of every plant goes back to attached (state 0); body class `bare` is removed.

## 7. Interaction: shaking

### Hit test
Convert the pointer to grid coords: `gx = clientX · DPR / C`, `gy = clientY · DPR / C`. For each visible plant, quick-reject unless `ox−3 ≤ gx ≤ ox+cols+3` and `oy−3 ≤ gy ≤ GY+2`. Then the plant is hit if **any attached cell** (state 0, wood or foliage) has `|ox + hx + sx − gx| < 3` and `|oy + hy − gy| < 3` (sx = that cell's current sway offset). First hit plant wins.

### Hover cursor
On pointermove (when not dragging) set the canvas cursor to `pointer` over a plant, otherwise `default`.

### Click (pointerdown)
If a plant is hit: capture the pointer, start a drag record `{plant, lastX = clientX}`, and **shake(plant, dir = random ±1, power = 1)**.

### Drag shake
While dragging, on pointermove compute `dx = clientX − lastX`; whenever `|dx| > 28` px, **shake(plant, sign(dx), power = 0.7)** and set `lastX = clientX`. (So brushing back and forth keeps shaking the same plant.) pointerup / pointercancel end the drag.

### shake(plant, dir, power)
1. `leaves` = all foliage (non-wood) cells currently attached.
2. Spring impulse: `kv += dir · (5 + 4·power)`.
3. Count to detach: `n = max( min(leaves, 30), min( round(leaves · 0.13 · power), 170 ) )` — at least 30 (or all if fewer), ~13 % of what's left, capped at 170.
4. Sort leaves descending by `loose + random·0.9` (looser, outer leaves preferred, with randomness) and detach the first `n` with initial velocity:
   - `vx = dir·(6 + random·16) + windDir·windSpeed·12`
   - `vy = −(6 + random·16)` (upward toss; units = cells/second, +y is down)
5. Increment the Shaken counter by 1 (always, even if nothing was left to drop) and re-render it as en-US formatted.

### Spring
Each plant has a 1-D damped spring `k` (position) / `kv` (velocity), integrated every frame: `kv += (−k·42 − kv·3.4)·dt; k += kv·dt` (stiffness **42**, damping **3.4**, semi-implicit Euler). Its contribution is added to the sway (§8), so a shake makes the whole plant whip side to side and settle over ~1–2 s.

---

## 8. Wind model and per-frame simulation

### Time
`t` = seconds since page start; `dt = min(0.05, frame delta seconds)`.

### Gust noise
`gustN(t) = ( sin(1.31t) + sin(2.17t + 1.3) + 0.8·sin(0.63t + 2.1) + 2.8 ) / 5.6` → a smooth 0…~1 signal.

### Wind value
`g = gustN(t)`; `w = dir · ( speed·0.75 + speed·g·gust·0.9 + gust·g·0.12 )`, `aw = |w|`. `dir` is −1 (Left) or +1 (Right). Note that even at speed 0 the gust term gives a faint idle breath.

### Automatic shedding rate
`rate = speed > 0.15 ? speed^2.4 · 0.045 · (0.35 + gustN(1.7t) · gust · 1.7) : 0`.

### Per plant, per frame
1. Draw its sand mound cells.
2. Integrate the spring (§7).
3. **Sway**: `sway = ( w·0.55 + sin(0.9t + cx)·0.05 + (aw > 0.05 ? sin(3.1t + cx)·aw·0.12 : 0) ) · flex + k·0.55·max(0.25, flex)` (cx = plant centre column, de-syncing plants).
4. For each cell with `hg = 1 − hy/rows` (0 at base, 1 at top):

**Attached (state 0)**
- Foliage only: counts toward `total` and `attached`. Auto-detach with probability per frame `rate · dt · (spine ? 0.25 : 1) · (0.2 + loose·1.6) · (0.4 + hg)`, initial velocity `vx = w·30 + (random−0.5)·8`, `vy = −random·6`. If detached, skip drawing as attached.
- **Bend offset** (all attached cells): `ox = sway · hg^1.7 · rows · 0.14`, `oy = 0` — the base is anchored, the top bends most.
- **Streaming tails** (foliage only): `arm = loose^1.6 · (flex > 0.3 ? 1 : 0.35)` (stiff plant — cactus — gets 0.35×); `g = 0.65 + 0.35·sin(2.6t − hx·0.18 + seed·0.3)` (a travelling ripple across the canopy); then `ox += w·aw·arm·rows·0.42·g + sin(7t + seed)·arm·aw·1.4` (pull downwind plus fast flutter) and `oy = −arm·aw²·3·g` (outer leaves lift slightly in strong wind).
- Store `sx = round(ox)`, `sy = round(oy)` (whole cells, keeping it crunchy pixel art). Draw at cell `(ox_plant + hx + sx, oy_plant + hy + sy)`.
- Colour: the cell colour, except cactus rib wood cells which are mixed toward their bare colour (§9).

**Not attached** — foliage counts toward `total` only.

**Flying (state 1)** — lifetime factor `lt` by kind: **petal 1.5, frond 1.25, flesh 0.95, spine 0.6** (set at detach; each flying cell also gets a random phase `ph ∈ [0, 6.28)`).
- Accelerations: `ax = w·48·lt + sin(4.2t + ph)·16·lt` (wind push + side-to-side flutter); `ay = (spine ? 50 : 18) / lt` (gravity: spines drop fast, petals float).
- Drag-toward-target integration: `vx += (ax − vx·1.6)·dt`; `vy += (ay − vy·1.1)·dt`.
- Position: `x += vx·dt + sin(6t + ph)·0.05·lt`; `y += vy·dt`.
- **Leaving the screen**: if `x < −4` or `x > cols + 4` or `y > canvasHeight/C + 4` → state 3 (gone, not drawn).
- **Landing**: with `c = round(x)`, if `c` is in range, `floor[c]` is set, `y ≥ GY − hm[c]` and `vy > 0` → state 2, snap `y = GY − hm[c]`, `x = c`, then `hm[c] = min(5, hm[c] + 1)`. Litter piles up on the ground row and stacks at most **5** cells high per column.

**Landed (state 2)** — if `aw > 0.55` (storm-strength), each frame with probability `(aw − 0.5)·dt·1.4` the litter is **re-lifted**: detach again with `vx = w·40`, `vy = −8 − random·10` (and its column's `hm` decrements by 1).

**Returning (state 4)** — see §9.

States 1, 2, 4 are drawn at `(round(x), round(y))` in the cell's own colour.

General detach rules: wood never detaches; a cell already flying is ignored; detaching an attached cell starts it at its current displayed position (home + sx, sy); detaching a landed cell decrements `hm` at its column; gone (3) and returning (4) cells cannot be detached. Every detach increments a per-frame counter used for sound.

5. **Skeleton overlay** (when Skeleton is on): after all the plant's cells, draw every attached wood cell again on top in `#c8382a` (light) / `#ff6a4d` (dark) at `(ox + hx + sx, oy + hy)` (horizontal sway applied, no vertical tail offset). Result: palm trunk and frond ribs, jacaranda trunk/branches and cactus rib lines show as a red x-ray rig while foliage still moves around them.
6. Plant bareness `bareK = total ? 1 − attached/total : 0`; the scene is "bare" if any visible plant has `attached < total`.

After all plants: unless a grow-back is in progress, toggle `body.bare` to the bare flag (shows/hides Grow back). Fire one rustle burst for the frame's detach count (§11). Update wind sound gain. Draw the windsock with the current `t` and `w`. Request the next frame.

## 9. Bare colour mixing & Grow back

### Cactus ribs
Cactus rib cells (wood with bare colour `#b2875a`) are drawn as `mix(original, #b2875a, bareK)` — linear RGB interpolation, rounded. As the cactus loses its green flesh/spines/flower, the dark rib lines warm up into a tan woody skeleton; when fully stripped they are pure `#b2875a`. (Uses the previous frame's bareK.)

### Grow back (button click)
1. Set a `growing` flag (suppresses toggling `body.bare` for **1800 ms**), clear `hm` to all zeros.
2. For every visible foliage cell not attached: if it is gone (state 3) or has never had a position, respawn it at `x = homeX + (random − 0.5)·30`, `y = GY + 6` (just below ground, spread around the plant). Set state 4, remember start `fx, fy`.
3. **Staggered, bottom-first** start time: with `r = hy/rows`, `t0 = now + (r > 0 ? (1 − r)·0.25 : 0) + (1 − r)·0.45 + random·0.35` seconds — cells near the base start first, the crown last (up to ~1.05 s later). Duration `du = 0.55 + random·0.35` s.
4. Remove `body.bare` immediately (button fades out).
5. Each frame for state 4: `e = clamp((now − t0)/du, 0, 1)`, `ez = 1 − (1 − e)^3` (**ease-out cubic**); `x = fx + (homeX − fx)·ez`, `y = fy + (homeY − fy)·ez − sin(e·π)·8` — every pixel flies home along an **8-cell upward arc**. Home = `(ox + hx, oy + hy)` (no sway). Before its start time a cell waits at its start position. When `e ≥ 1` it becomes attached (state 0) with `sx = 0`.

### Grow back visibility rules
- Visible (`body.bare`) whenever any visible plant has any detached foliage (flying, landed, gone or returning), recomputed every frame — except during the 1.8 s grow window, where it stays hidden.
- Removed on layout changes (resize, view switch, carousel step), which also reattach everything.
- In single view it sits right of the carousel nav (§3.9).

## 10. Windsock (pixel art, in the control bar)

Drawn every frame on the 28×30 canvas (displayed at 2×, pixelated). Clear it, then:
- **Pole**: colour `#6b6258` (light) / `#9a8f80` (dark). A 2-px-wide rectangle at x = 13, y = 1, height 29; plus a 4×2 base foot at x = 12, y = 28.
- **Sock**: `a = min(1, |w|)`, `d = sign(w)` (or +1 if 0), droop angle `ang = (1 − a)·1.25` rad (calm: hangs ~72° down beside the pole; gale: straight out horizontally). Five segments `i = 0…4`:
  - distance from pole `r = 2 + 2.4·i`
  - flap `fl = sin(10t − 1.2i) · a · 0.9` (a wave travelling down the sock, stronger in stronger wind)
  - `dx = cos(ang)·r`, `y = 3 + sin(ang)·r + fl`
  - segment height `h = max(2, 4 − floor(i/2))` → 4, 4, 3, 3, 2 (tapering)
  - colour: even i `#e8573b`, odd i `#f4efe6` (orange/white stripes)
  - x: if d > 0, `15 + dx`; else `9 − dx` (mirrored to the left side of the pole)
  - fill a rect `3 × h` at `(round(x), round(y − h/2 + 1))`.

## 11. Sound (Web Audio, created lazily on first Sound ON)

- Turning Sound ON the first time creates an `AudioContext` (with `webkitAudioContext` fallback); later ON clicks just `resume()` it.
- **Noise buffer**: mono, 2 s at the context sample rate, brown-ish noise: `l = (l + 0.02·white)/1.02`, sample = `l · 3.5`, where white ∈ [−1, 1).
- **Wind bed**: looping buffer source → **bandpass 420 Hz, Q 0.6** → gain (starts 0) → destination, started immediately. Every frame the gain is smoothed with `setTargetAtTime(target, now, 0.25)` where target = Sound on ? `min(0.5, aw·0.45 + 0.01)` : 0 (so turning Sound off fades it out but keeps the graph alive).
- **Rustle bursts**: once per frame when ≥ 1 cell detached that frame (and Sound is on): a new one-shot source on the same noise buffer → **highpass 1800 Hz** → gain envelope → destination. Peak `a = min(0.22, 0.02 + n/180)` (n = cells detached this frame); gain 0 at now, linear ramp to `a` in 20 ms, exponential ramp to 0.0005 by +0.35 s; start at a random offset 0–1 s into the buffer; stop at +0.4 s.

## 12. Controls state & behaviour

Initial state: weather off, mode `breezy`, direction +1 (Right), wind speed **0**, gust **0.45**, skeleton off, sound off, light theme, three-plant view, single index 1.

- **Weather switch**: toggles weather. Turning it **ON** applies the current mode's preset with animated sliders. Turning it **OFF** animates speed back to **0** and gust to **0.45**. The Breezy/Storm segment is dimmed (.55) while weather is off.
- **Presets** (speed, gust): **Breezy = 0.40 / 0.45** (labels "Breeze" / "Gusty"), **Storm = 0.95 / 0.95** (labels "Gale" / "Wild gusts").
- **Breezy/Storm buttons**: select the mode **and** force weather ON, then apply the preset (animated .7s).
- **Direction Left/Right**: sets dir −1/+1 and moves the `.on` highlight. Affects wind sign, leaf flight, toss velocity, sway direction and windsock side.
- **Sliders**: manual edit; touching one turns weather OFF (no preset reset).
- **Skeleton switch**: toggles the red wood overlay.
- **Sound switch**: toggles audio (initialises on first enable — requires that user gesture).

# Hale Moor: build brief for the full landing page

Build **one self-contained `index.html`**: a soft, pastel, scroll-driven landing page for a fictional venture fund called **Hale Moor**. Two real-time WebGL objects carry it:

- a luminous **iridescent particle sphere** that rises in the hero and then travels through the page as you scroll;
- a **faceted geodesic glass crystal** that takes over in the focus-area section.

Everything else is HTML/CSS laid over a fixed full-screen canvas. There are no images and no videos: all imagery is drawn live in WebGL or as inline SVG.

The page has seven parts, top to bottom:

1. Hero
2. Manifesto
3. Track record (portfolio cards)
4. Focus area (the crystal)
5. Who we are (names wheel)
6. Footer
7. A fixed nav and a fixed pager that sit over all of them

Follow every value below exactly. All desktop measurements are in a **1440 × 900 design frame**.

## 6. The WebGL scene (Three.js 0.173)

**Renderer:**
- `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, alpha:true, antialias:true, premultipliedAlpha:true, powerPreference:'high-performance' })`.
- `setClearColor(0x000000, 0)`.
- Pixel ratio `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`.
- If WebGL fails, still run the text entrance.

**Camera:** `PerspectiveCamera(35°, aspect, 0.1, 100)` at (0, 0, 10). The visible height at z = 0 is `VIS_H = 2·10·tan(17.5°)`.

**Placing an object from screen pixels.** Given a screen centre (cx, cy) and a screen radius r in CSS px:
- `k = VIS_H / innerHeight`
- `Rs = r·k`
- world radius `R = Rs·10 / sqrt(100 + Rs²)` (this undoes the perspective growth of the silhouette)
- `x = (cx − vw/2)·k`
- `y = −(cy − vh/2)·k`

**Shared material set-up.** Every material is a `ShaderMaterial` with:
- `transparent:true`, `depthWrite:false`, `depthTest:false`;
- `CustomBlending`, `AddEquation`, `blendSrc = OneFactor`, `blendDst = OneMinusSrcAlphaFactor`, and the same factors for alpha;
- shaders that output **premultiplied** colour.

This gives soft, additive-looking light that stays correct on a transparent canvas.

**Noise:** standard 3D simplex noise (Ashima Arts / Stefan Gustavson, MIT), `float snoise(vec3)`.

**Shared uniforms:**
- `uTime`
- `uReveal` (0→1)
- `uPx` (object size → device pixels)
- `uMouse` (vec2, world)
- `uMouseStr` (0–1)
- `uMouseRad` (0.3·R)
- `uFade` (scroll fade of the main sphere)

**Mouse push** (in the vertex shader of both particle layers):
- `wp = modelMatrix·p`; `dlt = wp.xy − uMouse`; `dd = |dlt|`.
- `push = uMouseStr · exp(−dd²/uMouseRad²)`.
- `dir = dlt/dd`; `wp.xy += (dir·0.6 + perp(dir)·0.4) · push · uMouseRad · 0.32`.
- `wp.z += push · uMouseRad · 0.25`.

The perpendicular term makes the cursor *stir* the particles rather than punch a hole in them.

### 6a. Main sphere: three layers inside `orb → spin`

Draw order is cloud (1), glass (2), spray (3).

**1. Inner cloud.** 120,000 points (65,000 on phones), placed at a random direction × `r = 0.5 + 0.47·rand^0.45`, with `aRand` vec4.

- **Vertex shader:**
  - Drift: `p += (snoise(q), snoise(q+17.1), snoise(q+43.7))·0.04`, where `q = p·1.6 + (0,0,t·0.12)`.
  - Reveal: `rv = smoothstep(aRand.x·0.45, aRand.x·0.45 + 0.55, uReveal)`, then `p *= mix(0.55, 1, rv)`.
- **Colour** (from the original position o):
  - `n = snoise(o·1.25 + 3)`, `n2 = snoise(o·2.6 − 5 + t·0.03)`.
  - Start with `mix(violet (0.50,0.33,0.84), lilac (0.74,0.55,0.95), smoothstep(−0.45, 0.6, n2))`.
  - Blend in teal (0.42,0.86,0.84) by `smoothstep(0.2, 0.75, −o.x·0.85 − o.y·0.25 + n·0.45)·0.85`, so teal sits on the lower left.
  - Blend in pink (0.98,0.48,0.80) by `smoothstep(0.2, 0.8, o.x·0.85 + n·0.5)·0.8`, so pink sits on the right.
  - 8% of points are sparkles (`aRand.y > 0.92`), mixed 92% toward white.
- **Clusters:** `cluster = smoothstep(−0.4, 0.55, snoise(o·2.3 + t·0.035))`.
- **Alpha:** `vAlpha = (0.35 + 0.65·cluster)·rv·(0.7 + 0.3·aRand.z)`.
- **Point size:** `0.0072·(0.55 + 0.9·aRand.w)·(1 + spark·1.1)·(0.75 + 0.45·cluster)·uPx / −mv.z`.
- **Fragment shader:**
  - Disc `a = smoothstep(0.5, 0.08, |coord − .5|)`.
  - Sparkles twinkle at `0.65 + 0.35·sin(t·4 + fragX·0.37 + fragY·0.21)`.
  - Output `(col·α, α·mix(0.92, 0.6, spark))`, where `α = a·vAlpha·tw·uFade`.

**2. Rim spray.** 40,000 points (16,000 on phones).
- **Directions:** 78% hug the silhouette ring, `normalize(cos θ, sin θ, ±0.32·rand)`; the rest are fully random.
- **Vertex shader:**
  - `life = fract(t·(0.045 + 0.07·aRand.x) + aRand.y)`.
  - Tufts: `tuft = (0.5 + 0.5·snoise(dir·3.2 + (0, t·0.02, 0)))^1.6`.
  - Reach: `reach = 0.015 + 0.42·aRand.z^1.7·(0.25 + 1.1·tuft)`.
  - Radius `r = 1 + reach·(0.35 + 0.65·life)`, plus a small noise drift of `0.03·(0.4 + life)`.
  - Reveal `rv = smoothstep(0.35 + aRand.w·0.4, 1, uReveal)`.
  - Silhouette weight `sil = 1 − |worldNormal.z|`.
  - `alpha = sin(life·π)·(0.45 + 0.75·tuft)·rv·(0.7 + 0.5·aRand.w)·(0.3 + 0.7·sil)`.
  - Colour: warm white, tinted 25% × aRand.x toward mint on the left and pink on the right.
  - Point size `0.0075·(0.45 + 1.1·aRand.x²)`.
- **Fragment shader:** `core = smoothstep(0.24, 0, d)`, `halo = smoothstep(0.5, 0, d)·0.55`, output alpha × 0.85.

**3. Glass shell.** `SphereGeometry(1, 160, 96)`, scaled `mix(0.8, 1, uReveal)`.
- `f = 1 − dot(N, V)`, `fr = f^2.6`.
- Thin-film colour: `irid = 0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·(f·1.15 + atan(y,x)·0.16 + t·0.025 + (0, .33, .67)))`, then mixed 50% with white.
- Edge line `edge = smoothstep(0.78, 0.96, f)·(1 − smoothstep(0.992, 1, f))`.
- `col = mix((0.98, 0.95, 1), irid, smoothstep(0.35, 0.95, f))`, then 60% toward white on the edge.
- `alpha = (0.025 + fr·0.42 + edge·0.6)·uReveal·uFade`.

**Size uniform.** `uPx = vh·dpr / VIS_H · 10 · sqrt(R·R_hero)`. The dots grow only with √scale, so the sphere stays fine-grained when it gets big.

**Motion:**
- `spin.rotation.y = t·0.045 + scrollY·0.0004`.
- `orb` rotation eases toward the mouse: `ry = ndcX·0.28`, `rx = −ndcY·0.16`, with `L = 1 − 0.0025^dt` and factor ×0.6.
- `orb.x` adds `ry·R·0.12`, eased with factor ×0.5.
- `uMouseStr` eases to 1 while the pointer has moved within the last 900 ms, and back to 0 otherwise.
- `uMouse` follows the pointer ray hitting the z = 0 plane, with factor ×1.4.
- **Hero rise:** `orb.y = layout.y − (1 − uReveal)·R·0.28`.

### 6b. The crystal (focus section): group `crystal → crystalSpin`

**Geometry:** `IcosahedronGeometry(1, 1)`, which gives 80 flat triangular panels and is non-indexed. Add a barycentric attribute `aBary`, with each vertex getting (1,0,0), (0,1,0) or (0,0,1) by index mod 3.

**Meshes:** draw it twice with the shared material settings, first `BackSide` (alpha × 0.5) and then `FrontSide`.

**Fragment shader:**
- Flat normal `N = normalize(cross(dFdx(viewPos), dFdy(viewPos)))`.
- `fres = (1 − |N·V|)^2.2`.
- `minB = min(bary)`.
- **Rib** `edge = 1 − smoothstep(0, 0.03, minB)`.
- **Bevel** `bevel = 1 − smoothstep(0.03, 0.12, minB)`, and `fringe = bevel·(1 − edge)`.
- **Dispersion:** `h = N·norm(0.35, 0.65, 0.6)·1.3 + minB·4 + objY·0.35 + t·0.04`, `rainbow = 0.55 + 0.45·cos(2π(h + (0, .33, .67)))`.
- **Caustics:** `caustic = (1 − |snoise(obj·2.6 + (0, t·0.18, t·0.07))|)^14`.
- **Glint:** `spec = max(N·H, 0)^48`, with light direction `norm(−0.45, 0.7, 0.55)`.
- **Colour:**
  - `col = (0.92, 0.9, 1)·(0.22 + 0.4·fres)`
  - `+ rainbow·(0.14·fres + 0.5·fringe + 0.12·caustic)`
  - `+ (1, 0.97, 1)·(edge + caustic·0.25 + spec)`
- **Alpha:** `(0.06 + fres·0.26 + edge·0.9 + fringe·0.26 + caustic·0.14 + spec·0.8)·(1 + 0.35·uHover)`, clamped, then × `mix(1, 0.5, back)` × `uFade2`.

The result is clear glass with white ribs and a thin prism fringe beside each rib.

**Core glow:** a camera-facing 2.6 × 2.6 quad drawn before the shell. Its alpha is `(e^(−5d²)·0.95 + e^(−1.6d²)·0.45)·smoothstep(1, 0.55, d)·(0.85 + 0.1·sin(t·0.8) + 0.2·uHover)·uFade2`, with colour (1, 0.94, 0.99). The `smoothstep` is required so the quad never shows its square edge.

**Motion:**
- `crystalSpin.rotation = (0.32 + t·0.025, t·0.11 + scrollY·0.0007, 0)`.
- `crystal.rotation = orb.rotation·1.4` (it follows the mouse).
- `crystal.x` adds `mouseOffset·0.6`.
- `uHover` eases to 1 while the cursor is inside the crystal's screen circle (`1 − 0.02^dt`).

## 8. Entrance (one Web Animations timeline, run once)

- `<html class="pre">` hides the wordmark, menu and headline (`opacity:0`).
- **Failsafe:** an inline script in `<head>` waits 2600 ms. If `.pre` is still there, it sets `window.__heroShown = true` and removes `.pre`.
- Once the module runs:
  - **Sphere reveal proxy:** a detached `<i>` animates opacity 0→1 over 2200 ms, easing `cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.24,1)`, `fill:both`. Every frame, `uReveal` = `proxy.effect.getComputedTiming().progress`, so the sphere shares the same timeline. It always runs.
  - If `__heroShown` is already set, stop here so the copy isn't hidden again. Otherwise animate, all with `fill:'backwards'` and easing `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`:
    - wordmark: opacity 0→1, translateY(−8px)→0, 700 ms, delay 200;
    - menu: the same, delay 280;
    - headline: opacity 0→1, `translate: 0 22px`→0, `blur(6px)`→0, 1100 ms, delay 350. Use the individual `translate` property so the CSS `transform` offset survives.
  - Then remove `.pre`.
- **Section reveals:** an `IntersectionObserver` (threshold 0.15, rootMargin `0px 0px -6% 0px`) adds `.in` to each `.reveal`, then unobserves it.
  - `.reveal`: `opacity 0; translate 0 28w`, with a 1 s transition on both properties using `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`.
  - Each item has `transition-delay = (index mod 4)·70 ms`.

---

## 9. Loop, resize and reduced motion

- `renderer.setAnimationLoop`. Skip frames while `document.hidden`. `dt = min(clock.getDelta(), 0.05)`.
- **On resize:** update the size and pixel ratio, set the camera aspect, re-measure the sections and rebuild the keyframes.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:**
  - No animation loop, no mouse listeners and no entrance animations. Remove `.pre` at once.
  - `uReveal = 1`. All `.reveal` elements get `.in`, with no transitions.
  - The sphere and crystal jump straight to their keyframe for the current `scrollY`; `render(0)` runs on every scroll and resize.
  - Card, button and pager transitions are off.
- **Phone layout:** at ≤ 820px, every section uses the phone values given above and there is no horizontal scroll.

---

## 10. Accessibility and semantics

- `<main>` wraps the hero and the sections. The headline is an `h1`; the closing line is an `h2`.
- The stage and canvas are `aria-hidden`.
- The wheel has `aria-label="Team"`. The pager is a `nav` with `aria-label="Focus areas"`, and its buttons are labelled.
- Every company, person and claim is fictional.

# NOWHERE® Lookbook — full recreation brief

Build a single-file, full-viewport fashion lookbook called **NOWHERE®**. Nine full-body models, each shot from a high overhead camera on a light grey studio floor, stand in a 3D carousel ring that can be dragged, scrolled sideways, played automatically or switched to a 3×3 grid. Clicking the front model zooms it into a "look view" with numbered dots on each garment, and a paper receipt prints down from the top-right listing the three pieces with sizes, a 10% whole-fit discount and an add-to-bag flow. Everything is plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file, with no libraries. The page is exactly one screen tall (100svh, never scrolls). Everything below must be reproduced exactly.

## 5. The ring (core math)

Measure on every stage resize (ResizeObserver):
- W, H = stage width and height. "mobile" means innerWidth < 810.
- bottomPad = 168 on mobile, 120 otherwise. topPad = 136.
- modelH = max(200, round((H − bottomPad − 18 − topPad) / 1.12)). Set it as `--model-h` on the stage.
- frontScale = 1.12 on mobile, 1.165 otherwise.
- dragPx (pixels per look) = max(90 on mobile or 120, W × 0.3).
- body width = modelH × 4/7.

Ring constants: radius factor 0.44 (0.84 on mobile), perspective factor 0.8 (1.1 on mobile), horizon 0.06, front step 0.03, lift 40 px, angular step = 2π/9.

For every look i, given the continuous ring position `pos`:
- a = (i − pos) × step, wrapped into (−π, π].
- R = W × radius factor, P = W × perspective factor.
- k = P / (P + R × (1 − cos a)) (the perspective factor).
- dist = |a| / step, near = clamp(1 − dist, 0, 1).
- scale = k × (1 + (frontScale − 1) × near).
- x = W/2 + R × sin(a) × k.
- yNear = H − bottomPad − 40, yFar = topPad + (H − topPad) × 0.06 − 40.
- y = yFar + (yNear − yFar) × k + (desktop only: H × 0.03 × near).
- blur = 1.8 × dist when dist ≤ 1, otherwise min(1.8 + (dist − 1) × 2, 6.5) px.
- transform = translate3d(x, y − H, 0) translateX(−50%) scale(scale). Opacity is 1, except 0 when the scaled body is fully outside the stage (more than 4 px past either edge), which also sets visibility hidden. pointer-events are off below opacity 0.5. z-index = round(scale × 1000). Only write opacity and filter when they change.

**Spring**: pos follows goal with a critically damped spring: stiffness 95, damping 2√95, integrated in 3 sub-steps per frame with dt clamped to 0.034 s. It settles when both |pos − goal| and |velocity| are ≤ 0.0005. Run requestAnimationFrame only while it moves, while dragging, or when a relayout is pending. Add an "is-moving" class meanwhile, which sets will-change on the models. Pause when the stage leaves the viewport (IntersectionObserver).

**Intro**: pos starts at −1.15 with the goal at 0, so on load the ring visibly spins about one look into place (instant under reduced motion).

**Active look**: active = round(goal) mod 9. Changing it updates the counter, name, live region, drawer highlight, grid captions, receipt and dock pieces; replays the name swap, the piece rise and a **light sweep**; closes the look view if open; and restarts the autoplay timer. The sweep is a 42%-wide skewed (−12°) white gradient band (transparent → .28 at 42% → .6 at 50% → .28 at 58% → transparent, 100°) in a soft-light blended overlay. It runs 1.5 s with cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) from translateX(−130%) to 330%, fading in by 18% and out by the end.

**Autoplay**: on by default, off under reduced motion. Every 5 s it advances one look, unless the tab is hidden, the stage is off-screen, the user is dragging or hovering the receipt with a mouse, or the look view, grid or drawer is open (then it just reschedules). The toggle button flips it. Any drag, wheel, arrow key, ring click, grid switch, drawer opening, look view opening or receipt interaction turns autoplay off.

**Dragging** (pointer events on the stage; ignored in grid or look view, and for non-primary mouse buttons):
- On pointerdown, record the start x/y, the start goal, the pointer id and a velocity trail.
- On move: if the vertical movement exceeds 10 px and beats the horizontal, give up (let the page scroll). If the horizontal movement exceeds 8 px and is more than 1.2× the vertical, start dragging: capture the pointer, add "is-dragging" (cursor grabbing) and stop autoplay.
- While dragging: goal = startGoal − dx / dragPx, active = round(goal), and keep the last 6 samples.
- On release: velocity v = (last x − first x) / (last t − first t) in px/ms; base = round(startGoal). On mobile, move ±1 if |dx| > 30 or |v| > 0.3, otherwise snap back. On desktop, target = round(goal − v × 160 / dragPx); if that equals base and |v| > 0.3, push one look in the flick direction; clamp to base ± 2.
- Ignore the click that fires within 60 ms after a drag ends.

**Clicking a model**: in the ring, if it is the front model (shortest signed distance 0) open the look view, otherwise rotate to it the short way. In the grid, jump the ring to it instantly and open the look view.

**Wheel**: only horizontal-dominant wheels (deltaX bigger than deltaY), not in grid or look view. Prevent the default, accumulate deltaX, and step one look when the total passes 45, then lock for 520 ms.

**Keys** (stage focused): ←/→ step; in the grid ↑/↓ jump ±3; Enter opens the look view. Escape anywhere closes the look view, or else the drawer.

## 0. Concept in one paragraph

A minimal, warm-beige kitchenware landing page for a brand called **olla**. At the top: a fixed white rounded navigation bar with a "Shop" mega-menu that wipes open downward into a strip of five line-icons. ## 8. The grill technique (green-screen clip → keyed frame cache → scroll scrub)

The grill is **not** a playing video. It is a set of pre-keyed frames scrubbed by scroll.

### 8.1 Two canvases

- Both canvases have class `.grill`: `position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; z-index: 2; pointer-events: none; will-change: transform`.
- `#gS` lives inside `#sky`; `#gK` lives inside `#kitchen`. Both always show the same frame at the same document-space position, size and rotation (§12 explains why).

### 8.2 Frame caching

- Constants: **NF = 48** frames, **FS = 560** px square cache canvases.
- Create an offscreen `<video>`: `crossOrigin = "anonymous"`, `muted = true`, `playsInline = true`, `preload = "auto"`, `src = GRILL_CLIP`. Wait for `loadeddata` (reject on `error`; the whole cache routine's failure is silently caught).
- Let `dur = video.duration − 0.05` (avoid seeking past the last decodable frame).
- For i = 0 … 47 sequentially: set `currentTime = dur · i / 47`, await the `seeked` event, then create a 560 × 560 canvas (2D context with `willReadFrequently: true`), draw the video scaled into the full 560 × 560, apply the chroma key (§8.3) in place, and push the canvas into the frames array.
- As soon as frame 0 is cached, set a `ready` flag and force a redraw, so the grill appears immediately while the remaining frames continue to cache.

### 8.3 Chroma key (per pixel, on the 560 × 560 canvas)

For each pixel with channels r, g, b:

1. m = max(r, b)
2. k = g − m (how much "greener than anything else" the pixel is)
3. If **k > 18**:
   - alpha = max(0, 1 − (k − 18) / 52) → written as alpha·255 (integer-truncated). So k = 18 is fully opaque, k ≥ 70 is fully transparent, linear in between (threshold **18**, soft range **52**).
   - **Despill**: g = min(g, m + 6) — clamps green to at most 6 above the larger of red/blue, removing the green fringe on edges.
4. Otherwise leave the pixel untouched (alpha stays 255).

Write the image data back with `putImageData`.

### 8.4 Drawing a frame

- Frame index f (see §11.4) is computed each animation frame; only when f changes (or on a forced redraw) do both canvases get cleared and redrawn: `clearRect` the full backing store, then `drawImage(frames[f], 0, 0, canvasWidth, canvasHeight)` (scale the 560 cache to the canvas backing size). If f exceeds the number of frames cached so far, use the last cached one.
- Before `ready`, f = 0 and nothing is drawn (empty canvas).

### 8.5 Canvas sizing

- m = ceil( max(c0, c1) · 1.05 ) CSS px, where c0 and c1 are the start and end grill sizes (§9, §10). Both canvases: CSS width/height = m px; backing store = m · dpr square, with **dpr = min(devicePixelRatio, 2)**.
- The visible size is then controlled purely by a CSS `scale(size / m)` in the transform (§11.5), so the canvas never needs to be resized during scroll.

## 9. Geometry: sky panel start state and balloons

All geometry is computed in **document coordinates** (bounding client rect + `scrollY`) in a `measure()` function, run on load, after `document.fonts.ready`, and on every `resize`.

- S = sky panel rect: S.x = left, S.y = top + scrollY, S.w, S.h.
- K = kitchen panel rect, same way.

**Grill start (hanging in the sky):**
- Centre x0 = S.x + **0.81 · S.w**; centre y0 = S.y + **0.525 · S.h** (81 % across, 52.5 % down the sky panel — right of centre, in the lower half, clear of the tagline).
- Frame size c0 = **0.425 · S.h** (the square frame is 42.5 % of the panel height).

**Balloons (strings meet the grill handle):**
- Width bw = **0.30 · S.w**; height bh = bw · 2048 / 1360.
- Handle point in the panel's local coordinates: x = 0.81 · S.w, y = 0.525 · S.h − c0/2 + **0.075 · c0** (top of the frame plus 7.5 % of the frame).
- Balloon element `left` = 0.81 · S.w − bw · **0.494**; `top` = (0.525 · S.h − c0/2 + c0 · 0.075) − bh · **0.946**. That places the image's string-meeting point (49.4 %, 94.6 %) exactly on the handle.

## 10. Geometry: kitchen cover-fit mapping and landing target

The kitchen photo is `background-size: cover` and centred, so image-relative coordinates must be mapped through the fit:

- Intrinsic KI = 2688 × 1520.
- sc = max(K.w / 2688, K.h / 1520) (cover scale).
- ox = (K.w − 2688 · sc) / 2; oy = (K.h − 1520 · sc) / 2 (negative overflow offsets, centred).
- Image point (nx, ny) in 0…1 → document px: ( K.x + ox + nx · 2688 · sc , K.y + oy + ny · 1520 · sc ).
- Displayed image height H = 1520 · sc.

**Landing gap** (empty spot on the counter) = image point **(0.489, 0.641)** → (gx, gy).

**End size**: c1 = H · **0.2 / 0.83** — the grill body (≈ 83 % of its square frame) ends up 20 % of the displayed image height, matching the scale of the neighbouring air fryer.

**End centre**: x1 = gx; y1 = gy − c1 · **0.91** + c1 / 2 — i.e. the frame is positioned so that the point at **91 % down the frame** (the bottom of the grill body / its feet) rests exactly on the gap point on the counter.

**Headline**: image point **(0.496, 0.125)** → set `#ktext` left/top to that point minus K.x / K.y (panel-local px). Set `--kh` = H · 0.0285 px and `--kp` = H · 0.0205 px on `#kitchen` (1 decimal).

**Scroll end** (progress = 1): end = max(200, K.y − 0.093 · innerHeight) — the scroll position at which the kitchen panel's top sits 9.3 % of the viewport height from the top, directly under the nav, mirroring the hero panel's offset.

After measuring, resize both canvases (§8.5) and force a redraw.

## 11. Scroll choreography (runs every requestAnimationFrame)

### 11.1 Progress and smoothing

- Every frame: target = scrollY / end. Smoothed progress sp += (target − sp) · **0.18**. If |target − sp| < 0.0005, snap sp = target.
- p = clamp(sp, 0, 1) (clamp = min/max to [0, 1]).
- The loop starts after `document.fonts.ready` resolves (measure first, then begin rAF). Also call measure once immediately at script end.

### 11.2 Fall parameter and curves

- q = clamp( (p − 0.02) / 0.9 ) — nothing moves for the first 2 % of progress; the fall completes at p = 0.92.
- **Vertical** uses gravity-like acceleration: fall = q^**1.75**.
- **Horizontal drift** and **size** use smoothstep: s(q) = q² · (3 − 2q).

### 11.3 Idle motion (while hanging)

Let t = performance.now() / 1000 (seconds), idle = 1 − clamp(p · 12) — full at p = 0, faded to 0 by p = 1/12.
- **Bob** = idle · sin(1.9 · t) · **6 px** (±6 px vertical, 1.9 rad/s).
- **Sway** = idle · sin(1.3 · t) · **1.4°** (±1.4°, 1.3 rad/s).

### 11.4 Grill position, size, tilt, frame

- x = x0 + (x1 − x0) · s(q)
- y = y0 + (y1 − y0) · q^1.75 + bob
- size = c0 + (c1 − c0) · s(q)
- tilt (degrees) = sin(q · π) · **−9** + sway — tilts up to 9° counter-clockwise mid-fall and returns to level on landing.
- Frame index f = round( clamp( (q − 0.12) / 0.72 ) · 47 ), also clamped to [0, cachedFrames − 1]; 0 when not ready. The grill stays closed for the first 12 % of the fall, opens into its V around the middle, and is fully closed again by q = 0.84 — it lands closed.

### 11.5 Applying to the two canvases

With scl = size / m:
- `#gS` transform: translate( x − S.x − m/2 px, y − S.y − m/2 px ) rotate( tilt deg ) scale( scl )
- `#gK` transform: translate( x − K.x − m/2 px, y − K.y − m/2 px ) rotate( tilt deg ) scale( scl )
- Order matters: translate first, then rotate, then scale; transform-origin is the default centre of the canvas, so rotation and scaling happen around the grill's centre.

### 11.6 Balloons release

- r = clamp( p · 1.25 ) (the balloons finish leaving by p = 0.8).
- Balloon transform: translate( r · −0.06 · S.w px, bob − r · 1.25 · S.h px ) rotate( sway · 1.6 − r · 6 deg ).
- So they bob in sync with the grill while idle (same bob, sway amplified ×1.6), and on scroll they rise by 1.25 panel heights (well out of the top of the sky panel, clipped by its rounded overflow), drift left by 6 % of the panel width, and rotate to −6°, pivoting on the string knot.
- Note there is no tether: the balloons rise and the grill falls simultaneously — the release reads as "let go".

### 11.7 Landed state

Toggle class `landed` on `<body>` whenever **p > 0.9** (on every frame — scrolling back up removes it and the headline fades out).

### 11.8 Debug hook (optional, but included in the original)

Expose `window.__olla` with getter `p` (current smoothed progress), getter `ready` (number of cached frames) and the `measure` function.

## 12. Layering — why two canvases (the key illusion)

- The sky panel and the kitchen panel are **separate rounded boxes with `overflow: hidden`**, separated by a **1.19vw strip of page beige** (#e9e7df).
- The grill is drawn **twice**: once in a canvas inside the sky panel, once in a canvas inside the kitchen panel. Both are positioned from the **same document-space centre (x, y)** by subtracting each panel's own document origin. Same frame, same size, same rotation.
- Each panel clips its own copy to its own rounded window. So while the grill crosses the boundary, its upper part is visible inside the sky panel, its lower part inside the kitchen panel, and **the slice that overlaps the beige gutter is invisible** — the grill appears to pass *behind* the page, as if the panels were windows onto one continuous space. The rounded corners clip it too.
- Do NOT use a single fixed/overlay canvas — that would paint over the beige gutter and break the illusion.
- In the sky panel the giant "olla" word (z 3) and tagline (z 3) are above the grill (z 2), and the grill (later in DOM, same z 2) is above the balloons. In the kitchen panel the headline (z 4) is above the grill.

## 16. Implementation notes and pitfalls

- Everything must be computed from live layout; never hard-code pixel positions. Re-run measure on resize.
- Use one rAF loop for everything; do not use scroll event listeners for animation (the loop reads scrollY directly).
- The grill canvases are never resized during scroll — only transformed. Redraw canvas pixels only when the frame index changes.
- Draw the cached 560 px frames with the default image smoothing.
- Do not add any opacity fades, blurs or crossfades to the grill, balloons or videos. The only opacity transitions on the page are the menu items and the landed headline.
- The card video must stay a real `<video>` element (not canvas), muted, looping, inline.
- Don't add shadows to any panel, nav or pill. Flat design: white, beige, navy, yellow.
- Panels' corner radius is **14px**; nav and drop strip **10px**; pill and button fully rounded (30px / 40px).
- If the grill clip fails to load (CORS/network), the page must still work: nothing is drawn for the grill and the rest animates normally.

# Plinth — "Shared Interiors": exact recreation brief

Build a single self-contained HTML page (one file, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks, no build step) for **Plinth**, a dark editorial atlas of invented buildings. The page has three stacked sections on the home view — (1) a hero with a huge two-line serif headline, a search field and a **drifting 3D ribbon of paper "book-cards"** sweeping from huge blurred cards at the bottom-left to tiny cards at the right; (2) a **bookshelf** of upright 3D book spines where one book is turned face-out; (3) a **footer** with a giant hatched outline wordmark. Clicking any sharp card (or any shelf book) launches a **3D flight**: the book flies to the centre while spinning one full turn, then zooms until its colour fills the screen, and a simple reading view fades in. Browser Back flies it back into place. Everything below is exact; follow it literally.

## 6. The drifting ribbon — exact math

Notation: `u` = stage width, `d` = stage height (scene-h), `A` = card width 230 (200 under 640px), `L` = card height 310 (280 under 640px), card thickness base `BT` = 26, `N` = number of (filtered) books, `ss(x)` = smoothstep with clamp (`x=clamp(x,0,1); x²(3−2x)`), pitch constant `PITCH = −0.065` rad. `cb` = title block rectangle relative to the stage (left, right, bottom of the search row).

### 6.1 Card volume (shared by ribbon cards, shelf books and the flight)

A `.vol` (absolute, size `--w`×`--h`, `transform-style: preserve-3d`, origin centre) containing six faces, each absolute `--w`×`--h`, backface hidden, background `--c`, overflow hidden:
- front `translateZ(t/2)`; back `rotateY(180deg) translateZ(t/2)`;
- spine (left edge) width `t`, left `50% − t/2`, `rotateY(-90deg) translateZ(w/2)`; pages (right edge) same with `rotateY(90deg)`;
- top height `t`, top `50% − t/2`, `rotateX(90deg) translateZ(h/2)`; bottom the same with `rotateX(-90deg)`.
Every front/back/spine also contains a `.paper` overlay (absolute inset 0, z 5, background `var(--paper, var(--c))`, `opacity: calc(1 − var(--co,1))`) used to fade content out during the flight.

**Ribbon card faces** (`--w 230px --h 310px --t 26px`, ink #171614):
- Spine = `color-mix(in srgb, --c 78%, #000)`. Pages/top/bottom = paper-edge stripes `repeating-linear-gradient(#f8f4ea 0 1px, #ded7c8 1px 2px, #eee8db 2px 3px)` (90deg on pages, 0deg on top/bottom) framed by 2px bands of `--c`; bottom brightness .82, pages .9.
- Front (flex column): header 35.5px tall, padding 12px 16px 0, Geist 9px: "Plinth" left, "Nº 07" right. Photo area flex 1 (`<i>` with filter `grayscale(1) contrast(1.08)`, `mix-blend-mode: multiply` over the card colour). Text block padding 12px 16px 10px: kicker Geist 9px (margin-bottom 10.5px); title Newsreader 25px/1.04, letter-spacing −.01em, max 2 lines; footer row margin-top 14px, padding-top 8px, 1px top rule rgba(23,22,20,.2), Geist 9px: "~2 min tour" left, "Open ↗" right.
- Back: header 57.5px tall (same labels); title Newsreader 27px/1.08, padding 0 20px, max 3 lines; summary Geist 12px / 18.6px, padding 12px 20px 0, max 6 lines; footer at bottom (padding 0 20px 20px, Geist 9px/13.5px): reading time, "Visited 12 Oct 2026", then the tagline (margin-top 12px, max-width 150px).
- Binding stripes on front and back: a 7px strip at the left edge = `linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(23,22,20,.15) 0 2.5px, rgba(23,22,20,.07) 2.5px 5px, transparent 5px 6px, rgba(23,22,20,.1) 6px 7px)`.

### 6.2 Per-card projection

Each card has centre `(x, y)`, scale `s`, yaw, pitch, rotation, blur. DOM: an outer `<a class="gcard">` (absolute at 0,0, size A×L) with `transform: translate3d(x − A/2, y − L/2, 0) rotate(rotation)` and `filter: blur(b px)` when b > .05; inside it the `.vol` with `transform: perspective(P px) rotateX(pitch) rotateY(yaw) scale3d(s,s,s)` where `P = max(900, A·s, L·s)`. (Keeping blur on the 2D outer and 3D on the inner avoids flattening.) Paint order = sorted ascending by depth then slot; z-index = rank.

For bounding boxes use the same projection: rotate a local point by yaw (`x' = x cosθ + z sinθ`, `z' = −x sinθ + z cosθ`), then by pitch (`y'' = y cosφ − z' sinφ`, `z'' = y sinφ + z' cosφ`), `w = max(.1, 1 − z''/P)`, screen = centre + rotate(rotation)·(x'/w, y''/w).

### 6.3 Position along the ribbon (desktop, `u ≥ 640`)

For a card whose left-to-right screen x is `S`:
- `r = ss(S/u)`; `a = clamp(d/1050, .85, 1.2)`; **scale** `= (0.34 + (2.4 − 0.34)·(1 − r)³)·a`; **rise** `= −0.8·d·(r − 0.4)²`; **order** `= (1 − r)·100 + 1`.
- **Yaw** `= 0.35 − ss(S/u)·0.24`. Pitch −0.065. Rotation 0.
- **Depth-of-field blur**: `n = clamp(S/u,0,1)`; `lft = 1 − ss(n/.38)`; `rgt = 1 − ss((1 − n)/.035)`; side = left if lft > rgt, else right if rgt > 0; `v` = that side's value; blur = `round(v·(left ? 60 : 3)·10)/10`, capped at 60. Only cards with blur exactly 0 are clickable ("hot", cursor pointer, tabbable).
- Card size `A·scale × L·scale`, thickness `26·scale`. Depth for sorting = order + 0.7 + 0.25·(bookIndex mod 3).

### 6.4 Spacing, margins and baseline (recomputed on resize)

- Margins: with `l = 2.88`, `o = 0.408`, `e(w,h,θ) = |cosθ|·w + |sinθ|·h`: `left = max(520, e(A·l/2+193, 1.4·A·l/2+193, 5.4°), bboxRight(card A·l × 1.4A·l, thickness 26·l, yaw .35, pad 193))`, `right = max(96, e(A·o/2+13.25, 1.4·A·o/2+13.25, 14.2°), −bboxLeft(card A·o, yaw .11, pad 13.25))`. (≈ left 584, right 96 at 1440px.)
- **Spacing** `T = max(A − 135, ceil((u + left + right)/22))` (≈ 97px at 1440).
- **Baseline** `R`: march 128 steps from `p = −3A` to `u + 3A`. For each pair (previous `dp`, current `p`) with scales `f = along(dp)`, `g = along(p)`: consider it if either has zero blur or they straddle `u/2`. Let `lx = A·f.scale/2 + 13`, `oy = L·f.scale/2 + 13`, `st = 26·f.scale/2`, `r = yaw(p)`, `a = yaw(dp)`; `cx = lx cos r + st sin a`; `hz = lx sin a + st cos r`; `k = 1/max(.1, 1 − (oy·0.0649542 + 0.9978882·hz)/900)`; projected half-extents `(cx·k, (0.9978882·oy + hz·0.0649542)·k)`. If `p + x ≥ cb.left − 10` and `dp − x ≤ cb.right + 10`, then `R = max(R, cb.bottom + 24 + y − min(f.rise, g.rise))`. Finally `R += 24`. This lifts the ribbon as high as possible while every sharp card clears the search row by 24px.

### 6.5 Which cards exist each frame

`B = mod(phase, N·T)`. First slot `C = ceil((B − A/2 − left)/T)`, last `J = floor((B − A/2 + u + right)/T)`, at most 24 slots from C. Slot `n` shows book `mod(n, N)` at `S = n·T + A/2 − B`, `y = R + rise(S)`. Reuse DOM nodes keyed by slot (rebuild only if the slot's book changes); remove nodes for slots that left.

### 6.6 Motion: drift, scroll, wheel, drag

- **phase = drift + wheel + drag + 0.8 · window.scrollY.** Scrolling the page therefore slides the ribbon left at 0.8× the scroll distance while the hero scrolls up.
- **Drift**: every frame `drift += T · dt / 10` (one card spacing every 10 s), `dt = min(.05, frame delta s)`. Paused while a flight is running, when the tab is hidden, or with reduced motion. Only run the loop work while the hero is within 200px of the viewport (IntersectionObserver).
- **Horizontal wheel / shift+wheel** on the stage (`preventDefault`): add the delta (×16 for line mode, ×width for page mode) to a pending pool; each frame move a smoothed share into `wheel`: `a = −expm1(−12·dt)`, `pending' = pending·(1 − a)` (snap to 0 below .01), `wheel += pending − pending'`.
- **Drag**: pointerdown on a card records start; once moved ≥ 6px the axis locks. Horizontal: `drag = −(x − startX)` live; on release fold `drag` into `drift`. A drag suppresses the click.

### 6.7 Phone deck (`u < 640`)

Cards fan around the centre instead of the ribbon. `g = mod(phase, N·T)/T`, `v = floor(g)`, `q(e) = e³(e(6e − 15) + 10)`, `b = v + q(q(g − v))` (so each step snaps with a double smootherstep). `y0 = min(1.15, .46u/A)`; centre line `E = cb.bottom + 24 + L·y0/2 + 24`. For each slot e within ±3 of b: `t = e − b`, `n = |t|`, `o = sign(t)`; interpolate across tables at n (linear between integers 0–3): X [0,.118,.22,.2], Y [0,.045,.105,.11], ROT° [0,6,7,7], SCALE [1,.92,.86,.78], YAW [0,.07,.12,.12]. Card: x = u/2 + o·X·u, y = E + Y·u, scale = y0·SCALE, yaw = −o·YAW, rotation = o·ROT°, clickable only if n < .5, depth = −n. Here `T` is `max(A − 135, ceil((u + left + right)/22))` with left/right computed using l = 1.7, o = .45.

### 6.8 Search filter

On input: 180 ms debounce → stage gets `data-filter=out` (layer opacity 0, translateY(14px) scale(.985), .16s) → after 160 ms swap the book list (titles+summaries containing the query, case-insensitive), clear all cards → `data-filter=in` (**filterIn** .52s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1): from opacity 0, translateY(18px) scale(.985)) → remove after 520 ms. No matches: centred text at 62% height "No listings match “query”." in fg-muted 15px.

## 7. The book flight (open)

Timeline: **0–600 ms "centering"**, **600–1060 ms "zooming"**, then swap to the reading view and **220 ms reveal**.

On click of a sharp card: hide that slot's card (keep its slot hidden while flying), pause drift, `history.pushState` to `#/b/<slug>`. Create a fixed overlay (inset 0, z-index 2147483000, role dialog, focused, blocks wheel/touchmove; Escape cancels, Tab is trapped). Inside, a `.flight` div (absolute, `preserve-3d`, origin centre, `left: −n/2`, `top: −o/2`, size n×o) holding a fresh `.vol` of that book. Variables: model size `n×o×a` = 230×310×26; origin box = the card's unrotated screen box (centre, `width = A·s`, `height = L·s`); pose = card yaw/pitch/rotation, thickness `26·s`; optics: perspective `Pp = max(900, A·s, L·s)`, camera/pivot/translate offsets 0. After the first paint at t=0, measure the flight's front face rect against the source card's front face rect and shift the origin by the difference, so the hand-off is seamless.

For time t (ms, clamped 0–1060):
- `f = ss(min(1, t/600))`, `h = ss(max(0, (t − 600)/460))`.
- `p = origin.width/n`, `m = origin.height/o`, `g = min(.46·vw/origin.width, .58·vh/origin.height, 340/origin.width)` (card grows to ~340px wide at most).
- `x = lerp(originCentreX, vw/2, f)`, `y = lerp(originCentreY, vh/2, f)`.
- `yaw = lerp(yaw0, K, f)` with `K = (floor(yaw0/2π) + 1)·2π` → **one full spin** to face front. `pitch → 0`, `rotation → 0` by f.
- `scaleX = p·lerp(1, g, f)`, `scaleY = m·lerp(1, g, f)`, `scaleZ = thickness/a`.
- `w = 1.08·max((vw + 8)/(n·p·g), (vh + 8)/(o·m·g))`; `zTarget = Pp − thickness/2 − Pp/w`; `z = lerp(tz·(1 − f), zTarget, h)` → the card grows until it covers the viewport ×1.08.
- Content fade: overlay `--co = 1 − f` (each face's `.paper` overlay rises to the book colour, so at the end the front is a flat field of the card colour).
- Transform on `.flight`: `translate3d(x, y, 0) rotateZ(rotation) translate(camX·σ, camY·σ) perspective(Pp) translate(−camX·σ, −camY·σ) translate3d(tx·σ, ty·σ, z) translate(pivX·σ, pivY·σ) rotateX(pitch) rotateY(yaw) scale3d(scaleX, scaleY, scaleZ) translate(−pivX·σ, −pivY·σ)` with seed `σ = 1 − f`.

At t ≥ 1060: show the reading view underneath (page background becomes the card colour, scroll to top), wait two animation frames, add `.revealing` to the overlay (opacity 0 and `scale(1.02)` over 220 ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)), then remove it.

**Shelf books** use the same flight with: model = that book's volume (n = 210, o = its height, a = 38); pose read from the volume's computed matrix (`yaw = atan2(−m13/sx, m33/sz)`, `pitch = asin(m23/sy)`, `rotation = atan2(−m21/sy, m22/sy)`); origin from its bounding box centre and unprojected size; optics: perspective 1200, camera offset = perspective-origin (50% 100%) minus the volume's centre, pivot = transform-origin (50% 100%) minus centre, translate = m41/m42/m43; the source face is the cover if the book is open, else the spine. Paper colour = page bg (the reading view keeps the page colour).

**Reduced motion**: skip straight to t = 1060 and no reveal transition.

## 8. Return flight (Back)

On `popstate` from the reading view (or the "← All buildings" link, which calls `history.back()`): create the overlay in the final zoomed state (t = 1060) at opacity 0 and fade it to 1 over 200 ms linear ("re-emerging"). Then show the home view, restore the scroll position saved at open, and re-aim: for ribbon cards shift `drift` so that a slot of that book lands at the same x it was opened from (fraction of the stage width, clamped 24px from the edges; slot chosen nearest the current phase); for shelf books, use the book's current rect. Then animate r = 0 → 1060 ms with state `flight(1060 − r)` (zoom out 460 ms, then spin back 600 ms), remove the overlay, unhide the card, resume drift. Turn off native scroll restoration (`history.scrollRestoration = "manual"`).

# Glaze — "Crafted for Motion": exact recreation brief

Build a single-file landing page (one `index.html`, no build step) for **Glaze**, a fictional programmable video editor. It has three sections stacked vertically, plus a fixed header and a full-screen loader:

1. **Hero** — a pale blue-grey gradient screen with a large live 3D keychain hanging from the top centre (five charms on chains, real rigid-body physics, pushed by the mouse), a huge two-line headline "Crafted for / Motion" anchored bottom-left, and the subtitle with a black "Get Started" button anchored bottom-right.
2. **Logo ticker** — a grey caption and an endlessly drifting row of invented wordmarks.
3. **Timeline → statement** — a dark editor timeline with two video tracks (V1, V2) holding five motion-graphics clips, staggered in time, under a moving orange playhead; below it, a large centred three-line sentence with five empty inline slots. When the sentence scrolls into view while you scroll down, the five clips fly out of the timeline and land, small, inside the sentence. Scrolling back up sends them back onto their tracks.

Everything below is exact. Follow it value for value.

### The 3D keychain — renderer, light, camera
- WebGL renderer on the hero canvas: antialias, transparent (`alpha`), `preserveDrawingBuffer`, pixel ratio `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`, ACES Filmic tone mapping, sRGB output. Clear colour `#e3e9f2` at alpha 0 (so glass transmission samples a colour close to the page sky).
- Environment: three's `RoomEnvironment` through a PMREM generator (sigma 0.04), environment intensity 1.05. No visible background.
- Lights: a white directional "rim" light, intensity 1.6, at (−29, −14.8, −35) aimed at (0, 2.2, 0); a white directional key light, intensity 1.1, at (6, 10, 12).
- Camera: perspective, FOV 35°, near 0.1, far 500, inside a rig group. The rig starts at (0, −4, 10) and rises to (0, 0, 10) in the entrance. The camera's own offset inside the rig: desktop (aspect ≥ 0.9) (0, +1.06, −4.4) — so it sits only **5.6 units** from the z = 0 plane, centred on the keyring, which makes the bunch large and hangs it from the top centre with the keyring just above the top edge; phones/portrait (aspect < 0.9) (0, −0.9, +2.2). Canvas and camera aspect follow the hero size on every resize.
- Render only while the hero is in the viewport (IntersectionObserver).

### Physics world (Rapier) — the same rig and tuning as a real keychain
- World gravity (0, −9.81, 0); fixed timestep 1/60 s stepped from an accumulator (frame delta capped at 0.1 s).
- Every body: linear damping **2.3**, angular damping **2.9**, can sleep.
- Collision groups (Rapier interaction groups, membership in the upper 16 bits, filter in the lower 16; group bit = 1 << n): groups **none = 0, tags = 1, chain = 2**. Charms ("tags") are in *tags* and collide with *tags*. Chain links are in *chain* and collide with *none* (they pass through everything). The small start/end rings of every chain are in *chain* and collide with *tags* and *chain*.
- **Main keyring**: a steel torus, radius 0.5, tube 0.04, at (0, 3.2, 0), facing the camera (a visual only; it sits just above the top edge of the frame on desktop).
- Attachment points lie on that ring: for an angle θ (degrees), the point is (0.5·cos(θ−90°), 0.5·sin(θ−90°)) relative to the ring centre, so 0° is the bottom of the ring.

**Every charm hangs on its own chain**, built like this (θ = the charm's ring angle, base = the attachment point on the ring at z 0):
1. A fixed anchor body at base.
2. A **start ring** body at base: collider a cuboid with half extents (0.12·0.12, 0.12, 0.12), density 5; drawn as a steel torus radius 0.12, tube 0.0144, turned 90° about Y (edge-on). Spherical joint anchor↔start ring at their origins.
3. **N link bodies**, each spawned at base + (0.5, 0, 0) (they swing into place on the first frames): ball collider radius 0.1, density 1, group chain/none. Spherical joint from the start ring's local (0, −0.12, 0) to link 0's origin. Consecutive links are joined with **rope joints** of maximum length L (0.06 for metal chains).
4. An **end ring** body at base: same as the start ring but radius 0.08. Spherical joint from the last link's local (0, −0.08, 0) to the end ring's origin.
5. The **charm body**, spawned at (base.x, base.y, z): its collider and density are listed below; it is welded to the end ring with a **fixed joint** — end ring origin ↔ the charm's local point (0, offset, 0). The offset always puts the end ring just *above* the charm's collider, so nothing rubs at rest and the bunch settles completely still.
6. A constant outward force on the charm (set once, persists): with angle φ, F = (0.7·cos(φ−90°), 0.7·sin(φ−90°), z). This fans the charms apart like a real bunch of keys.

Chain links are drawn with one instanced mesh per chain: each instance sits at its link body's position, oriented along the chain (direction to the next link, or from the previous one for the last), with that direction smoothed per frame (lerp factor 10·dt). Metal links are a steel oval: a torus radius 0.062, tube 0.02, scaled 1.5 along Y, colour `#a9afba`, metalness 1, roughness 0.2, and each link is twisted about its own axis by i·16°, plus 90° on every other link, so neighbouring links interlock visually.

Per-frame orientation keeping (runs every rendered frame): the start ring's yaw is limited to ±15°; the end ring's and the charm's yaw to ±12° (yaw = the angle of the body's local +Z axis around world Y; when exceeded, rotate back to the limit about world Y and zero the Y angular velocity). The charm also eases its rotation toward identity by a slerp of 0.001 per frame, skipped while it sleeps (and without waking it).

### Mouse interaction — a push field, not a constant animation
At rest the keychain is completely still. Only the mouse moves it:
- Track `pointermove` on the window; the pointer counts as "inside" while its y is within the hero canvas. Convert to normalised device coordinates over the canvas.
- Every physics step while inside (and only if the step delta ≤ 0.1 s): cast a ray from the camera through the pointer and intersect it with the plane z = 0 → point P.
- For every charm body within **radius 2** of P (distance d, d > 0): apply an impulse along the vector from P to the charm of magnitude **4.4 · (1 − d/2)² · dt / d** per unit of that vector. Near charms get shoved away from the cursor, swing on their chains and settle back within ~5 s thanks to the damping.

### Entrance physics (the drop-in)
When the entrance starts: one GSAP timeline, defaults duration 1.5 s, delay 0.5 s, `elastic.out(1,1)`. Track 1 moves the camera rig y from −4 to 0. Track 2 runs a dummy progress 0 → 1 alongside; on every update set every body's gravity scale to **−0.25** (the charms float up while the camera rises to meet them) and, once progress reaches 1, to **1** for good (they drop and swing into place).

### The timeline ⇄ statement flight (FLIP)
- The blocks always live in their timeline slots. For block i, from the bounding boxes of sentence slot i and its timeline slot: scale = sentenceSlot.width / timelineSlot.width; x = sentenceSlot.left − timelineSlot.left + (sentenceSlot.width − timelineSlot.width) / 2; y = sentenceSlot.top − timelineSlot.top + (sentenceSlot.height − timelineSlot.height) / 2. Applying that transform (origin centre) parks the block exactly over its slot in the sentence; scale 1, x 0, y 0 puts it back on its track.
- **Start state: on the tracks.** On load, after fonts are ready, and on every width change, set every block straight to its current state with no rotation.
- **Trigger**: while the section is on screen, listen to scroll. Whenever the **sentence** is on screen (its top above the viewport bottom, its bottom below the viewport top) and the page scrolls **down**, send the blocks into the sentence; when it scrolls **up**, send them back to the timeline. Nothing happens if they are already there.
- **The flight** (one GSAP timeline): block i starts at i × 0.1 s going down into the sentence (i × 0.05 s going back up). Track 1: scale, x and y to the target over 1.5 s `power2.inOut`. Track 2, at the same start: rotation to a random angle between −15° and +15° over 0.75 s `power2.in`, then back to 0° over 0.75 s `power2.out`. The clips peel off their tracks, wobble down the page and drop into the words.
- **First reveal**: the first time the timeline comes within 300 px of the viewport bottom (once only, and only while the blocks are on their tracks), the first clip's inner content drops onto its track from y −300 px and rotation 15° over 2 s `power1.out`.

# Recreation prompt — "Kai Renn / KR.ST" dark three-view portfolio

Build a single-page, dark-mode portfolio for a fictional motion and brand designer called Kai Renn (wordmark "KR.ST"). It has three views switched by a floating dock: (1) Gallery, a WebGL sphere of looping website preview videos that you spin, zoom into and open an overview for; (2) Projects, a WebGL grid of the same videos with glass-lens edges, frosted labels and hover-to-play; (3) About, a WebGL page where a chrome robot head floats over a centred serif headline and a horizontal, endlessly looping text track slides past it, each line of text pulling away from the head like a magnet. Everything below is exact: reproduce every value.

The whole thing is one HTML file. Three.js 0.160.0 (ES module from jsDelivr, via an import map that maps "three" to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/" to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/) and GSAP 3.12.5 (https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js, global) are the only libraries. No sound.

Each tab is a 30px-tall flex row, padding 0 9px, radius 5px. It holds an italic Newsreader label (17px, line-height 1, max-width 0 and opacity 0 when inactive) and a Geist 500 number (12px, translateY −1px). Tabs: "Gallery" 1, "Projects" 2, "About" 3.

The menu dot is a 30px square, radius 5px, with a 4px ink dot that scales ×2.2 (.5s) when open. Clicking it toggles a menu panel that opens upward: fixed, bottom 66px, centred (left 50%, margin-left −110px), 220px wide, padding 14px, radius 8px, background rgba(22,22,24,.82) with 18px blur and a 1px --line border.
