## 5. View 1 — Gallery (sphere of videos)

Renderer: WebGL, alpha true, antialias on non-touch devices, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Perspective camera, fov 60, at z 12. A conversion px(v) = v × (2 × 12 × tan(30°)) / viewportHeight turns CSS pixels into world units at the sphere's depth.

Layout constants: radiusX/Y/Z 250px (×0.8 when the viewport width is 1025–1440), planeSize 104px (×0.8 in the same range; 72px at ≤640), centerScale = planeSize × 120/82, expandHeightVh 70, expandPush 1.8, expandFade 0.1, expandDuration .8s power4.out. Twenty planes (PlaneGeometry 1×1, MeshBasicMaterial transparent, double-sided, depthWrite off, starting colour #1b1b1d until its video has a frame). Plane scale: the longer side equals planeSize, the other follows the video's aspect (16:9 → wider than tall). The texture is the full video frame: repeat (1,1), offset (0,0).

Positions: a Fibonacci sphere. For item i of N: y = i×(2/N) − 1 + (1/N), r = sqrt(1 − y²), angle = π×(3 − √5)×i, position = (cos(angle)×r, y, sin(angle)×r) times the radii. On phones (≤640) the radius is the half-width minus 24px minus half a plane. Every plane always faces the camera: its quaternion is the inverse of the sphere group's quaternion.

Spin model, every frame:
- drag: velocity += pointer delta × 0.001 (x drives yaw, y drives pitch); wheel and two-finger pinch add deltaY × 0.0002 to yaw.
- velocity × 0.94 each frame (friction); accumulated angle is smoothed with a factor of 0.11; the per-frame difference of the smoothed angle is applied as a rotation about world Y (yaw) and world X (pitch), premultiplied into the group quaternion.
- idle: an auto-spin of 0.001 rad per frame about an axis tilted 23° from vertical, which stops for good after the first user interaction.

Videos: each plane's video starts loading 200ms into the intro and plays once it has a frame. Every 300ms, videos on the far hemisphere are paused (when the plane's direction faces away: z/length below −0.25; resumes above −0.1) so only around ten decode at once. While a plane is zoomed, all others pause.

Intro sequence (first visit only):
- The centre shows the wordmark "KR.ST" drawn in Geist 600 64px into a canvas, displayed 90px wide, fading in (.6s, .2s delay).
- Side labels "Kai Renn" (left) and "Motion & Brand Designer" (right), Geist 13px, sit at 9% from each edge in overflow-hidden masks and slide up from yPercent 100 (.9s expo.out, stagger .07s, delay .5s). They are hidden at viewport ≤1024px.
- A counter at the bottom (Newsreader 14px, 3 digits, "001") slides in from below (.75s power4.out, .5s delay) and then tweens towards the share of loaded circle videos (.5s power1.out each update, capped at 099).
- After 2s, once the first ten videos have frames (or 30s pass), the counter tweens to 100 and slides out upward. The first ten planes appear on a circle of radius 240px (×0.75 on phones), starting at −90° and 36° apart, each fading in (1s power3.out) and scaling from 0.01 to 70px with back.out(1.7), staggered 0.1s. The circle spins 0.5° per frame.
- 1.3s later the spin ramps up to 7.3× over 1s (power2.in).
- 0.8s after that the wordmark fades out (0.75s power2.inOut), the side labels slide up out of view, and the ten planes collapse into the centre (1.25s power2.inOut, stagger 0.05s), stacking 1.5px apart in depth and growing to centerScale.
- 0.2s after the collapse ends, everything explodes: all twenty planes move from the centre (or from their stack position) to their sphere positions over 1s power3.out, with an overshoot multiplier of 1 + 0.1 × sin(π × t). The side labels slide back in, the dock rises in, and the "DRAG TO EXPLORE" hint (Geist 10px, tracking .24em, mute) fades in at the bottom.
Reduced motion skips the intro and shows the finished sphere with no auto-spin.

Hover: raycast on pointermove (batched once per frame). The hovered plane's title and category appear in the bottom caption (13px Geist 500 title, 14px Newsreader mute category, 6px gap); the caption text leaves upward (.25s power2.in) and the new one rises from yPercent 110 (.6s expo.out). The cursor is "pointer" over a plane, "grab" within 250px of the centre, otherwise default; "grabbing" while dragging.

Click (pointer moved under 6px and total path under 10px):
- Clicking a plane expands it: expand 0→1 over .8s power4.out. Its target height is 70% of the visible height (minus the reserved overview band), its width follows its aspect, and on phones it is capped at the viewport width minus 16px. It moves to the centre of the screen. All other planes are pushed outward ×1.8 and fade to 10% opacity. Its video plays. A cursor label "Overview" (Geist 500 12px, dark text on rgba(237,237,235,.92), radius 4px, offset 14px from the pointer) follows the mouse via gsap.quickTo (.5s power3.out) and scales from .6 to 1 (.6s power4.out) while over the zoomed plane.
- Clicking the zoomed plane again opens its overview: a reserved band of 290px opens at the bottom (factor 0→1, .8s power4.out), shifting the plane up by half that band and shrinking it to 70% of the remaining height. The overview panel (max 600px wide, centred, bottom 78px) fades up from y 16 (.7s expo.out, .12s delay). It shows the title (Geist 500 15px) with "Category, Year" (Newsreader 15px mute), a Close button (12px, 26px tall, --pill), the description (Newsreader 17px, line-height 1.35, #cfcfcc, max 54ch) and three 11px tags on --pill: "Preview video", "MotionSites", "Live WebGL". The cursor label changes to "Close".
- Clicking the zoomed plane while its overview is open closes the overview. Clicking anywhere else, pressing Esc or using the Close button collapses the zoom.

## 6. View 2 — Projects (WebGL grid)

Renderer: antialias, opaque, clear colour #0c0c0d, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Perspective camera fov 35, placed at (width/2, −height/2, height/2 / tan(17.5°)), looking at (width/2, −height/2, 0), so one world unit equals one CSS pixel and the page runs downward along −y.

Layout (in px): columns 3 above 1024px, 2 at 641–1024px, 1 at ≤640px. Page padding 8, column gap 8, row gap 40. Tile width = (viewport − 16 − gaps) / cols; tile height = width × 9/16 (tiles are 16:9). The headline sits 200px from the top and is centred: "A Curated Selection of " (Geist 500 16px, tracking −0.16px) followed by "Motion and Interactive Sites" (Newsreader 400 17px). On phones it breaks into "A Curated Selection of Motion and" / "Interactive Sites" with a 20px line step. The grid starts 80px below the headline. Under each tile, 12px below: the title (Geist 500 12px, ink), then 6px lower "Category, Year" (Newsreader 13px, mute). A footer, Newsreader 13px mute, sits 240px below the last row: "Kai Renn — Index 2019–2026" centred (on phones split as "Kai Renn" left and "Index 2019–2026" right).

Tile shader: each tile samples a still (uTex) and its video (uTex2) and crossfades by uMix. Before its media lands it shows a skeleton of grey 0.085 with a diagonal shimmer band (sweep = fract(time × 0.6), band = smoothstep(0.18, 0, |(u+v)/2 − sweep|) × 0.035). uReveal fades from skeleton to media.

Loading: a tile starts loading when it is within 1.6 viewports below or 0.6 above the visible area. It creates its video (preload auto), seeks to min(1.2s, 30% of the duration), draws that frame into a 480px-wide canvas as the still, and reveals it (uReveal 0→1 over .8s power2.out).

Chip: at the tile's top-left (8px inset) sits a frosted label "01  Motion" (index two digits, two spaces, category; Geist 500 12px, padding 8px sides, 6px top, 4px bottom, radius 4px). Its shader blurs the tile's own media under it with a 32-tap golden-angle spiral (radius 40px), mixes that toward rgb 0.05 by 45%, and draws the label text on top. It follows the same still/video crossfade as the tile.

Glass-lens post pass: the scene renders into a 4×-multisampled render target, then a fullscreen pass refracts the top and bottom 8% of the screen. Inside a band, t runs 0 at the inner edge to 1 at the screen edge, sag(t) = 1 − sqrt(1 − t²), and the sample is pushed toward the inner edge by sag × band × strength (1). Inside the bands a 16-sample spectral dispersion spreads samples along y by (t − 0.5) × 0.01 × distortion × 30 with red/green/blue weights smoothstep(.8,.2,t) / smoothstep(0,.5,t)×smoothstep(1,.5,t) / smoothstep(.2,.8,t). The result is converted to sRGB at the end.

Scroll: wheel adds deltaY to a target; touch drags add the finger delta with inertia (velocity × 0.95 per frame). The rendered offset eases toward the target by 0.12 per frame and clamps between 0 and page height minus viewport height.

Hover (desktop wider than 1024px): the hovered tile's video starts playing and uMix tweens to 1 (.45s power2.out); leaving tweens it back to 0 and pauses. A 64px round "View" bubble (italic Newsreader 16px, dark on rgba(237,237,235,.94)) follows the pointer through gsap.quickTo (.5s power3.out) and scales .6→1 with opacity (.75s power4.out on enter, .6s on leave). On touch or ≤1024px, the tile closest to the viewport's vertical centre plays instead.

Entrance: the headline pieces fade in (.3s) while their letters resolve out of random ". : · , ; _" glyphs over 1.1s (power2.out; each character resolves once progress passes 0.7 × its position + 0.3 × random). Tiles, chips, titles and categories fade in and rise 60px (opacity .9s power2.out, position 1.2s expo.out), delayed .35s + .08s per column + .06s per row.

Click a tile: a lightbox fades in (.45s) over a rgba(8,8,9,.86) backdrop with 14px blur. It holds the video at up to 1100px wide and 70vh tall (16:9, contain, radius 6px) rising from scale .94, y 20 (.9s expo.out). Below it: the title (Geist 500 15px) with "Category, Year" (serif mute), the description (serif 17px), and a Close button. Esc, Close or clicking the backdrop closes it and unloads the video.

## 7. View 3 — About (chrome bot + horizontal magnetic text track)

Renderer: antialias, opaque, clear colour #0c0c0d, scene background #0c0c0d, output sRGB, no tone mapping, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Camera fov 45 at z 13. A half-float render target the size of the canvas holds the scene without the bot and the lens disc, for the click effect.

Environment (for the chrome): a PMREM of a small black room (background #0a0a0b) lit by emissive white panels: a 14×5 ceiling panel at y 6 (intensity 1.1), a 3.2×10 strip at x −6 (1.0), a 2.4×10 strip at x 6 (0.85), a 12×2.2 panel behind at z −6, y −1.5 (0.6), a 5×4 panel in front at (3, 2.5, 6) (0.8) and a 14×6 floor at y −6 (0.22). Keeping every panel at or below about 1.1 is what avoids bloom-like blocks.

The bot (own model, built from primitives and centred on its bounding box):
- Head: a sphere of radius 1 scaled (1.1, 1, 0.98) in chrome (MeshPhysical, white, metalness 1, roughness 0.07).
- Visor: a front patch of the same sphere (phi from π/2 − 1.02 over 2.04 rad, theta from π/2 − 0.5 over 1.0 rad), scaled 1.5% larger, in near-black glossy material (#040405, metalness 0.3, roughness 0.12, clearcoat 1, clearcoat roughness 0.04).
- Eyes: two capsules (radius 0.075, length 0.2) at x ±0.3, y 0.03, sitting on the visor surface, flattened to 45% depth, in an unlit #f2f2ee material.
- Antenna: a chrome stem (0.022–0.03 radius, 0.42 tall) at y 1.15 with a 0.095 chrome ball at y 1.38.
- Ears: chrome tori (radius 0.2, tube 0.065) at x ±1.1 with dark visor-material caps (cylinders of radius 0.15).
- Halo: a chrome torus (radius 0.78, tube 0.05) under the head at y −1.28, tilted 0.92 × 90°, spinning at 0.35 rad/s.
- Scale: the bot is always 200px tall on screen (×0.9 at ≤1440px wide, ×0.85 at ≤1024px), placed at the screen centre, z −1.

Shader additions on all bot materials (injected with onBeforeCompile):
- Liquid-glass reveal: a front line rises from the bounding-box bottom minus the band (0.97) to the top plus 0.25 × band, wavy by value noise (amplitude 0.95 × (1 − reveal)). Fragments above it are discarded. Within one band below it the surface is mixed toward a brighter, #8fa0ff-tinted "liquid" look, with a blue (#1621ff) shimmering meniscus line (power-3 falloff, ×1.4).
- Hover glow: a #1621ff glow around the raycast hit point (radius 1.09 world units, spread 0.262, falloff power 3, brightness 0.4), multiplied by a hover factor that eases toward 1 at 0.1 per frame on hit and back toward 0 at 0.05 per frame.

The reveal runs 0→1 over 3.85s power2.out with a 1s delay on the first visit (0.45s on later visits). Clicks are ignored below 0.8.

Behaviour every frame:
- Mouse follow: the target rotation is x = clamp(vertical offset from the centre ÷ half the height, ±0.62), y = clamp(horizontal offset ÷ half the width, ±0.59), z = 0.2 × horizontal offset. The current rotation eases toward it at 1 − (1 − 0.08)^(60 × dt). Before any mouse movement on desktop the target is (−0.62, 0.59, 0.2); on phones it is 0.
- Float: y = sin(phase) × 0.2 × amplitude × reveal, where the phase advances by dt × 1.5 × speed, eased with factor 1 − (1 − 0.08)^(60 × dt).
- Blink every 3–5s: the eyes squash to 10% height over 0.18s and back.
- Sleep: after 30s with no mousemove, wheel, pointerdown, touchstart or keydown (desktop only, fully revealed), the eyes close to 20% height (1.1s power2.inOut), the rotation target tweens to (0.42, 0, 0.12) over 1.4s, and the float slows to speed 0.35 and amplitude 1.6 (1.6s). Any input wakes it: speed and amplitude return over 0.8s, the eyes snap open, and the head shakes.
- Head shake: the y offset goes +0.22 (0.09s), −0.18 (0.12s), +0.10 (0.11s), then 0 (0.18s).

Click on the bot (fully revealed, not mid-effect):
- The rotation freezes. A lens disc (a circle of radius 1 at z −8) scales from 0 to 10 world units over 4s expo.out; once it passes 6.14 it dissolves (0→1 over 0.8975s sine.inOut), then resets.
- The disc samples the background render target in screen space and pulls it toward the centre: zoom pull = 0.5 × 0.30 × nd², where nd is the distance normalised to the disc's screen radius. The rim (from nd 0.85) is pulled inward by 0.2344. Chromatic dispersion of 1.64 × 0.004 applies from nd 0.6, with 8 samples and per-channel Gaussian weights.
- Light on top: a white nova (Gaussian, size 4 × glow 11 × 0.003, intensity 0.285 × 11/17 × 1.15), a #252ba7 ring at radius 0.49, width 0.08 (×0.9 × 11/17 × 1.8) with a wide aura, a thin white rim at 0.483, and an edge ring at 0.478 (width 0.06, softness 1, intensity 1.053, #252ba7).
- Dissolve order: the light fades by 60%, the distortion by 80%, and the alpha from 80% to 100%.
- At the same time the bot plays one of two alternating hit reactions, then the head shake:
  - Recoil: rotation x −0.45 and y +0.18 (0.16s power3.out) with the eyes squashed, then back with elastic.out(1, .45) over 0.9s.
  - Spin: one full turn on y (1.1s power3.inOut) with a z wobble of 0.25 settling with elastic.out(1, .5).

Text layer: all text is drawn into canvases (software-backed 2D contexts, willReadFrequently, drawn at the renderer's pixel ratio, linear filtering, no mipmaps) on planes at z −8. One world unit equals visibleHeight(at z −8) ÷ viewport height px.

Headline: a full-viewport canvas centred on the screen. Newsreader 300 at 75px (62px at ≤640; at ≤1024 it shrinks to fit the widest word and wraps), line height 1.18, tracking −0.01em, ink. Three lines:
- "Shaping quiet systems into"
- "restless, precise and wildly kinetic"
- "Motion™ that people remember."

The "™" is Geist 400 24px (16px at ≤1024), raised by 0.2 × the font size and spaced 8px after "Motion". Fifty-six pixels below the last line, centred, is "Currently at Northfold® Studio" in Geist 500 14px (12px on phones). Hovering just "Northfold® Studio" fades a background-coloured plane over it to 50% opacity (0.55s expo.out).

Horizontal track: the wheel (whichever of deltaX or deltaY is larger) and swipes on either axis move a target. The rendered offset eases toward it at 0.12 per frame, with touch inertia of 0.95 per frame. Scrolling down or right moves the content left. Every element's x is wrapped with ((x + L/2) mod L) − L/2, so the track loops forever and the headline returns after the last stop. L = (end of the last block + 260px, or 140px on phones) + half the viewport width.

The track starts half a viewport plus 200px (70px on phones) to the right of the headline. Stops alternate between above the centre line (block bottom 78px above centre; 64px on phones) and below it (block top 78px below centre). Each stop advances x by max(0.62 × block width, 200px) + 90px (150px + 60px on phones). Blocks are left-aligned.

Every block starts with a grey heading (Geist 500 12px, mute). The ten stops, in order:
1. Paragraph, top. "Motion" over "Product films, UI motion and 3D loops that explain a product in seconds." (Newsreader 300 22px, 29px line step, wrapped at 320px; 16px below the heading).

Magnetic make-space (the key interaction): the bot owns an oval keep-out zone on the text plane, with radius X 3.4 world units and Y 4.0543 (both ×0.7875 at ≤640) and 0.35 of padding.
- Every frame, for each line of each block, take the horizontal distance from the bot to the nearest point of that line's own text: 0 if the text spans the bot's x.
- If that distance is less than the X radius, the oval's half-height there is h = Ry × sqrt(1 − (d/Rx)²) + padding. A line above the bot must keep its lower edge at least h above centre; a line below must keep its upper edge at least h below centre.
- Lines are processed from the one nearest the bot outward. Each line's need is at least its inner neighbour's current shift, so lines never overlap.
- Each shift eases toward its need with a factor of max(0.1, 0.14 − 0.012 × k), where k is the line's order from the inside, so the nearest line leads and the outer lines follow a touch later. All of them ease back to their resting place once the bot has passed.

### 2.4 Cover-crop math (the `.ph` tile system)

Every photo tile is an empty div with class `ph` and a `data-img="sheet:index"` attribute, such as `ringa:1`. The `.ph` class gives it background-color var(--secondbg) and background-repeat no-repeat. An IIFE at the top of the body script then does the following.

1. **Cell lookup.** Split the key on ":" and read the sheet. Compute column and row as above. Set x0 = xs[col].start + 8, x1 = xs[col].end − 8, y0 = ys[row].start + 8, y1 = ys[row].end − 8. The constant inset IN = 8 keeps any white gutter edge from showing. The cell rect is x = x0, y = y0, w = x1 − x0, h = y1 − y0, all in native sheet pixels.
2. **Fit (object-fit: cover by hand).** Read the element's offsetWidth (ew) and offsetHeight (eh), and skip if either is 0. Offset sizes ignore transforms, so the rotating ring tiles still measure correctly. Scale k = max(ew / w, eh / h). Focal point fx = data-fx, defaulting to 0.5, and fy = data-fy, defaulting to 0.5. Set background-size to (W × k)px by (H × k)px, where W and H are the sheet's native pixel size, not the proxy width. That is why a 1200px-wide WebP still lines up. Set background-position to −(x·k + (w·k − ew)·fx) px horizontally and −(y·k + (h·k − eh)·fy) px vertically. The overflow is split by the focal fraction, so fy = 0.3 keeps more of the top of the cell.
3. **Wiring.** For every [data-img] element, set the inline background-image to url("…proxy URL…") once, call fit, and register it with one shared ResizeObserver that calls fit again on every size change.

Focal overrides used on the page: life:0 with data-fy .3 (step 3), life:2 with data-fy .35 (step 4 wide card), studio:1 with data-fy .2 (step 4) and pre:1 with data-fy .3 (step 4). No data-fx is used anywhere.

## 4. Head, libraries, root scale, type scale

**Document.** The html element has lang "en" and starts with class "is-loading". The head contains, in this order:

1. meta charset utf-8.
2. meta viewport width=device-width, initial-scale=1.
3. title "Reshoot — AI Beauty Photography".
4. The meta description quoted in section 1.
5. One style block.
6. A tiny inline script. It adds is-loading to the html element again, then removes it if prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches.
7. Three blocking scripts, in this order:
   - GSAP 3.12.5 from `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js`
   - ScrollTrigger 3.12.5 from `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/ScrollTrigger.min.js`
   - SplitType 0.3.4 from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/split-type@0.3.4/umd/index.min.js`

The body has classes "body light". The main behaviour script sits at the end of the body, and ScrollTrigger is registered there.

**Global resets.** Every element gets box-sizing border-box and zero margin and padding. html and body get overscroll-behavior none. body gets background-color var(--mainbg), color var(--fonts-100), display flex with column flow, and font-size 1vw. Links inherit colour. The plain focus outline is removed, and :focus-visible gets a 2px solid var(--accent) outline at 2px offset. Images are display block. The `main.page` wrapper is a flex column with min-height 100svh and overflow hidden.

**Fluid root font-size.** These rules sit on html. The rem inside each calc is the browser's 16px initial size.

| Viewport width | html font-size |
|---|---|
| Above 2560px (base rule) | 1.484375rem (23.75px fixed) |
| ≤ 2560px | calc(−0.006009615384615419rem + 0.9314903846153846vw) |
| ≤ 1728px | calc(−0.009345794392523143rem + 0.9345794392523362vw), so 1rem = 16px at 1728 |
| ≤ 991px | calc(0.021640258215962493rem + 1.8779342723004695vw) |
| ≤ 767px | calc(−0.0025905678851174934rem + 4.14490861618799vw) |

All of these are `@media screen and (max-width: …)` rules, written in descending order so the narrowest match wins.

**Type-scale variables on :root.** --h1 5.5rem, --h2 7.5rem, --h25 4rem, --h3 3.25rem, --body2 1rem, --tag 1.125rem, --title1 1rem, --title2 0.875rem, --title3 1.5rem, --btn 1.0625rem. ## 8. Animations and interactions

### 8.1 Preloader timeline

- **Start.** It starts on window load, or immediately if document.readyState is already "complete". A failsafe setTimeout calls it after 8000 ms. A started flag makes it run only once.
- **Returning visitors.** It reads localStorage "reshoot_preloader_v1" and treats the visitor as returning if the value is "1", then writes "1". The speed factor sp is 1/5 for a returning visitor and 1 otherwise. Both reads and writes are in try/catch.
- **Scroll lock.** It scrolls to (0, 0), then sets overflow hidden on both html and body.
- **Image hard-cuts.** A setInterval every 500 × sp ms (100 ms when returning) sets z-index 9 on the layer at the current index and 1 on the others, then advances the index modulo 4.
  - Before the first tick the last DOM layer (pre:1) is on top.
  - From then on the sequence is pre:3 (0.5 s), pre:0 (1.0 s), pre:2 (1.5 s), pre:1 (2.0 s), and so on.
  - These are instant cuts with no crossfade.
- **New-visitor counter.**
  - Steps are 0, 17, 35, 58, 76, 89, 100 with total T = 2.5 s, run on a GSAP timeline with delay .5.
  - Each segment tweens a plain number from the previous step to the next over 2.5/6 ≈ 0.4167 s with ease power2.out, writing Math.round of the value into the counter.
  - The first segment is 0 to 0, a short hold. The counter reaches 100 at 3.0 s.
  - The number is printed with no "%" sign.
- **Returning-visitor text.** The counter text becomes "Synced". It also gets its own fromTo: from opacity 0, y 8px, blur 6px to opacity 1, y 0, blur 0, over .2 s with delay .1 and ease power2.out.
- **Main timeline.**
  1. Set all direct children of the preloader to visibility visible.
  2. Fade them in: fromTo opacity 0 with filter blur(20px) to opacity 1 with blur(0px), duration 1 × sp, stagger .05 × sp, ease power2.out. The three children are the counter, the logo/loader row and the image stack.
  3. Fade them out: opacity 0 with blur(20px), duration 1 × sp, delay 2.5 × sp, stagger .05 × sp, ease power2.in.
  4. Fade the whole preloader to opacity 0 over .6 × sp with ease power2.in.
- **On complete.**
  - Remove is-loading from html and set the preloader to visibility hidden.
  - Dispatch the document event "preloader:done", which starts the hero intro.
  - Clear the image interval.
  - After 1 × sp seconds (gsap.delayedCall), release the scroll lock.

### 8.2 Opening sequence table (first visit, seconds from window load)

| Element | Property | Starts at | Duration | Stagger | Ease |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preloader children (3) | opacity 0→1, blur 20px→0 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.05 | power2.out |
| Preloader photos | hard-cut z-index swaps | 0.5, then every 0.5 | instant | — | — |
| Counter | 0→17→35→58→76→89→100 | 0.5 (first segment holds at 0) | 6 × 0.4167 = 2.5 | sequential | power2.out per segment |
| Preloader children | opacity 1→0, blur 0→20px | 3.6 | 1.0 | 0.05 | power2.in |
| Preloader overlay | opacity 1→0 | 4.7 | 0.6 | — | power2.in |
| "preloader:done" fires (T₀) | — | ≈ 5.3 | — | — | — |
| Hero text words (©, year, "scroll", "down", headline words) | flash keyframes | T₀ + 0 | 0.15 per word | 0.2 per word, per element | power2.out |
| Header logo link | opacity 0→1, y 24→0, scale .9→1 | T₀ + 0.10 | 0.5 | — | power2.out |
| Header pill + menu holder | same | T₀ + 0.20 | 0.6 | — | power2.out |
| Ring cards (8) | opacity 0→1, scale .5→1 | T₀ + 0.30 | 0.5 | 0.12 | power2.out |
| Sign-in + Get started (is-header-btn) | opacity 0→1, y 24→0, scale .9→1 | T₀ + 0.35 | 0.5 | — | power2.out |
| Hero chips (12) | opacity 0→1, x 40→0, scale .9→1 | T₀ + 0.35 | 0.5 | 0.12 | power2.out |
| Scroll unlock | overflow restored | T₀ + 1.0 | — | — | — |

On a returning visit, every preloader value is divided by 5, so T₀ ≈ 1.06 s. The hero intro timings stay the same.

### 8.3 Hero intro details

At script start, unless reduced motion is on, GSAP sets these hidden states:

- Every data-hero-text element: opacity 0.
- Header logo link, header pill, menu holder and .is-header-btn: opacity 0, y 24, scale .9.
- Ring cards: opacity 0, scale .5.
- Hero chips: opacity 0, x 40, scale .9.

On "preloader:done", playHeroIntro builds a timeline. Each data-hero-text element is word-split (see 8.11), its words are set to opacity 0 in the violet flash colour, and the element itself is set to opacity 1. All three elements' word tweens are placed at time 0 with stagger .2 and ease power2.out, using three keyframes per word:

1. opacity 1 in --flash-a over .05.
2. Colour to --flash-b over .05.
3. Opacity to the word's stored final opacity (1, or .5 inside .u-fonts-50) and colour to var(--fonts-100) over .05.

So each word blinks violet, then pink, then settles to ink. The headline's words are "Your", "shelves,", "radiantly", "re-shot.", and the italic span keeps its styling. The other tweens follow the table above.

### 8.4 Ring rotation

- On load, each holder is set to rotate d and its photo to rotate −d. This runs even with reduced motion.
- Unless reduced motion is on:
  - hero__carousel__in rotates to 360 over 32 s, ease none, repeat −1. The ring turns clockwise.
  - Every ring photo rotates by "−=360" over 32 s, ease none, repeat −1.
- The two cancel out, so every photo stays perfectly upright while its card tilts around the orbit. The intro's scale and opacity tweens act on the cards, not the photos, so they don't conflict with the rotation.

### 8.5 Hero chip loop

The CSS keyframe "hero-row" runs 24 s, linear, infinite. It goes from translate(var(--tx, 0%), var(--ty, 0%)) to translate(var(--tx-end, 0%), var(--ty-end, −100%)). With two identical rows, the list scrolls up seamlessly, one row-height (100%) per cycle. At ≤991 the variables change it to a leftward horizontal scroll (see section 7). The 7rem mainbg fades soften the entry and exit.

### 8.6 Menu open and close

- **Open timeline** (paused). Tween the card to y 0 and the open width, height and padding over .4 s with ease power2.out. Then tween the groups to opacity 1, stagger .05, duration .3, starting .2 s before the first tween ends ("−=0.2").
- **Burger timeline** (paused, duration .25, ease power2.out, both bars at time 0):
  - The top bar goes from y −.2rem to y .025rem and rotate 45.
  - The bottom bar goes from y .2rem to y −.025rem and rotate −45.
  - Transform origin is centred, which forms an X.
- **Label scramble.**
  - Total frames T = 20, one frame every 20 ms. L is the longer of the old and new label lengths.
  - On frame f, character i shows the new character if i is within the new label and f/T > i/L. Otherwise it shows "•".
  - After frame 20 the text is set to the final label and the interval clears.
  - The label scrambles to "Close" on open and back to "Menu" on close.
- **Opening.** Set the open flag, add class is-open to the button, play the burger timeline, scramble to "Close", set aria-label to "Close menu" and play the open timeline.
- **Closing.**
  - Clear the flag, remove is-open, reverse the burger, scramble to "Menu" and set aria-label to "Open menu".
  - Tween the groups in reverse DOM order to opacity 0 (stagger .05, duration .2).
  - Call the open timeline's reverse with argument .3. In GSAP this jumps the playhead to 0.3 s and plays backward from there, so the close is a quick ~0.3 s collapse, not a delay.
- **Close triggers.** Clicking the button while open, clicking anywhere outside both the card and the button, pressing Escape, and clicking any menu group (so following a link closes it).
- **Resize.** While open, the card tweens to the new open size over .2 s. While closed, it snaps to the new collapsed state.

### 8.7 Hover-stagger roll (buttons and menu links)

- **Scope.** Every [hover-stagger] element. Skipped entirely under reduced motion. The hover target is the closest [hover-stagger-wrap] ancestor (the whole pill for buttons), or the element itself for menu links.
- **Setup.**
  - The element gets position relative (if unset), display inline-block (if unset) and overflow hidden, plus the 100% × 70% centred mask from section 5.
  - Its text moves into a span, and a clone of that span is placed absolutely at left 0, top 100%, directly underneath.
  - SplitType splits both spans into characters.
- **Animation.** A paused timeline (defaults: duration .2, stagger .02, ease power1.inOut) tweens the original characters and the clone characters from yPercent 0 to −100 at the same time, with opacity held at 1. The label rolls up letter by letter and the copy rolls in from below.
- **Triggers.** mouseenter calls restart. mouseleave calls reverse.

### 8.8 Scroll percentage indicator

A requestAnimationFrame loop runs forever, including under reduced motion. Each frame computes m = scrollHeight − innerHeight. The value is 0 if m ≤ 0, otherwise scrollY / m × 100 clamped to 0–100. It writes Math.round(value) + "%" into #progress. The markup holds "100%" until the first frame.

### 8.9 Theme toggle

- **Storage.** The localStorage key is "reshoot-light" and holds the string "true" or "false". The default is "true" (blush) when the key is missing or invalid.
- **apply(on).** Toggles class light on body, writes the key (in try/catch) and sets aria-pressed on every [data-theme-toggle] to the opposite of on, so pressed means night. Except during the initial apply, it dispatches a window CustomEvent "theme:changed" with detail on.
- **Clicks.** A click flips the current state.
- **Icons.** CSS shows the sun in blush and the moon in night.
- **Flash colours.** Word-flash colours are read from the body's computed --flash-a and --flash-b. The scroll-flash colours are captured when the page loads.

### 8.10 Scroll word flashes

- **Targets.** Every [data-flash] element (the How it works heading and the Photoshoots h3) and every [data-flash-stb] element (the four step headlines and four step numbers).
- **Setup.** Each is word-split. Unless reduced motion is on, its words are set to opacity 0 in --flash-a.
- **Trigger.** A ScrollTrigger on the element with start "top 90%" and once: true.
- **Animation.** Words staggered .1 apart, three keyframes each:
  1. opacity 1 in --flash-a over .2 with ease power2.out.
  2. Colour to --flash-b over .05.
  3. Colour to the final ink over .1. The final ink is var(--ink) (#3a1d43) for data-flash-stb, otherwise var(--fonts-100).

### 8.11 Word-split helper

A TreeWalker collects every text node inside the element. Each node is split on whitespace runs, keeping the whitespace as plain text nodes. Each non-blank piece is wrapped in a span with the given class (flash-word or hero-flash-word). Its data-final-opacity is .5 if the text node's parent is inside a .u-fonts-50 element, otherwise 1. Nested markup such as the italic spans and line breaks is preserved, because only text nodes are replaced.

### 8.12 How it works column crawl and brightness

- **Crawl.** CSS keyframe "columnanima": translateY 0% to −100% over 24 s, linear, infinite, on both duplicated columns. The phrase list rises endlessly inside the masked 34rem window.
- **Brightness loop.** A requestAnimationFrame loop with fadeFinish = .15. Each frame, for each of the six phrases, it measures the phrase relative to the window:
  - top = phrase top − window top, bottom = top + phrase height, H = window height.
  - Default opacity is .2.
  - If the phrase is at least partly visible (bottom > 0 and top < H):
    - n = clamp(1 − bottom / H, 0, 1)
    - p = clamp(n / (1 − .15), 0, 1)
    - opacity = .2 + .8 × p
- **Effect.** Phrases near the bottom of the window sit at .2. They brighten linearly as they rise and reach full opacity once their bottom edge is in the top 15% of the window. The mask then fades them out at the very top.

### 8.13 Trusted-by marquee

The CSS keyframe "marquee" runs translateX 0% to −100% over 24 s, linear, infinite, on both duplicated rows. This gives a seamless leftward loop. Each row's padding-right equals the gap, so the seam stays even. The 6.5rem side fades blend the tiles into the page.

### 8.14 Step slides: pinned 3D stack

This applies to every slide except the last, and is skipped under reduced motion.

- **Tween 1: tip back and shrink.** Tween the content card to:
  - rotationZ = (Math.random() − .5) × 10, a random tilt between −5° and +5°, chosen once per page load
  - scale .7
  - rotationX 40
  - ease power1.in

  Its ScrollTrigger pins the slide's content wrap (the element carrying perspective 250vw), with the slide as trigger, start "top 0%", end "+=" + innerHeight (one viewport of scroll) and scrub true. Pin spacing uses GSAP defaults.
- **Tween 2: fade.** Tween the same card to autoAlpha 0 with ease power1.in. Its ScrollTrigger has the card as trigger, start "top −80%", end "+=" + 0.5 × innerHeight and scrub true.
- **Effect.** As you scroll past a slide, it holds in place while it tips backward away from you, shrinks and twists slightly, then fades out across the last stretch of the pin. The next pastel slide scrolls up to replace it. The fourth slide is never transformed.
- Inside step 02, the "Generating…" chip icon ticks constantly via spinStep.

## 9. Reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)

- **Preloader.** The inline head script removes is-loading at once. The CSS media query sets the preloader to display none. The preloader JS also hides it, removes is-loading and returns early: no scroll lock, no counter, no localStorage write.
- **CSS animations.** These are set to none with !important: the hero chip rows, the How it works columns, the marquee rows, the preloader spinner and the step chip spinner.
- **Ring.** The cards are placed at their angles with upright photos but don't rotate.
- **Hero intro.** Not run, and the hidden starting states are never applied, so the header, hero text, ring cards and chips are visible right away.
- **Scroll flashes.** Words are still split into spans but never hidden or animated.
- **Hover-stagger.** Not set up at all, so links and buttons keep plain text.
- **Step pin and 3D stack.** Not created. The four slides scroll normally as 100vh panels.
- **Still active:**
  - The menu open/close timeline, burger and scramble (not gated)
  - The theme toggle
  - The percentage readout
  - The How it works brightness loop, which keeps applying position-based opacities to the now-static column
  - The ResizeObserver photo cropping

# Noa Ellsworth — Sea Ring Portfolio: exact recreation prompt

Build a two-view, single-file portfolio site (one `index.html`, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks, no build step) for a fictional product engineer called **Noa Ellsworth**. View one, **Home**, is a full-screen stage: a serif sentence and three stats across the top, and below it a large rounded panel showing a looping video of a sunlit turquoise sea with white flowers, inside which a 3D cylindrical ring of 16 landscape website-preview video cards surrounds the viewer and spins with the wheel, drag and touch. View two, **Build**, is a rounded panel with the same sea video behind a centred two-line headline and a fill-in-the-blanks project brief card. A full-screen loader opens the site: the name "Noa." rises letter by letter, a percentage odometer counts up while the card posters load, the cards assemble into a small tilted ring, then the ring expands to wrap the viewer while the loader fades, the panel's clip closes to its rounded frame and "Noa." flies into the nav wordmark. Every value below is taken from the shipped source; reproduce it exactly.

Structure: the wall fills the frame (cursor grab, touch-action pinch-zoom, no text selection). Inside it a "lens" box (absolute, inset −100vh 0, carries the CSS perspective) contains the ring centre: a zero-size element at 50%/50% with preserve-3d and transform translate(--intro-x, --intro-offset) rotateZ(--intro-roll) rotateX(--intro-tilt) scale3d(s, s, --intro-sz), where s = wall-scale × --intro-scale and wall-scale = 1.1 on desktop (0.9 when the viewport is ≤760px tall, 0.8 on phones).

Cards: 16 slots, one per site. Each card is an anchor (opens the motionsites link in a new tab), height 160 px and width 160 × the site's ratio (so 284 px for 16:9, 256 px for 16:10, 240 px for 3:2), positioned with its centre on the ring centre (top −80 px, left −width/2), preserve-3d, starting at opacity 0. Inside: a tilt wrapper (preserve-3d), a frame (inset −9px, 3px border in the world colour, radius 24px, glow 0 40px 80px −30px world colour, clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0 round 24px) that opens to full in .55 s on hover), and the face (radius 16px, overflow hidden, backface hidden, navy #0E2A3B fill, shadow 0 18px 36px −24px rgba(0,0,0,.45), and a reflection below it: `-webkit-box-reflect: below 10px linear-gradient(transparent 52%, rgba(255,255,255,.32))`). The face holds the poster image (cover), the preview video (cover, muted, loop, playsinline, preload none, opacity 0 → 1 over .4 s on "playing"), a chip at bottom-left (14px in, pill, rgba(0,0,0,.45) background, white Geist Mono 13px, a 6px dot in the world colour, text "No. 01" … "No. 16"; it fades out on hover), and a label bar (12px from left/right/bottom, padding 11px 14px, radius 12px, world colour background, `--on` text; contents: world label in Geist Mono 500 12px .12em tracking, the site title in Newsreader 22px truncated, and an "↗" that springs from translate(−6px,6px) to 0 over .5s cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) with .15 s delay; the bar is revealed by clip-path from the left over .5 s with 50 ms delay on hover). A paper-coloured overlay on the face rises to opacity .6 on cards whose world is not the one currently focused by the sentence hover.

Slot → site mapping: slot e shows site `((e − a·16 + min(3, N−1)) mod N + N) mod N`, where a = floor((360e/16 + rotation + 180) / 360) and N = 16 (with exactly 16 sites this is a stable offset of 3; during the intro rotation is treated as 0). Slot angle: `angle(e) = ((((360e/16 + rotation + 180) mod 360) + 360) mod 360) − 180`.

Ring geometry for expansion e ∈ [0,1] (e = 0 small intro ring, e = 1 final ring):
- tilt = −22 × (1 − e) degrees
- radius = 460 + 1340 × e
- anchor = −radius × sin(tilt) + 460 × sin(−22°) × (1 − e)
- perspective = 1000 + (760 − 1000) × e (final camera distance 760)
- roll = −20 × (1 − e) degrees
- card scale = 0.52 + (2.3 − 0.52) × e²

Card placement for a slot with angle r and formation f ∈ [0,1]: n = ((r + 180) mod 360), a = n/360, i = clamp((f − 0.7a)/0.3, 0, 1), s = 1 − (1 − i)³, yaw l = −180 + n × s, effective radius c = radius − (1 − s) × a × 24, x = −sin(l) × c, z = −cos(l) × c, appear = min(1, 2.5 i). The card transform is translate3d(x, 0, z) rotateY(l deg) scale(card scale) and its opacity = appear. A card is hidden if z × cos(tilt) ≥ perspective − 70 (behind the camera), or, once the intro is complete, if |r| > 96°. If z > radius² / perspective, the face is flipped with rotateY(180deg).

Per-frame camera values (A = wall-scale × (fit + (1 − fit) × e), fit = min(1.05, (innerWidth − 32)/1240, 0.66 × innerHeight/800) ÷ wall-scale, introOff = 0.44 × innerHeight − frame centre y): --intro-offset = introOff × (1 − e) + anchor × A px; lens perspective = perspective × A px; lens perspective-origin = 50% calc(50% + introOff × (1 − e) px); --intro-tilt, --intro-roll in degrees; --intro-x = 160 × sin(roll) × A px; --intro-sz = A; --intro-scale = fit + (1 − fit) × e. (So during the intro the small ring sits centred at 44% of the viewport height, tilted and rolled, slightly to one side, and it grows into the frame.)

Rotation: a target value m and a displayed value g that follows m with a spring (stiffness 150, damping 27, mass 1). Every frame (frame factor k = dt in ms ÷ 16.67, capped at 3): an easing factor E moves toward 0.2 when the mouse is over a card (checked every third frame with elementFromPoint) and toward 1 otherwise, by min(1, 0.08 k) of the gap. If not dragging, not focused inside the wall and not reduced motion, m increases by 0.3 × E × k degrees once the intro is complete; during the intro by 0.3 × (0.5 + 0.5e) × clamp((78 − m)/20, 0, 1) × E × k (so it spins until about 78° and eases off).
- Wheel (window listener, non-passive, Home view only, ignored over inputs or with Ctrl/Meta; it always prevents page scroll): delta = the larger of deltaY/deltaX, ×16 for line mode or ×innerHeight for page mode, then m += 0.5 × clamp(delta, −480, 480). Only after the intro completes.
- Drag (mouse button 0 on the wall, after the intro): m = start m + 0.2 × (the larger-magnitude of dx, dy); moving more than 4 px marks it a drag, and a click right after a drag (within 50 ms) is cancelled; cursor shows "grabbing".
- Touch (one finger, not starting on a card or input): same 0.2 factor.
- With reduced motion the spring jumps straight to the target.

- Videos: a card's preview video plays only when formation > 0.5, |angle| ≤ 78°, the tab is visible, the Home view is shown and reduced motion is off; its src is set the first time it needs to play; it pauses otherwise. When a slot's site changes, the video is paused, its src removed and reloaded.

**6d. Sentence hover and preview card.** Only after the intro has entered. Hovering a choice marks it active and the sentence "hovering": all words drop to opacity .28 except the active choice, whose words turn the `--on` colour while its marker sweeps in (scaleX 0 → 1, .5 s main ease) behind it in the world colour. For build/brand/learn the stage gets a focus attribute that dims every card of another world (a page-black overlay to .6). Its media area is 146 px tall, shows that site’s poster as its background (and as the video poster) straight away, and plays the first site of that world (Look Circle for brand, Video Studio for build, Sphere Gallery for learn); below it a meta block (12px padding 14px, 12px Geist, line-height 1.5): a Geist Mono 500 11px .1em line with an 8px world-coloured square, "BRAND · LOOK CIRCLE" style text, then the world blurb. ## 11. Reduced motion

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` hides the loader, stops the petals, motes and grain jitter, shows all text instantly with no transitions on masks, underlines, markers, frames or labels, keeps the scene as the still image (videos never play), keeps the ring static at its final shape, and makes wheel/drag move it directly without the spring. Changing the setting live re-applies this.

# Foldwild Studio: full recreation brief

Build this website exactly as described: a single-page, hash-routed site for a fictional paper-craft studio called **Foldwild Studio**. Everything is one `index.html` with inline CSS and JavaScript, plus GSAP 3.12.5 from `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js`. There is no build step and no framework. All imagery and video are loaded from the URLs listed below. Do not substitute, re-host or crop them into new files. Several objects are shown from one sprite sheet using CSS `background-size` and `background-position`.

The site has five page types: an **intro film**, a **home slider**, a **product page** (five items), a **menu overlay**, and an **editorial page** (About, Studio, Journal). The look is matte low-poly folded-paper sculptures floating over flat pastel colour fields, with deep-ink type.

## 5. Home slider (the stage)

The stage is a fixed full-screen layer holding:
- a background div whose colour follows the current slide;
- a "card" div, a W×H rectangle with `transform-origin: 0 0`, hidden until Discover;
- for each slide, in this stacking order: the back object and its shadow, then a `<canvas>` with the two-line title, then the front objects and their shadows.

The stage uses `cursor: grab`, `touch-action: pan-y` and `user-select: none`.

### 5.1 Viewport configuration (recomputed on resize)

- **Desktop**, any viewport except a phone or tablet held upright:
  - title font size `fs = round(min(0.099W, 0.19H))`;
  - `coeffWidth = 1`;
  - card (the Centre stage product layout): width = 0.36W, height = 0.64H, x = (W − card width)/2, top 0;
  - `dcx = 0.1W` (how far the title drifts right while closing), `dcy = 0`.
- **Mobile**, W ≤ 820 and H ≥ W:
  - `fs = 0.13125W`;
  - `coeffWidth = 1.5`;
  - card x = 0.11W, card width = 0.78W, card height = 1.2675 × card width;
  - `dcx = 0`, `dcy = −0.1H`.
- In both, `ratio = 0.5 × fs / 190`.

### 5.2 Index controller

This is a looping, smoothed index, ported from the original site's slider.

- **State:** `goto`, `smooth`, `int` (the rounded current slide), `drag`, `trans`, `rc` (0 means home, 1 means closed into the card), `alpha`.
- `real(i) = ((i mod 5) + 5) mod 5`.
- **Every frame:**
  - if a tween is running (`trans`), `smooth = goto`;
  - otherwise `smooth += (goto − smooth) × k`, with k = 0.1 while dragging and 0.05 otherwise, and snap when the difference is under 1e-5;
  - `int = real(round(smooth))`. When it changes, fire "change".
- **`gotoIdx(t)`:**
  1. Wrap `smooth` and `goto` with `real`.
  2. Take the shortest path round the loop: if |target − goto| > 2.5, add or subtract 5.
  3. Set `int` to the target immediately.
  4. GSAP-tween `goto` to the target over **2.5s, ease `power4.inOut`**, with `trans = true` until it completes.
- **On "change":**
  - move the tab indicator;
  - restart the autoplay timer;
  - point the Discover link at `#/item/<id>`;
  - tween the background colour from its current value to the new slide's colour, over 2.5s with quintic in-out easing if a slide tween is running, otherwise 1s linear.

### 5.3 Per-frame rendering of each slide i

1. Compute `n = i − real(smooth)`, wrapped into the range −2.5…2.5. Show the slide only while −1 < n < 1.
2. **Slides move vertically (the Left index layout).** Offsets are `dx = 0` and `dy = n × H × coeffWidth`: the next slide waits one screen below and rises into place, and the previous one leaves upward. Each object multiplies dy by its own speed `sp`, so back and front objects separate as they travel.
3. **For each object**, precompute on resize:
   - width w = card width × l/100, height h = w × cropH/cropW;
   - card position `pc = (cardX + o.l/100 × cardW, o.t/100 × cardH)`;
   - home offset `ph = (dx' × W/100 − pc.x, hy − pc.y)`, where hy = d.y × H/100. On desktop each object's home x is remapped to clear the left tab list: `dx' = 20 + 0.76 × d.x` (for example 7 → 25.3, 23 → 37.5, 70 → 73.2). On phones dx' = m.x.
   - On mobile, keep objects clear of the title. With `tt = H/2 − 1.36fs − 0.04H`: hy = min(hy, tt − 0.95h) for the back object, and hy = max(hy, tt + 1.45fs) for front objects.
4. **Each frame, for each object**, with r = 1 − rc:
   - `X = pc.x + ph.x × r + md.x` and `Y = pc.y + dy × sp + ph.y × r + md.y`.
   - **Mouse parallax:** `mouse = −(clientX − W/2, clientY − H/2)`, scaled by r.
   - Each object eases its own offset: `md += (mouse × ratioObj − md) × mr`, with `mr = lerp(0.05, 1, rc)`.
   - `ratioObj` interpolates from 0.005 to 0.01 for the back object and from 0.02 to 0.05 for front objects, by the object's index ÷ 2.
5. **Title canvas.** Pre-render each line in Figtree 500 at size fs, colour #1D1B2E, `textBaseline: middle` at 0.62fs, at up to 2× device pixel ratio. The lines are spaced 1.02fs apart and centred on each other.
   - **Stretch effect** (from the reference's letter sprites): each line has one "stretch column", a 1px-wide slice inside a letter.
   - To choose it, scan columns between 25% and 75% of the line width. Keep columns whose ink pixels are all between 36% and 86% of the line height and number fewer than 13% of that height. Score each as `count + |x/width − pref| × h × 0.4`, where pref is 0.42 for line 1 and 0.58 for line 2, and take the lowest score.
   - Stretch amount `i = 225 × clamp(|n|, 0, 0.5) × ratio × |horizontal component of the slide direction|`. With vertical slides this is 0, so the column-picking code is kept but the title does not stretch in this layout.
   - Draw the left part, then the 1px slice stretched to width i, then the right part shifted by i. If n ≥ 0 the left edge stays fixed; if n < 0 the whole line shifts left by i.
   - **Canvas position:** desktop x = 0.56W + rc × dcx − canvasWidth/2 (lines centred on each other); phones x = 0.5W − canvasWidth/2. y = H/2 − 1.36fs (minus 0.04H on phones) + rc × dcy + dy. Opacity is `r × alpha`.
6. The home UI's opacity is `r³ × alpha`.

### 5.4 Home UI (tabs and Discover)

- **Layout (desktop and landscape).** The tabs are a fixed vertical list on the left: left 46u, vertically centred (top 50%, translateY(−50%)), 22u left padding, 18u gaps, aligned to the left. Discover is fixed on its own: left `56vw − 96u`, top `71vh − 33u`, sitting under the title.
- **Tabs.** Each is a row of a small number ("01" to "05", 11u, 70% opacity, baseline-aligned, 12u gap) followed by the name at 19u, weight 500. Tabs are at 62% opacity; the current tab is at 100%.
- **Tab indicator.** A vertical 2px bar (`rgba(29,27,46,.22)`) at the list's left edge, positioned with `translateY` and `scaleY` (base height 100px, transform-origin top). Inside it, an ink progress line is scaled with `scaleY` from 0 to 1. Tab positions are measured as each tab's top and height relative to the list.
- **Indicator move**, ported exactly from the reference but along y. Let a = the new tab's top, l = its height relative to the bar, and `n_w` = its height in pixels. ("Right" below means down the list, "left" means up.)
  - Moving right: phase 1 keeps x and stretches the width to reach the middle of the new tab (scx = (a − x + 0.5 × n_w) / barWidth), and the progress line goes to 1.
  - Moving left: phase 1 sets x to x + 0.5(a − x) and widens so the right edge stays put, and the progress line goes to 0.
  - Phase 1 is 0.5s `quint.in`. Phase 2 moves to (a, l) over 0.5s `quint.out` with the progress line fading out, then the autoplay timer starts.
- **Autoplay.** The progress line runs from scaleX 0 to 1 over **5s linear**, then the slider moves to the next slide. It pauses while dragging, while the menu is open and away from home.
- **Discover.** A 66u-tall ink pill with 38u horizontal padding, ivory 17u text "Discover", and a 26×12u arrow. The shadow is `0 18u 40u rgba(29,27,46,.18)`. On hover the pill rises 3px and the arrow moves 6px right over 0.5s.

### 5.5 Input

- **Drag** (pointer events on the stage):
  - On pointerdown, ignored during a tween: record the start x and the start smooth value; `drag = true`; add an `is-grabbing` class to the html element; pause the timer.
  - On move, project the pointer movement onto the slide direction V = (0, H × coeffWidth): `panIndex = −(Δx·Vx + Δy·Vy) / |V|²`, so dragging up by one screen height moves one slide forward, and `goto = startSmooth + panIndex`. Velocity is the projected px/ms, smoothed (new = 0.6 × old + 0.4 × instantaneous).
  - On release: `r = goto − velocity × 0.2`, rounded to n. If real(n) is still the start slide and |panIndex| > 0.3, step one slide in the drag direction. Set `goto = n`; the smoothing then settles it.
- **Wheel:** `delta = wheelDeltaX || −deltaX`, else the Y equivalent, times 0.5; then `goto −= delta / (3W)`. 50ms after the last wheel event, round `goto`.
- **Keyboard:** ArrowLeft and ArrowRight step through the slides.
- **Phones held upright** keep the stacked horizontal tab row and Discover under the title (see §11), but the slides still move vertically and dragging is up and down.

### 5.6 Entrance

After the intro film (or straight away with reduced motion):
- `smooth = goto = int − 0.45`, then tween `goto` to `int` over 2s with `power3.out`;
- tween `alpha` from 0 to 1 over 1.1s linear.

## 6. Discover → product (the card morph)

The full-screen colour shrinks into the product card while the objects fly into it.

- Show the card div with its colour starting at the current background colour.
- Over **1.5s with `expo.inOut`**, tween `rc` from 0 to 1 and `goto` to the item (shortest path, `trans = true`).
- **Each frame:**
  - card transform: `translate3d(cardX × rc, 0, 0) scale(lerp(W, cardW, rc)/W, lerp(H, cardH, rc)/H)`;
  - card colour: a mix from the start colour to the item's card colour by rc.
- The objects move from their home positions to their card positions (ph × r → 0), the mouse influence fades out, and the title fades out while drifting by dcx/dcy.
- When the morph completes:
  - build the product page DOM with the card and objects at exactly the same pixel positions;
  - hide the stage;
  - fade the text in with a 30px rise, 1s `expo.out`, staggered 0.08s.
- **Back to home** via the logo or Collection, while within the top 30% of the page:
  - set the stage to that item with rc = 1 and show it;
  - fade the page out over 0.35s;
  - tween rc back to 0 over 1.5s with `power4.inOut`.
- **From any other page to home:** fade the stage `alpha` from 0 to 1 over 1.5s.
- **Between other pages:** fade the current page out over 0.6s, then fade the new one in over 0.8s. The editorial cover image and card enter from −40px and +40px with 1.3s `expo.out`.

## 4. Scene layers (fixed, full viewport)

1. `#scene` is fixed with `inset: 0` and `overflow: hidden`. It contains:
   - **`#grade`**: absolute, `inset: -3%`, `transition: filter .9s ease`. It holds the filter grade. Inside it:
     - **`#bg`**: absolute, `inset: 0`. The background image uses `center / cover`. Its transform is `translate3d(var(--bx), var(--by), 0) scale(1.04)` with a `.6s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)` transition.
     - **`#tint`**: absolute, `inset: 0`, `mix-blend-mode: soft-light`, `transition: background .9s`.
   - **`#vignette`**: absolute, `inset: 0`, with two backgrounds:
     - `radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 45%, transparent 55%, rgba(20,18,22,.38) 100%)`;
     - `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(20,20,24,.22), transparent 18%, transparent 70%, rgba(20,20,24,.35))`.
2. **Parallax** runs on `pointermove` with `x = clientX/innerWidth − .5` and `y = clientY/innerHeight − .5`:
   - `--bx = −x·22px` and `--by = −y·12px` on `#bg`;
   - `--mx = x·10px` on the model's inner wrapper.

## 6. The model

**Structure:** `#modelWrap.full` › `#shadow` + `#modelInner` › `#breath` › (`#figs`, `#scan`, `#hotspots`).

- **`#modelWrap`:**
  - `left: 800px; top: 72px; width: 440px; height: 663px; margin-left: -220px`;
  - `transform-origin: 50% 100%`, `transition: transform 1s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.2,1)`.
  - Framing classes:
    - `.full`: no transform;
    - `.mid`: `translateY(345px) scale(1.5)`, waist-up with the head kept in frame;
    - `.portrait`: `translateY(940px) scale(2.4)`, head and shoulders.
- **`#modelInner`:**
  - transform `translate3d(var(--mx),0,0) scaleX(var(--build)) scaleY(var(--height))`;
  - origin at the bottom centre, `.7s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)` transition.
- **`#breath`:** animation `breath 5.5s ease-in-out infinite`, going from `scaleY(1)` to `scaleY(1.006)` and back, with the origin at the bottom.
- **`.fig`:**
  - absolute, `inset: 0`, image at `center bottom / contain`, `filter: var(--real)`;
  - one `.fig` per shown look, stacked in `#figs`.
- **`#shadow`:**
  - a 300×34 ellipse at the bottom centre (`bottom: -6px`);
  - background `radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(30,28,26,.55), rgba(30,28,26,0))`, `blur(4px)`.

### 6.1 Outfit swap (the signature effect)

`showLook(i)`:
1. Immediately mark grid card `i` as `.on`.
2. Await `IMGS[i].decode()`, so the wipe never reveals an unloaded image. A token guards against rapid clicks: only the latest call proceeds.
3. Append a new `.fig.in` with look `i`'s `w=1000` image. `.in` starts at `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)` and runs `wipe 1.05s cubic-bezier(.7,0,.25,1) forwards` to `inset(0 0 0 0)`. The new outfit is revealed **top to bottom** over the old one. No opacity is involved.
4. At the same moment, restart `#scan.go`. `#scan` is a 2px line spanning `left: -10%; right: -10%`:
   - background `linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #fff 25%, #fff 75%, transparent)`;
   - glow `0 0 22px 6px rgba(255,255,255,.55), 0 0 60px 18px rgba(214,226,255,.35)`.

   Its animation, `scan 1.05s` with the same easing, moves it from `top: 0` to `top: 100%`. It stays fully visible until 92%, then fades. The line rides exactly on the wipe edge.
5. On the wipe's `animationend`, remove all older `.fig`s and drop `.in`.
6. Re-render the accordion rows, the hotspots and the favourite states for the new look.

`rescan()` replays only the scan line. It is used as "re-render" feedback by the tuning controls.

# Recreation prompt: "For Noor" pitch letter with a photo globe

Build a single-page personal pitch letter from a small brand studio called **ostra** to a future client called **Noor**, who is opening a natural wine and ceramics bar. The page is quiet, letter-like and editorial: one narrow centred column of small sans-serif type on warm paper, broken by one loud element, a large interactive 3D globe made of curved, rounded photo tiles. It ends with an auto-sliding row of work cards and a handwritten sign-off. Recreate it exactly as described below: every text string, colour, size, spacing value, asset URL, animation timing and interaction. Use plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, plus three.js 0.160.0 for the globe.

## 4. The globe in detail (three.js)

### Renderer and camera

- **Renderer:** WebGLRenderer on the canvas with antialias and alpha on, pixel ratio `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`, and output colour space LinearSRGB. The textures are left in their default colour space, so photo colours pass through untouched and match CSS.
- **Camera:** a perspective camera at z = 3.7 looking at a unit sphere (radius 1). The vertical field of view is `2·asin(1/3.7)` in degrees × 1.015, so the sphere exactly fills the square canvas with a hair of margin.
- **Resizing:** a ResizeObserver on the wrapper resizes the renderer and camera aspect.

### Tile layout

- **Latitude rings:** nine bands, with heights from top to bottom of 11, 14, 17, 21, 24, 21, 17, 14 and 11 degrees. There is a 2.1° gap between bands, and the whole stack is centred vertically on the sphere, so roughly 6° caps at each pole stay empty.
- **Random source:** a seeded Park–Miller generator with seed 20261113, where s = s·16807 mod 2147483647 and the value returned is s / 2147483647.
- **Tiles within a band:** each band is filled around the full 360° with tiles whose arc width is the band height × (0.82 + random × 0.62), divided by sin(band centre polar angle). That keeps tiles roughly square-ish to 1.4 wide on the surface.
  - Gaps between tiles in longitude are 2.1° / sin(centre).
  - All widths and gaps are scaled together so the ring closes exactly.
  - The ring starts at a random longitude.
- **Collage jitter:** 45% of tiles are shortened by a random 0–20% of the band height, flush to either the top or the bottom of the band at random.
- **Geometry:** each tile is its own SphereGeometry patch (radius 1, phiStart/phiLength from the longitude span, thetaStart/thetaLength from its polar span). Segments are about one per 3°, with a minimum of 6 each way. Tiles are truly curved with the sphere, not flat cards.

### Photo assignment

- **Order:** tiles are numbered in creation order, top band first and around each ring. Tile n uses sheet n mod 8 and quadrant floor(n/8) mod 4, so all 32 photos are used before any repeats.
- **Cropping:** each tile's photo is a UV sub-rectangle of its quadrant. Inset 3.5% from the quadrant edges, then centre-crop to the tile's on-surface aspect (arc width / arc height at the tile's mid-latitude).

### Material

The tiles use a custom ShaderMaterial: transparent, depth write on, front faces only, so the back of the sphere is culled and the paper shows through the gaps.

- **Vertex shader:** passes the UV and the facing factor (dot of the view-space normal with the direction to the camera, clamped 0–1).
- **Fragment shader:**
  - **Rounded corners:** a rounded-rectangle signed distance in tile space, scaled by the tile aspect, with corner radius 0.085 of the tile height. The edge is antialiased with smoothstep over ±1.2·fwidth.
  - **Colour:** sampled at rect.xy + uv·rect.zw.
  - **Rim fade:** the colour mixes toward paper (#E4DED3) by (1 − facing)^2.2 × 0.62, so tiles near the silhouette wash out softly into the page, as in a printed sphere.
  - **Opacity:** alpha is the mask × the per-tile opacity uniform. Fragments under 0.003 are discarded, and the output is premultiplied (colour × alpha, alpha).

### Base pose

- The sphere group's X rotation (tilt) rests at 0.2 rad, so the top cap shows. Its Y rotation starts at −0.6 rad.
- There is no idle auto-rotation: the globe stays still unless something moves it.

### Load intro

The intro starts when all 8 textures have loaded, or after a 4s safety timeout.

- **Shape (1.1s, ease-out cubic, p from 0 to 1):**
  - Uniform scale s = 0.42 + 0.58p, with the Y scale additionally multiplied by (0.22 + 0.78p). The globe starts as a wide, squashed band and inflates into a sphere.
  - Group y position = −(1 − p) × 0.62, so it rises from the bottom.
  - A spin-in adds (1 − p)² × 2.6 rad/s to the Y rotation.
- **Tile build-up (one by one, bottom to top):**
  - Each tile gets a start delay: (ring index counted from the bottom ring) × 0.2s, plus (its position in its ring sorted by longitude ÷ tiles in ring) × 0.42s.
  - From its delay, the tile fades in over 0.5s with ease-out cubic.
  - At the same time its mesh scale goes from 0.9 to 1.0, so it rises out from just inside the sphere onto the surface.
  - The bottom ring fills first, tile after tile around it. Each ring above starts 0.2s later, and the top ring finishes about 2.5s after the start.
  - Once the time passes the end of the sequence, all tiles are set to fully visible in one final pass, even if frames were skipped.

### Scroll coupling

- Every scroll event adds (scroll delta in px × 0.0042) rad/s to the angular velocity, clamped to ±6. Scrolling down spins one way and scrolling up spins the other.
- Each frame, the Y rotation advances by velocity × dt, then the velocity decays by exp(−2.6·dt). The globe coasts briefly and stops.
- Tilt eases back toward 0.2 with a factor of 1 − exp(−2.2·dt) per frame.

### Drag

- **Pointer down on the canvas:** capture the pointer, add the `drag` class (grabbing cursor) and zero the velocity.
- **Pointer move:** the Y rotation changes by dx × (2.6 / wrapper width), and the tilt changes by dy × (2.6 / wrapper width) × 0.8, clamped to −0.55…0.75. The horizontal velocity is tracked as a smoothed value (0.6 old + 0.4 new).
- **Release:** the tracked velocity becomes the spin velocity (clamped ±6), so the globe keeps spinning and slows with the same decay. The tilt then eases back to 0.2.

### Performance

An IntersectionObserver (120px root margin) pauses rendering while the globe is off screen, except during the intro and tile build-up.

## 6. The carousel (the core of the section)

### 6.1 Geometry, measured from the runway each time it resizes

```
narrow = innerWidth <= 820
MH  = min(runwayH * (narrow ? .66 : .705), runwayW * (narrow ? 1.05 : .92))   // model box height
MW  = MH * 421/634                                                           // model box width
U   = MH / 634                                                               // unit scale
CX  = runwayW * (narrow ? .5 : .523)                                         // centre x
FEET= runwayH * (narrow ? .86 : .85)                                         // centre model's feet y
```

- Set `--mh` and `--mw` CSS variables from these values.
- Re-measure on `resize` and with a `ResizeObserver` on `#runway`.

### 6.2 Model element

- `.model`: absolute, `width: var(--mw); height: var(--mh); margin-left: calc(var(--mw)/-2)`, `transform-origin: 50% 100%`, `pointer-events: none`.
- It contains:
  - **`.fig`**, filling the box: the look image at `center bottom / contain`, with `-webkit-box-reflect: below -2px linear-gradient(transparent 68%, rgba(255,255,255,.22))`. This produces the floor reflection.
  - **`.hit`**, the only clickable area: `left: 29%; right: 29%; top: 3%; bottom: 2%; pointer-events: auto; cursor: none`, with the default cursor on the centre model. This body-sized hit area means the centre model's transparent margins never block clicks on its neighbours.

### 6.3 Continuous position and depth table

`pos` is a float carousel position (start 2). Each frame, for each model `i`:
- `d = wrap(i − pos)` into `[−3, 3)`;
- interpolate linearly through this table by `a = |d|`.

| a | x offset | scale | feet lift | blur px | brightness | opacity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 160 | .94 | 12 | 1.2 | .90 | 1 |
| 2 | 284 | .85 | 59 | 4 | .72 | 1 |
| 3 | 362 | .78 | 95 | 8 | .55 | .55 |
| 3.6 | 392 | .74 | 110 | 11 | .48 | 0 |

- x offset and lift are multiplied by `U`; blur is multiplied by `max(.6, U)`. The x offset takes the sign of `d`.
- `transform: translate3d(CX + x, FEET − lift − MH, 0) scale(sc)`.
- `filter: blur(bl) brightness(br)`; `opacity: op`; `z-index: 100 − round(a·10)`.
- The model with `|d| < .5` gets class `c` (centre).

The result is that neighbours overlap the centre slightly, and the row recedes into depth: feet higher, smaller, blurrier, darker. The outer pair fades away, and models wrap round smoothly from one side to the other.

### 6.4 Transition

`go(i, dir)`:
1. Take the shortest signed distance `d = wrap(i − pos)`. If `dir` is given and the distance is exactly 3, use that direction.
2. Tween `pos` from its current value to `pos + d` over `760 + (|d| − 1)·140` ms with **`ease = t => 1 − (1 − t)^4.2`**. This is a fast ease-out: about 60% of the travel happens in the first 150 ms, followed by a long soft settle.
3. On start: set `active`, hide the pins, hide the VIEW cursor, swap the sidebar cards (§8.2), update the timeline, restart the autoplay timer, and set the floor-glow tone.
4. On end: show the pins.

### 6.5 Ways to change looks

- Click a side model's `.hit` area.
- **Drag / swipe** on the runway:
  - `pos = startPos − dx/(170·U)`;
  - on release, snap with `go(round(pos))`, and swallow the click that follows a drag;
  - `touch-action: pan-y` on the models layer.
- The ← and → buttons step one look in that direction, and the ArrowLeft / ArrowRight keys do the same.
- Click a timeline segment to jump to that look.
- Autoplay (§7).

### 6.6 VIEW cursor

`#view` is fixed and follows the pointer:
- 58px white circle centred on the pointer;
- the text `VIEW` inside: 8px/600, .18em tracking, colour `#0d0e10`;
- `scale(0)` → `scale(1)` with `.35s cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1)`.

**Every animation frame**, run `elementFromPoint(lastPointer)`. Show the circle only when the pointer is over a non-centre model's hit area, no tween is running and no drag is in progress. Re-checking every frame keeps it correct while models slide under a still cursor.

## 6. Outfit compositor (the core)

**State:** `look = {t, k, s, g}`, starting as `{t1, k1, s1, g1}`, which is the base photo.

**`draw(ctx, look)`:**
1. Draw base at full size.
2. For each category in the order **shoes → skirt → top → bag**, if its key is not `*1`:
   - on an offscreen canvas, draw the variant's mask, then `source-in` the variant image (this gives the masked variant);
   - on the main canvas, use `destination-out` with the mask, which punches the region out;
   - then use `lighter` with the masked variant.

This is an exact soft replacement (premultiplied lerp), so any combination composes cleanly.

**Swap animation (`render(category)`):**
- Draw the new state into `#cNew`.
- Animate a sweep from the category's region top to its region bottom, over 720ms with ease-in-out (quadratic). Region y-ranges as fractions of the figure height: top `.07–.53`, skirt `.32–.57`, shoes `.53–1`, bag `.45–.75`.
- Each frame:
  - `#cNew` has `clip-path: inset(0 0 (100 − y)% 0)`, so it shows above the line;
  - `#cOld` has `clip-path: inset(y% 0 0 0)`, so it shows below the line.
  - This means the old outfit never shows through the transparent areas of the new one.
- A 2px white glint line with a glow rides on `y`.
- At the end, copy the state to `#cOld` and reset both clips.
- If a new change starts mid-sweep, first redraw `#cOld` with the previous state.

**`wear(key)`:**
- push the history;
- update `look`;
- render;
- sync the whole UI (§7);
- fly the clicked thumbnail to the strip slot;
- toast "Trying on · <name>".

`cycle(cat)` steps 1 → 2 → 3 → 1.

**Undo** restores the previous state and animates the changed region.

# BUNTO° — kids' basics hero with a rotating garment ring

Build a single-screen, full-viewport hero for a fictional premium kids' clothing brand called BUNTO°. It is one HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript, no frameworks and no build step. The page never scrolls (body overflow hidden). Everything below is exact; follow the numbers, the copy and the timings as written.

## 1. Overall idea

A warm off-white page with tiny wide-tracked all-caps labels around the edges, a huge pale ghost word "TINY" behind the centre, and six floating kids' garments arranged on an invisible horizontal ring that turns slowly and continuously, left to right across the front. The front piece is the largest, straight and highest. The side pieces are smaller, lower and lean outwards. The back pieces sit lower still, tucked behind the side pieces. Visitors can drag or fling the ring with mouse or touch. Hovering a piece updates the large index number bottom-left. Clicking any piece opens a product view: the ring freezes, the chosen piece glides to the left and grows, the others shrink and drift out to the sides, a round close button appears on the piece, and a product panel with name, description, four colour swatches and an "Add to bag" link fades in on the right. Swatches swap the garment's colourway in place. "Add to bag" flies a shrinking copy of the garment in an arc into the bag icon in the top bar, which bounces and shows a count badge.

## 8. The ring (the core motion)

Products in ring order (index: column, starting row): 0 = Romper Peach (1, 0), 1 = Tee Pink (2, 1), 2 = Dungarees Sage (0, 2), 3 = Cardigan Butter (3, 3), 4 = Bucket hat Pink (4, 1), 5 = Cardigan Sage (3, 2). The colours alternate so neighbours never match.

Product copy:

- Dungarees: category "Dungarees · Ages 1–5"; description "Washed cotton twill with a bib pocket, adjustable straps and rolled-up cuffs."
- Romper: "Romper · Ages 1–3"; "Soft knit in organic cotton, with wooden shoulder buttons and snaps for easy changes."
- Tee: "Long-sleeve tee · Ages 1–6"; "Heavyweight organic jersey with a little chest pocket and ribbed cuffs."
- Cardigan: "Cardigan · Ages 1–6"; "Chunky hand-feel knit with wooden buttons, made for layering on cool mornings."
- Bucket hat: "Bucket hat · Ages 1–6"; "Garment-dyed cotton canvas with a soft brim that folds into any pocket."

The product name is "<Colour> <Kind>", for example "Peach Romper" or "Sage Cardigan".

Geometry, in design px, run every animation frame with `requestAnimationFrame`:

- Constants: centre `CX = 718`, `CY = 418`, radius `R = 411`, vertical drop `DROP = 110`, base scale `S0 = 0.97`, tilt `TILT = 9°`, `N = 6`, `STEP = 2π/6`.
- Piece *i* sits at angle `θ = base + i·STEP`. Let `c = cos θ`, `s = sin θ` and `k = (1 + c)/2` (1 at the front, 0 at the back).
- x = `CX + R·s`; y = `CY + (1 − k)·DROP`; scale = `S0·(0.72 + 0.28·k)`; z-index = `round(k·100) + 1`; rotation = `TILT·s` degrees, so pieces on the left lean outwards anticlockwise, pieces on the right lean outwards clockwise, and the front piece is straight.
- Apply it as `transform: translate(x·u, y·u) scale(scale) rotate(rotation deg)`.
- Auto-turn: `base` grows by `OMEGA·dt` every frame, where `OMEGA = STEP / 4.2 s`. One slot every 4.2 s and a full turn every ≈ 25 s. Because x = R·sin θ, the front pieces travel left to right, come round behind on the right, and re-emerge on the left. Clamp `dt` to 50 ms, and do not advance while the tab is hidden.
- Front piece: the one with the largest cos θ. It drives which pagination dot is active.

Drag and fling:

- `pointerdown` on the stage (left button only, not in the product view) starts a drag. The stage has `touch-action: pan-y` (vertical page scrolling still works on phones), `cursor: grab`, and `cursor: grabbing` while dragging, with user-select disabled.
- `pointermove` (on window): convert the horizontal pointer delta to design px (divide by stage width / 1440) and add `dx / R` to `base`, so the front piece tracks the pointer. Keep a smoothed velocity `v = 0.6·v + 0.4·(dθ per 16.7 ms)`. Once the accumulated movement passes 6 design px, mark the gesture as a drag, add the `dragging` class and capture the pointer. A drag never opens a piece.
- On `pointerup` or `pointercancel`: if it was a drag, start a fling of `clamp(v, ±0.12)` rad per frame. Each frame add the fling to `base` and multiply it by `0.92^(dt·60)` until it falls below 0.0005. At release the auto-turn weight drops to 0 and climbs back to 1 at 0.8 per second, so the throw blends smoothly back into the slow turn.
- The auto-turn and the fling pause during a drag and while a piece is open.

Hover: entering a piece sets the index to that piece's number (01–06) and the label to "<KIND>" / "COLLECTION". Leaving resets it to "01" / "ROMPER COLLECTION". The number change is a vertical roll: the current digits slide up out of view (translateY −110%, .7s `cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)`), then after 300 ms the new digits jump to +110% with no transition and roll back to 0.

## 9. Product view (click)

- Clicking (or pressing Enter/Space on) any visible piece opens it. Add class `detail` to the hero. A blend value `d` animates 0 → 1 over 560 ms with ease-in-out cubic (`t<.5 ? 4t³ : 1 − (−2t+2)³/2`). Closing animates it back to 0 the same way.
- Chosen piece: interpolate from its live ring pose to a target. Desktop target x 470, y 425, scale 1.12; phone target x 716, y 300, scale 0.86. Rotation goes to 0, and z-index becomes 300.
- Every other piece: move outwards along x by `240·d` (away from the chosen piece's ring x), multiply its scale by `1 − 0.45·d`, multiply its opacity by `max(0, 1 − 1.4·d)`, and disable its pointer events.
- Floor shadow: translate by `((targetX − 718)·0.82·d, (targetY − 418)·d)` design px (an extra −60·d px vertically on phones) and scaleX `1 − 0.45·d`, so it settles under the opened piece.
- Pagination dots fade to `opacity: 1 − d`.
- The ring stops turning while open and resumes from the same angle after closing.
- Close button: placed at `(targetX + 205·targetScale, targetY − 200·targetScale)` design px, which is the top-right corner of the opened garment. With class `detail` it becomes opacity 1, scale 1 and clickable, after a .25s delay (opacity .35s ease, transform .45s `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`). Focus moves to it.
- Product panel: each child starts at opacity 0 and translateY 18u. In detail it goes to opacity 1 and none, with opacity .55s ease, transform .7s `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`, staggered by 60 ms per child (0, .06, .12, .18, .24 s).
- Index: shows the opened piece's number. The "KIND / COLLECTION" label fades out upwards (−8px) while "CHOOSE / A COLOUR" fades in from +8px.
- Closing: the close button, the Escape key or keyboard all reverse everything. Focus returns to the piece and the index resets to 01 / ROMPER COLLECTION.

Colour swatches: clicking a swatch puts the new row's crop on `.art2`, adds a `swap` class (opacity transition .35s), and fades `.art2` to 1. After 360 ms it copies the crop to `.art`, hides `.art2` again without a transition, and plays a small scale bounce on the piece (×(1 + 0.035·sin(π·t)) over 420 ms). The product name, the aria-label, the selected ring and `aria-checked` all update.

## 10. Entrance (on load, once)

Wait until the sheet image has loaded (with a 2.5 s failsafe), then:

- Every chrome element starts hidden (class `rv`, opacity 0, only applied when JS has run) and is animated with the Web Animations API from opacity 0 and translateY 14px (its existing transform preserved) to its rest state. Each takes 1000 ms with `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`, staggered 80 ms + 60 ms × order. The order is logo, tagline, nav, left label, right label, vertical label, ghost, shadow, dots, index, scroll hint. The ghost word is the exception: 1400 ms rising from 40px, starting at 150 ms. When each animation finishes, remove `rv` and cancel the animation so later inline styles (dot fade, shadow move) take over.
- The ring rises in at the same time, starting 300 ms after load and taking 1.6 s overall. Each piece's progress is `clamp((entered·1600 − (1 − cos θ)·260)/1000)` with ease-out cubic, so the front pieces arrive first and the back pieces a little later. Each piece moves up 36 design px into place, scales from 0.95 to 1, and fades from 0 to 1.

## 11. Add to bag

- Clicking "ADD TO BAG →" takes the opened piece's on-screen rectangle and the bag button's rectangle. It creates a fixed-position copy (`.fly`, z-index 1000, no pointer events) of the same size with the same sheet crop and colour, the `#clean` filter plus `drop-shadow(0 10px 14px rgba(90,70,60,.18))`.
- The copy flies along a quadratic Bézier from the piece's top-left to the point that centres it on the bag. The control point is at x = start + 0.62·(end − start), y = max(0, min(startY, endY) − 0.12·height). The path is sampled into 25 keyframes. The scale rises to 1.06 over the first 12% (sine), then shrinks to `max(0.04, bagWidth·0.9/width)` with an exponent of 0.55, so it shrinks early. The rotation is `−14·sin(π·t)` degrees, and the opacity drops by 60% over the last 10%. Duration 950 ms, easing `cubic-bezier(.45,0,.25,1)`.
- On landing: remove the copy and increment the count. The badge (a 17px-tall pill at the bag's top-right, −5px offsets, `--ink` background, `--bg` text, 9.5px weight 600) pops in from scale 0 with `cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)` .45s. The bag button wiggles (scale 1 → 1.28 with −8° → 0.94 with 4° → 1, 520 ms ease-out), the badge pulses (scale 1.45, 420 ms, 60 ms delay), and the bag's aria-label becomes "Bag, N item(s)".
- The button text changes to "ADDED TO BAG ✓" and goes back to "ADD TO BAG →" after 1.8 s. The garment in the product view stays where it is.
