# Maison Verrel — "The Rail" boutique hero: exact recreation prompt

Build a single-file, one-screen luxury fashion storefront hero called **Maison Verrel**. The whole screen is a calm warm-ivory studio. A thin gold clothing rail curves across the full width like a shallow smile, and twenty garments (tailored blazers, belted trench coats, silk slip dresses and a satin gown in ivory, champagne, black, oxblood and taupe) hang from it side-on on dark wooden hangers, each with a small cream price tag. The rail scrolls sideways with inertia and the clothes swing on their hooks. Hovering a piece turns it to face you. Clicking it opens a full-screen quick-view with a size picker and an Add to cart button. Adding to cart shrinks the garment into the bag icon in the nav, and the bag opens a cart drawer that slides in from the right. Everything below is the exact specification: reproduce it pixel for pixel.

Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file. No frameworks, no libraries, no build step. The page never scrolls vertically (`overflow: hidden` on html and body); the rail is the only thing that moves sideways.

## 4. Interactions (exact behaviour)

### 4.1 Load sequence (runs once)
The `html.is-loading` guard hides the garments, headline words and footer until fonts plus the side and front sheets are ready. A failsafe starts the intro anyway after 2.5 s. When the intro starts, remove the class and run Web Animations:

| Element | From → to | Duration | Delay | Easing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Garment `.drop` i (0–19) | translateY(−42u), opacity 0, blur(6px) → none, 1, blur(0) | 620 ms | i × 70 ms | cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1), fill backwards |
| Garment swing impulse | add ±1.6 to the sway velocity, alternating sign by index | — | i × 70 + 420 ms | spring (see 4.2) |
| Headline word j (0–3) | blur(12px), opacity 0, translateY(6u) → sharp, 1, 0 | 820 ms | 60 + j × 110 ms | cubic-bezier(.25,.8,.3,1) |
| Footer left / progress / footer right | opacity 0 → 1 | 420 ms | 600 / 680 / 760 ms | ease-out |

The rail, nav, utility bar and eyebrow are visible from the first frame. So the garments drop onto their hooks one by one from left to right, each with a little pendulum swing, while the headline sharpens word by word out of a blur.

### 4.2 Rail scroll, inertia and sway (one requestAnimationFrame loop)
- State in px: `target`, `cur`, `vel`. `maxScroll = max(0, (2·start + 19·gap)·u − pageWidth)`, and `target` is clamped to [0, maxScroll].
- Every frame (dt = elapsed / 16.667, capped at 3): `cur += (target − cur) · (1 − (1 − 0.085)^dt)`, and `vel = Δcur / dt`.
- **Wheel** anywhere, when the quick-view is closed: `preventDefault()` and add the dominant of deltaX or deltaY × 0.9 to target.
- **Drag** (pointer on the rail zone): it counts as a drag once the pointer moves more than 6 px. While dragging, `target = startTarget − dx × 1.15`, and hover is cleared. On release, fling with `target −= releaseVelocity(px/ms) × 260`. A click that followed a drag is ignored.
- **Keys:** ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move one gap. Escape closes the quick-view, or the cart if the quick-view is shut.
- **Sway** (per piece, a damped spring, skipped when reduced motion is on): target angle = clamp(−vel × 0.22, −7°, 7°); `av += (target − a) · 0.05 · dt; av *= 0.88^dt; a += av · dt`; apply `rotate(a deg)` on `.sway` around the hook. Fast scrolling makes the clothes swing against the direction of travel, and they settle when the rail stops.
- **Progress thumb:** `left = (cur / maxScroll) × 42%`.

### 4.3 Hover: turn to face (mouse only)
- Entering a hit area with a mouse pointer (not while dragging or adding to cart) gives `.g` the class `hov` and raises it to z-index 5.
- **Lift:** `.lift` goes to `translateY(12u) scale(1.2)` over 0.42 s, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). It scales from the hook, so the garment grows and drops slightly.
- **Turn:** the side face rotates Y 0 → −90° in 0.15 s (cubic-bezier(.5,0,1,1)). Then the front face rotates Y 90° → 0 in 0.15 s with a 0.15 s delay (cubic-bezier(0,0,.3,1)). On leave it plays in reverse, front out first, then side back in after 0.15 s. Both faces use `backface-visibility: hidden` and `transform-origin: 50% 0`.
- **Neighbours make room:** each piece eases (factor 0.16 per frame) towards an offset of sign(d) × [0, 50, 24, 9, 0][min(|d|, 4)] × (gs/0.48)u, where d = its index − the hovered index.
- **Label:** the hint fades up and out (opacity 0, translateY −6u, 0.3 s), and the name/price label fades in from translateY 6u.
- **Touch** (`hover: none`): the hint reads "Tap a piece · tap again to look closer". The first tap does the hover turn and the second tap opens the quick-view.

### 4.4 Click: quick-view
- `body.qv-open` fades `.stage` to opacity 0 with blur(8px) over 0.45 s, and disables pointer events on it.
- **Image:** a `.qv-img` layer holds a front face and a back face of the piece. On desktop they are painted at scale 0.9u, with the hook at x 440u and y 62u. A 1.5 px rod in `#3B3631` hangs from the top of the screen down to the hook. It fades in after 0.45 s.
- **Fly-in:** the image animates from the garment's current position and size on the rail (the front face if it was hovered, otherwise the side face) to its place. Use a translate plus a scale from origin 0 0, with the scale set by the height ratio, opacity 0.6 → 1, over 700 ms, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Hide the rail copy while the quick-view is open. Cancel any running animation on the layer before starting, and use a token so a close that finishes late can never clear a newer open.
- **Info column** (left 972u, width 430u, vertically centred with translate −42%), every item fading up 10u with a stagger of 0.28 s + j × 0.045 s:
  1. Counter "i / 20": Inter 12, tracking 0.12em, colour `#8A7F72`.

  3. Price "$690.00": Inter 600 15.5.
  4. Tabs "Front" and "Back": Inter 15, gap 32, inactive `#8A7F72`, active ink with a 2 px underline and bottom padding 6. Switching crossfades the two faces over 0.25 s, but only once that sheet has loaded.
  5. "SIZE": Inter 11, tracking 0.14em, muted.
  6. Size pills S, M, L, XL: 52 × 44, fully rounded, border 1.5 px `#DDD5C9`, Inter 500 14. The selected one is filled `#0E0D0C` with white text. S is selected by default.
  7. "Add to cart": full width, 58 tall, fully rounded, `#0E0D0C`, white Inter 600 16.

### 4.5 Add to cart: fly into the bag
1. The button turns `#8D8780` and shows a 16u white spinner (0.7 s linear rotation) and the text "Adding…" for 1000 ms.
2. Clone the face that is currently showing (front or back) as a fixed element on top of everything at its exact on-screen rectangle. Close the quick-view without the return flight: the piece reappears on its hook with a small drop (translateY −24u → 0, opacity 0 → 1, 520 ms, delay 260 ms) and a sway nudge of +1.4.

# HINA — Little Wardrobe: interactive garment-rail hero

Build a single-page, full-screen hero for a fictional children's clothing label called **HINA**. The page is one quiet studio wall with a steep diagonal clothes rail running from the top-left corner down towards the centre-right. Twelve small garments hang on it; the first one hangs large at the front-left, the other eleven hang behind it on the rail at full width, each one tucked behind the piece in front so that only its right-hand side shows, and they get smaller as they recede. A thin, very airy info column sits on the right. Visitors browse the rail (wheel, arrow keys, arrow buttons, swipe), hover a piece on the rail to see it pulled out like someone lifting a hanger to look at it, click a rail piece to bring it to the front, and click the front piece to open a detail view in which the rest of the rail closes up into a soft blurred stack behind it while a detail panel with three photo tabs slides in. Everything must feel calm, soft and premium — pastel, thin type, very wide letter-spacing, slow eased motion. Use a single HTML file with inline CSS and inline JavaScript, no frameworks, no build step.

## 4. Background wall

The effect is a soft lilac-grey studio wall that is slightly darker on the left and lightest just right of centre. There are no props, no floor and no other scenery.

## 5. Scaling system

All hero content (rail, garments and info UI) lives in one fixed **1440 × 900 px frame**, absolutely positioned at 50 % / 50 % of a fixed full-viewport stage with transform-origin top-left. Every coordinate in this brief is in frame pixels. On screens wider than 820 px the frame is scaled by `min(max(vw/1440, vh/900), vh/870, vw/1380)` and translated by −720 × scale and −450 × scale, so it covers the viewport but never crops the UI at the edges on unusual aspect ratios. The nav is not inside the frame: it is pinned to the viewport edges with its own unit `--ns` = max(0.62, min(1, vw/1440)), by which its font size, offsets, gaps and the burger width are all multiplied. Recompute both on resize.

## 7. The rail (inside the frame)

**Rail line.** The rail is a straight line through frame space with y = 5 + 0.641 × (x − 330). Draw it as an SVG polygon in a 1440 × 900 viewBox, behind the garments: a tapered tube from x = 250 to x = 1062, 18 px thick at the left end (railY − 9 to railY + 9) narrowing to about 5.4 px at the right end (railY − 2.6 to railY + 2.8, with the bottom-right corner at x 1065). Fill it with a vertical gradient #FFFFFF → #F3F1F5 (55 %) → #C9C5D0, so it reads as a white powder-coated tube catching light from above. It runs off the top-left corner of the frame.

**Garment elements.** Create twelve absolutely positioned divs, one per piece, each sized to its sprite box (w × h), with the garment sheet as a non-repeating background at its native size (3312 × 2480 px) shifted by (−x, −y). Set each element's transform-origin to (hookX − x, 0), i.e. the top of its hook, so every scale and rotation pivots on the hook. Transitions on each piece: transform 0.55 s with the main easing curve, opacity 0.35 s ease, filter 0.55 s ease. Pieces never receive pointer events; all hit-testing is done mathematically (section 10).

**Slots.** The piece currently shown is "cur"; each piece's slot is (index − cur) mod 12, so slot 0 is the front and slots 1–11 run back along the rail. The hook x of each slot is: 352, 440, 505, 565, 620, 670, 716, 758, 796, 831, 863, 893. Fractional and negative slots interpolate linearly (a negative slot is 352 + slot × 120). The z-index is 100 − slot, so nearer pieces cover farther ones.

**Scale.** The front piece is drawn at scale 0.93. A piece behind is scaled by the hook x through this piecewise-linear table: 352 → 0.94, 435 → 0.905, 545 → 0.83, 670 → 0.70, 778 → 0.57, 878 → 0.445, 958 → 0.33, 1045 → 0.19. Scaling is uniform: never squash or skew a garment horizontally.

**Placement.** For a piece at slot j with hook x X and scale S: translate it to (X − (hookX − x) + dx, railY(X) − 9 × S + dy), then rotate(rot), then scale(S). dx, dy and rot are 0 except during the hover pull-out. The hook therefore sits just on top of the rail, and each garment hangs at full width from it. Because the pieces are drawn at full width and overlap, the viewer sees the whole front piece (its left sleeve near x 100 and its hem around y 700) and only the right-hand sides and hems of the pieces behind, getting smaller up to about x 1000. Their hems may hang slightly below the front piece's hem.

**Floor shadow.** A 600 × 60 px ellipse (radial gradient rgba(70,60,90,.14) fading to transparent) placed behind all pieces at x 52 and y = railY(352) + frontSpriteHeight × 0.93 − 26, so it sits under the front garment's hem.

## 10. Interactions

**Browsing (next).** Triggered by a mouse wheel (deltaY + deltaX accumulated; one step each time the total passes ±40, desktop only, and the page's own scrolling is prevented), the Right or Down arrow keys, the right pager arrow, or a left swipe of more than 36 px on touch. Steps are throttled to one every 95 ms, so a fast wheel flick runs through several pieces quickly, like flicking hangers. On a step forward:
- the front piece moves to slot −1.3 (back up the rail to the upper left, about 156 px left of the front hook) and fades to opacity 0, using its normal transitions;
- every other piece moves one slot forward with the 0.55 s eased transform, growing as it comes forward, and the new front piece lands at scale 0.93;
- after 360 ms the old front piece is jumped, with transitions switched off for one frame, to the last slot at the far end of the rail, then fades back in there;
- the hover pull-out is cleared.

**Browsing (previous).** Left or Up arrow keys, the left pager arrow, or a right swipe. The piece in the last slot is jumped invisibly to slot −1.3 with a z-index above everything, then on the next frame everything is laid out again: that piece slides down the rail into the front slot while fading in, and the others step back one slot.

**Text swap.** On every step all changing texts (counter, both title lines, both description lines, the three spec values, the pager counter) fade out with a 5 px downward shift (opacity 0.22 s, transform 0.32 s eased). After 140 ms they are replaced and fade back up. The left index number and the index fill update at the same time.

**Hover pull-out (mouse only).** Track mousemove over the stage and convert the pointer into frame coordinates (subtract the frame's on-screen left/top and divide by the frame scale). For each piece compute its span: left = hookX − (hookX − x) × S, right = hookX + (x + w − hookX) × S, top = railY(hookX) − 9 × S, bottom = top + h × S. The pointer is on the front piece if it lies between its left + 30 and right − 20 and between its top + 60 and bottom. Otherwise walk the slots from 1 to 11 and take the first piece whose right − 6 is at or past the pointer's x; that piece is hovered only if the pointer is between its top + 40 and bottom − 10 and to the right of the front piece's right − 20. The hovered rail piece is drawn pulled out: dx = 38 × S, dy = +6 px, rotate −6° (its hem swings out to the right around the hook) and scale × 1.035. Every piece behind it shifts right by 18 × its scale to make room, and the pieces in front stay still. All of this animates with the normal 0.55 s eased transitions, and moving off the pieces (or leaving the stage) settles everything back. The cursor becomes a pointer over the front piece or a hoverable rail piece. Nothing happens while the detail view is open, or on devices without hover.

**Click a rail piece ("click again to follow").** Show the pull-out on that piece (this is what a tap shows on touch screens), then after 260 ms step forward as many times as its slot number, 120 ms apart, so the rail runs and that piece arrives at the front.

**Click the front piece, or VIEW DETAILS: the detail view.** Add the class `detail` to the body. For 0.76 s every piece uses slower transitions (transform 0.7 s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.25,1), opacity 0.55 s, filter 0.55 s), then goes back to normal.
- The front piece does not move.
- The rail closes up behind it. Every piece behind is re-placed with its rail x compressed to 352 + (x − 352) × 0.36, scaled for that new x, and drawn at opacity 0.62 with filter blur(7px) saturate(.55) brightness(1.04). The result is a soft, blurred, faded wedge of garments hugging the right side of the front piece and receding up along the rail. Nothing flies away or disappears.
- The rail tube is clipped from the right (clip-path inset(0 46% 0 0), 0.7 s same curve), so it ends just behind the wedge.
- The info column and the pager slide 328 px left (0.75 s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.2,1)), and the pager widens to 596 px so its arrows sit at x 790 and about 1386 with the counter centred between them.
- After a 0.32 s delay the detail panel fades in from 46 px to the right (opacity 0.45 s ease, transform 0.7 s eased).
- Clicking the front piece again, the BACK TO COLLECTION button or pressing Escape reverses all of it. Browsing still works while the detail view is open: the front piece changes and the stack stays blurred.

## 8. Motion (measured frame by frame from the reference; reproduce exactly)

Add a js class to html immediately. Elements marked hidden-until-animated (both navs, rays, CTAs, avatars, hero copy, video card, side cards, collage word, both paragraphs, LEVEL UP tag) start at opacity 0 only when that class is present. A 6 s failsafe timer shows them all if the intro never starts. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, show everything at once in its final state and skip all motion.

Helpers. Fade = Web Animations opacity 0 → 1, fill both, default easing cubic-bezier(.25,.6,.3,1). Strip reveal = a CSS mask on the element: repeating-linear-gradient(180deg, black 0 to a px, transparent a px to P px) where P is the band pitch and a = max(0.6, f × P) grows from 0 to P, so every band grows downward from its own top edge; mask-position-y = phase mod P; f follows the given curve via requestAnimationFrame; remove the mask at the end. Letter wipe = each letter animates clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) → inset(0 0 0 0) and opacity 0.35 → 1 over 110 ms, easing cubic-bezier(.3,.6,.4,1), letters started one after another at a fixed step; letters start clipped and invisible.

| 1020 ms | 620 ms | Athlete slides from translateY(−236u) to 0, no scaling, to the chest-up framing | cubic-bezier(.3,0,.15,1) |
| 1100 ms | 600 ms | Rays fade in | default |
| 1130 ms | 550 ms | Video card fades in | default |
| 1240 ms | 350 ms | Avatars and body copy fade in | default |
| 1370 ms | 500 ms | CTA pills fade in | default |
| 1540 ms | 18 ms step | Headline line 1 letter wipe | as above |

| line 2 end + 150 ms | — | Once only: hide the letters of WORKOUT! from the end back to "WOR" at 45 ms each, hold 450 ms, show them again at 50 ms each | visibility toggles |

Smooth scrolling (wheel only; touch, keys and the scrollbar stay native): intercept wheel events (non-passive, ignore ctrl+wheel), add deltaY to a target clamped to the scrollable range (line mode × 40, page mode × viewport height) and each animation frame move the current position toward the target by 1 − 0.9^(dt / 16.67), scrollTo it, and stop within 0.5 px. The hero simply scrolls away; nothing scales or rises on its own.

Collage trigger: when the collage top is above 18% of the viewport height (and its bottom below 30%), or the whole section is on screen: the centre photo layer (hidden until now, so the empty gradient card shows while scrolling in) strips in over 470 ms, pitch 40u, phase 0, cubic-bezier(.3,0,.2,1); at the same moment the side cards, outlined word and both paragraphs fade in over 500 ms with cubic-bezier(.45,0,.35,1). Runs once.

Marquee rows, every frame: d = −(marquee section top) × 0.45 + drift. With w = one repetition's width (row scrollWidth / 6) and o = −6u, row 1 is translated by mod(d, w) − w + o and row 2 by o − mod(d, w), using translate3d. Scrolling down moves row 1 right and row 2 left; when the section is settled at the top of the viewport "FRESH" and "YOUR" start at the left edge.

Marquee trigger: when the section top is above 15% of the viewport (bottom below 40%), or the whole section is on screen: LEVEL UP fades in over 150 ms, title line 1 wipes from 150 ms at 18 ms per letter and line 2 from 180 ms at 40 ms per letter. 400 ms after the title finishes, the rows begin drifting (drift grows by 0.05u per ms) and the look cycle starts: every 1270 ms the next look is raised above the current one, made visible and strip-revealed over 200 ms (pitch 34u, phase 0, cubic-bezier(.3,0,.3,1)), then the previous look is hidden; it loops 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 1 forever.

# Krung Travel — "Welcome to Bangkok" cinematic travel booking landing page

Build a single-file, full-bleed, fully responsive travel booking landing page for an invented brand **"Krung Travel"** (Bangkok, Thailand). It has a cinematic three-slide hero with giant gradient-faded titles, drifting volumetric clouds, a soft misty right-to-left wipe between slides, a column of round destination thumbnails on thin concentric rings, a white search bar with working date-range and guest popovers, a "Recomended Places to Stay" grid of eight photo cards, and a shared-element transition from a card to a property detail page with booking. The whole palette is warm sunset peach and mauve. Every visual must match this description exactly.

### 4.4 Slide transition: soft misty right-to-left wipe (the signature move)

Clicking a thumbnail switches slides; otherwise slides auto-advance 1 → 2 → 3 → 1 every 5.2 s. The wipe lasts 1.25 s with easeInOutCubic and is driven by requestAnimationFrame.

- **Incoming slide:** placed above the outgoing one and revealed by a moving linear-gradient mask (to the left) with a soft edge about 35% wide. With progress `p`:
  - fully opaque up to `p·135 − 35` % from the right edge;
  - 60% at the midpoint;
  - transparent at `p·135` %.

  The photo and the giant title wipe together, so mid-transition you read hybrids like "FIND PLACE TO BANGKOK".
- **Incoming photo:** settles from scale 1.12 to 1.04 while sliding from +2% to 0.
- **Outgoing photo:** pushes from scale 1.04 to 1.09 and drifts −2%.
- **Mist band:** a vertical band 34% of the viewport width rides along the wipe edge, a radial blush-white haze (`rgba(255,236,226,.75)` → transparent) blurred 10 px. Its opacity follows sin(π·t) up to .95, so the edge looks like a cloud passing.
- **Rail:** when the wipe starts, the rail re-lays out, and the connector and caption hide. After 650 ms the connector and bar grow back and the new caption text clips in.
- **After the wipe:** the live photo does a very slow Ken Burns. Scale grows 0.0035 per second for up to 12 s, plus a pointer parallax shift of ±0.6% horizontally and ±0.5% vertically.

### 4.5 Intro (on load)

- After 250 ms, each title word rises from below its mask (translateY 105% → 0, 1.15 s `--out`), staggered by 90 ms.
- The thumbnails scale from 0 to 1, staggered 140 ms from a .35 s start.
- The rings fade in.
- The search bar slides up 30 px while fading in over 1 s.
- The caption reveals after 900 ms.

| Element | Movement |
|---|---|
| Slide stack | translateY(+0.42 × scrollY), so the photo lags |
| Bottom cloud bank | translateY(−0.38 × scrollY), scale 1 + 0.35 × scrollY / viewport height, so clouds rise and swell past the photo |
| Top cloud layer | fades in |
| Rail | translateY(+0.2 × scrollY), fades out by half a viewport |

## 7. The garment swap (exact timeline, 1200 ms in total)

A swap to target product T, from current product A, runs these steps. The two worn jackets cross-dissolve; the base plate (black tee) never shows during a swap.

| Time (ms) | What happens | Easing |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Layer order: wear plate A gets z-index 1 and stays fully opaque; wear plate T gets z-index 2 and class "on" (its animation holds it at opacity 0 until its delay ends) | — |
| 100–350 | Old title span and old price span translate from Y 0 to −105% inside their masks. They are set absolute (top-left) as soon as the swap starts and removed when done | cubic-bezier(.55,0,.8,.3) |
| 100–300 | Every rail packshot except the flyer fades to 0 | linear |
| 60–1010 | Glide: T's packshot is moved out of the rail into the hero itself (its own layer, so the rail refill cannot cut the flight short). It translates from its rail slot to the torso while scaling up, one transform animation of 950 ms. The end transform puts its box centre at (ox + 1012·ps, oy + 710·ps), scaled by k = (0.86 · 600 · ps)/(760 · s), so it lands slightly smaller and lower than the worn jacket and never covers the face. Transform-origin is the centre, z-index 4 | cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.3,1): fast start, long soft landing |
| 60–1070 | Flyer opacity, a separate 1010 ms animation with keyframes 1 → 1 at 0.45 → 0.6 at 0.72 → 0. It is removed when this finishes. If the packshot was not in the rail (going backwards), it is created at slot 0 and its keyframes start at 0, reaching 1 at 0.18 | ease-in-out |
| 350–800 | New title and new price spans translate from Y 105% to 0 inside their masks | cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) |
| 420–1180 | Wear plate T fades from opacity 0 to 1 on top of A. When it finishes, A loses class "on" | cubic-bezier(.45,0,.25,1) |
| 600 | The rail is rebuilt with T+1 in slot 0 and T+2 in slot 1. Each new packshot enters from 45u to the right of its slot at opacity 0, reaching its slot at opacity 1 over 350 ms. The active pagination dash moves to T. The cart pill's thumbnail, name, sub-label and price fade to 0 over 150 ms, are swapped, then fade back to 1 | cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) |
| 1200 | The swap is complete. If another swap was requested during this one, it runs now; otherwise the autoplay timer restarts | — |

The motion copies the reference video: the next jacket travels from the rail and settles softly onto the model while the worn jacket changes underneath it, and the title rolls up behind a mask.

## 8. Triggers, scroll and autoplay

- Autoplay loop: after the loading reveal (at 600 ms), schedule the next product (active+1, wrapping 3 to 0) after a 2000 ms hold. Each swap restarts the hold when it finishes, so the jackets cycle about every 3.2 s forever.
- Scroll (desktop): listen for wheel events on the window with passive false and call preventDefault (the page never scrolls). Scrolling down goes to the next jacket and scrolling up to the previous one. Every scroll counts:
  - Convert the delta to pixels: deltaMode 1 × 16, deltaMode 2 × the viewport height.
  - Add it to an accumulator, which resets when the direction changes or after 250 ms without wheel events.
  - When the accumulator reaches ±50 px and at least 140 ms have passed since the last step, take one step in that direction and reset the accumulator. One mouse-wheel notch (100 px) is therefore always one jacket, and the 140 ms gap stops trackpad momentum from racing through the rail.
- Stepping: step(dir) moves one jacket from wherever the page is heading. If a swap is running, the base is the queued target rather than the current one. A request made during a running swap replaces the queue with that target (or clears it if the target equals the current jacket), and runs when the swap finishes. Rapid scrolls therefore all register: five quick notches down land five jackets along.
- Touch: a pointer movement of more than 40 px on release counts as a swipe. A mainly horizontal swipe goes next (left) or previous (right). A mainly vertical touch swipe goes next (finger up, like scrolling down) or previous (finger down). The hero has touch-action: none.
- Click a rail packshot: swap to that product. Clicks that end a drag are ignored.
- Keys: ArrowRight, ArrowDown and PageDown go next. ArrowLeft, ArrowUp and PageUp go back.
- User control: any scroll, swipe, drag, key press or rail click sets a 6000 ms user hold. Autoplay waits until 6 s after the last user input before moving on, so it never undoes a scroll back.
- Pausing the loop (the visitor can stop it):
  - While a mouse pointer is over a packshot, the cart pill or the Shop Now button. It resumes when the pointer leaves those elements or leaves the window.
  - While a pointer is pressed on the hero (dragging or touching).
  - While the tab is hidden, using visibilitychange.

# Noa Ellsworth: a botanist made of 66,000 dots

Build a single-page, full-screen portfolio hero: a dark moss-black room where the head-and-shoulders bust of a fictional botanist, Noa Ellsworth, is drawn entirely from about 66,000 soft glowing dots in WebGL (three.js). Her hair is gathered into a loose bun with a small sprig of leaves tucked into its right side, a few wavy strands hang beside her cheeks and neck, she wears a linen shirt with an open pointed collar, and across her eyes sits a single wraparound visor, also made of dots, with a faint sage-tinted lens. Her face is smooth and featureless, like a clay sculpture: the likeness lives in the silhouette, the hair, the leaves and the visor, never in eyes or a mouth.

The page opens on a ring-shaped loader whose number is the real download of the 3D model. At 100 every dot leaves the ring and arcs forward into place, so you watch her assemble herself. As the last dots land, one diagonal band of light sweeps down the bust once. From then on the visitor's cursor is a small light: it lights whatever part of her it is near, and her head turns gently to look at it. Every few seconds a sage glint runs across the visor and then across the leaves. Faint dust drifts upward through the whole room and a fine film grain sits over everything. The mood is calm, quiet and premium; nothing is busy, nothing reacts loudly.

**Pill.** "How this page was made →": position fixed, bottom 20 px, left 20 px, z-index 7, background #fff, colour #111, Geist Mono 12 px, letter-spacing 0.04em, padding 8 px 12 px, border-radius 6 px, no underline, box-shadow of a 1 px #1111111a ring plus 0 10px 24px −12px #0006. It plays one animation from 4 s: 0.6 s, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), fill both, keyframe 0% at opacity 0 and translateY 8 px (so it fades up into place).

## 5. Mobile layout

At max-width 700 px: the name and tagline drop to 16 px, move to top 72 px, start at translate 0 10 px and end at translate 0 (so they sit side by side near the top: name on the left, tagline on the right); the hint moves to bottom 60 px.

At max-width 600 px: the pill shrinks to padding 6 px 9 px and 11 px text, sits at bottom 12 px, and moves to the right (left auto, right 12 px).

The canvas and loader stay full screen; the camera fit below keeps the whole bust visible on narrow screens.

## 6. Building the dots from the model

After the download and parse, take the first mesh in the scene, clone its geometry with the mesh's world matrix applied, and compute vertex normals if missing. Build a three.js MeshSurfaceSampler on it.

**Candidates.** Sample 330,000 candidate points (5 × 66,000) with their normals, in model units.

**Even density (so the hair doesn't swallow every dot).** Put every candidate in a 3D voxel grid of 0.022 model units. Find the smallest per-voxel cap such that the sum over voxels of min(count, cap) reaches 1.8 × the number of bust dots needed. Keep at most cap candidates per voxel (in sampling order), shuffle that pool, and take as many as needed. The 1.8 headroom keeps some extra density in the hair so it keeps its texture.

**The leaf sprig (part 2).** A candidate is a leaf when x > 0.13, y > 0.6 and (x − 0.02)² + (z + 0.06)² > 0.035 (model units). Leaf candidates skip the voxel cap: keep the first 60% of them, so the sprig is denser than its area alone would give it, the way the original draws its glasses.

**The visor (parts 3 and 4).** Drawn as its own dots, as one rigid curved shape fitted to the face:
- Build a front height map of the face: for candidates whose normal z ≥ 0.2 and that lie within x −0.32…0.32 and y 0.2…0.45, keep the highest z per 0.01 × 0.01 cell. The face height at (x, y) is the maximum over the 3 × 3 neighbouring cells.
- Half-width W = 0.215. Clearance 0.028. Top edge: y = 0.378 − 0.022 (x / W)². Lower edge: y = 0.282 + 0.032 exp(−(x / 0.034)²) + 0.026 (x / W)⁴. The Gaussian term is a notch over the nose; the fourth-power term tapers the ends.
- The lens depth is one smooth curve, z = front − wrap × x². "front" is the highest face height over x −0.06…0.06 and y 0.30…0.36, plus the clearance. "wrap" is the smallest value of (front − need − 0.7 × clearance) / x² over x from −W to W in 0.01 steps (skipping |x| < 0.05), where "need" is the highest face height between the lower and top edges at that x. Fall back to 2.4 if the fit fails. Each dot's normal is (2·wrap·x, 0, 1) normalised.
- Dots, each with a small random jitter: 950 along the top bar (x uniform across −W…W, y = top edge minus a random amount weighted toward the edge, up to 0.016; pushed 0.004 forward); 380 along the lower edge (pushed 0.002 forward); 70 at each end, filling between the two edges at x = ±W; 1,500 lens dots filling the area between the edges (part 4); and 70 per side for the arms, running from each end 0.03 outward and 0.15 back along z, 0.008 below the top edge. Frame dots are part 3; lens dots are part 4.

**Placement.** Every dot is moved into world space by x × 2.8, y × 2.8 − 0.68, z × 2.8. That puts the top of the bun near the top edge of a 1440 × 900 view and lets the bottom edge crop the shoulders.

**Total.** Exactly 66,000 dots: the visor dots, the kept leaf dots, and the voxel-thinned bust dots fill the rest. Every dot also gets aRand, a uniform random number from 0 to 1.

**Depth values (aShade).** For every final dot, look at the candidates within radius R = 0.03 (model units), using the first half of the candidates in a hash grid of cell size R.
- The ridge value is −(the average neighbour offset · the dot's normal) / R. Positive means the dot stands proud of its neighbours (bun twists, leaf edges, collar points); negative means it sits in a crease. Divide by the 90th percentile of its absolute value and clamp to −1…1.
- The thin value is 1 − neighbourCount / (0.55 × the median count), clamped to 0…1. It is high for loose strands and leaf tips.

Store both as a two-component attribute. Also record the smallest and largest world x of all non-bust dots (parts 2–4); these bound the glint sweep.

## 7. Scene, camera and renderer

Use a WebGLRenderer with antialias off and powerPreference high-performance, pixel ratio min(devicePixelRatio, 2) (called dpr below), clear colour #0f110d. Use a PerspectiveCamera with fov 30, near 0.1 and far 100, looking at the target (0, −0.15, 0).

On every resize: the camera distance is max(2.35 / tan 15°, 1.7 / (tan 15° × aspect)). Put the camera at (0, −0.15, distance) looking at the target, so the view is always 4.7 units tall, or wider when the screen is narrow. One CSS pixel at the bust's depth is 2 × distance × tan 15° / height world units. The loader ring's world radius is 92 of those pixels and its centre is (0, −0.15, 0), so the WebGL ring lines up exactly with the SVG ring.

There are three Points objects, all with transparent true, depthWrite false and additive blending, and all with frustum culling off.

**1. The bust (uniforms).**

| Uniform | Value |
|---|---|
| uTime | Seconds since start |
| uAssemble | 0 to 1 |
| uSize | 26 × dpr |
| uGlint | Glint x position; −9 when off |
| uShine | Shine band position; 99 when off |
| uHead | 2D head turn |
| uLight | Cursor light position, starting at (−1.4, 1.2, 1.6) |
| uRingCenter, uRingRadius | Set by the resize |
| uInk | #c9d4b8 |
| uBlue | #7fa8a3 |
| uCream | #f0e5c8 |

**2. The cursor light.** One point with a light shader: point size 240 × dpr × uOn / depth. Its fragment is a white core, smoothstep(0.14, 0.08, r), plus a glow, exp(−4r) × 0.45 + exp(−12r) × 0.7, where r is twice the distance from the sprite centre.

**3. The dust.** 900 points spread over x −9…9, y −6…6 and z −6…2. Each rises at 0.03 + aRand × 0.05 units per second, wrapping y through a 12-unit range. Each sways in x by sin(t × 0.2 + aRand × 40) × 0.15. Point size is 22 × dpr × (0.5 + aRand) / depth. Brightness is (0.1 + aRand × 0.18) × uOn in the bust's ink colour, with the same Gaussian falloff as the bust dots.

## 8. The bust's vertex shader, step by step

1. **Head turn.** head = smoothstep(−1.3, −0.6, y). The rotation is rotY(uHead.x × (0.25 + 0.75 × head)) times rotX(uHead.y × head), applied about the pivot (0, −1, 0) to both the position and the normal. The head turns fully and the shoulders follow at 25%.
2. **Breathing.** Each dot moves along its normal by sin(uTime × 1.4 + aRand × 60) × 0.006.
3. **Entrance.**
   - r2 = fract(sin(aRand × 91.7) × 43758.5453).
   - Per-dot progress: t = clamp((uAssemble − aRand × 0.45) / 0.55, 0, 1). Each dot starts after a delay of up to 0.45 and takes 0.55 of the assemble time.
   - Ease in-out cubic: e = 4t³ when t < 0.5, otherwise 1 − (−2t + 2)³ / 2.
   - Start point: on the ring at angle aRand × 2π, radius uRingRadius × (1 + (r2 − 0.5) × 0.06), so the ring unwinds in the same order the SVG ring filled.
   - Position: mix(start, home, e), plus an arc toward the camera: (sin(aRand × 40 + uTime × 0.3), cos(aRand × 31), 0.9 + r2 × 1.4) × sin(e × π) × 0.45.
4. **Light terms.**
   - lit = max(n · toLight̂, 0) / (1 + |toLight|² × 0.32), where toLight is the cursor light's position minus the dot's world position.
   - key = max(n · normalize(−0.5, 0.6, 0.7), 0), a soft key from the top left.
   - facing = the view-space normal's z.
   - rim = (1 − |facing|)³.
5. **Brightness.**
   - Start with b = 0.3 + key × 0.22 + lit × 1.5 + rim × 0.14. It's mostly an even tone, like a scan.
   - Multiply by mix(0.55, 1, smoothstep(−0.3, 0.25, facing)), so the far side of the head is a little darker.
6. **Depth.**
   - Multiply b by 1 + ridge × 0.7 when ridge > 0, otherwise 1 + ridge × 0.5.
   - Add thin × (0.26 + key × 0.3).
7. **Parts.** Leaf dots × 0.9. Visor frame and lens dots × 0.78. Lens dots a further × 0.7. Then every dot × (0.7 + r2 × 0.5), so no two dots are alike.
8. **Glint.** Only leaf and visor dots: glint = smoothstep(0.09, 0, |x − uGlint|), measured on the dot's home x. Add glint × 1.2 to b.
9. **Shine.** band = y − x × 0.5 − uShine, measured on the turned home position. shine = exp(−band² × 4). Add shine × 1.3 to b.
10. **Alpha.** mix(0.75, 1, e).
11. **Size.** uSize × (0.45 + r2² × 1.3) × (1 + shine × 0.6) / view depth. Most dots are small, a few up to about three times larger, and dots swell slightly as the shine passes.

**Fragment.**
- Discard outside radius 0.5.
- Alpha is exp(−16 r²) × the vertex alpha, a soft Gaussian like a lens rather than a hard pixel.
- The ink starts at #c9d4b8, mixed toward cream #f0e5c8 by shine × 0.6, then toward sage #7fa8a3 by 0.6 on lens dots, then toward sage by glint × 0.7.
- The output colour is ink × brightness × alpha.

## 9. Timeline and interactions

| Time / trigger | What happens |
|---|---|
| Page load | Ring of 96 faint dots, counter "000", label "66,000 DOTS". Cursor is a crosshair. |
| While the GLB streams | Progress = bytes received / Content-Length (if no length: min(0.95, bytes / 1.5 MB)); ring dots light up clockwise from 12 o'clock, counter counts up. |
| Download done | Parse, build the dots, set progress to 1 ("100", ring full), hold 380 ms. |
| t = 0 (renderer starts) | uAssemble = min(1, t / 2.6): over 2.6 s every dot leaves the ring and arcs into place. Light sprite and dust fade in (light: uOn eases toward min(1, 1.6 × uAssemble) at rate 4; dust: toward 1 at rate 0.8, with ease = 1 − e^(−dt × rate)). |
| uAssemble > 0.55 (t ≈ 1.43 s) | data-phase becomes "ready": loader fades out (0.5 s after 0.15 s), cursor hides, logo fades to 0.9, name and tagline fade and rise 10 px over 0.9 s (tagline 0.12 s later), hint fades to 0.45 after 0.5 s. |
| t = 2.34 s → 4.54 s | The shine: s = (t − 2.34) / 2.2; uShine = 2.8 − (1 − (1 − s)²) × 7.4 (ease-out), so one diagonal band sweeps from above the bun down past the shoulders, once. |
| 4 s | The "How this page was made →" pill fades up. |
| t = 4.6 s, then every 4.2 s | The glint: over 0.9 s uGlint runs linearly from (smallest non-bust x − 0.15) to (largest non-bust x + 0.15), i.e. across the visor first and then across the leaves. Then it resets to −9. |
| Pointer move / pointer down | Pointer position in normalised device coordinates. A ray from the camera through it hits the plane z = 2.6; the light eases toward that point (rate 5), and the head eases toward (0.5 × x, 0.18 × y) (rate 3). uHead = (head.x, −head.y). |
| No pointer (or pointer left, or 1.5 s after the last touch) | The light orbits on its own at (1.9 sin(0.45 t), 0.5 + 0.8 cos(0.33 t), 2.6), and the head eases toward (0.35 sin(0.45 t), 0.12 cos(0.33 t)) at rate 1.5. |
| Frame step | dt is capped at 0.05 s. |

Easing for all of these "eases toward" is exponential smoothing: value += (target − value) × (1 − e^(−dt × rate)), or a lerp with that factor.

## 10. Reduced motion and errors

With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, there is no 380 ms hold, uAssemble starts at 1 (no entrance), uTime stays 0 (no breathing, no drifting dust), there is no shine and no glint, the head stays still, the light snaps to its target, the dust and light start fully on, CSS transitions on the loader, logo, name, tagline and hint are off, and the pill does not animate.

If the model fails to load, the counter shows "Could not load" and the label "Refresh to try again".

## 11. Acceptance checklist

- At 1440 × 900 the bun's top sits about 36 px from the top edge, the head is centred, the shoulders run off the bottom edge, the name is at left 58 px and the tagline at right 58 px, both vertically centred.
- The loader number climbs with the real download, the dots fly from the ring into the bust, the text appears around 1.4 s, the shine runs once around 2.3–4.5 s, the glint crosses the visor and leaves every 4.2 s.
- The cursor is hidden once ready; a soft glowing point follows it, the bust brightens near it, and the head turns toward it.
- The bun's twists, the leaf edges and the collar points catch light; the area under the bun and inside the collar falls into shadow; hanging strands glow softly.
- The visor reads as one wraparound piece with a brighter top bar, a finer lower edge with a nose notch, a faint sage lens and short arms; it turns with the head.
- At 375 px wide the name and tagline sit at the top, the pill is bottom-right, there is no sideways scroll.
- No console errors; exactly 66,000 bust dots.

# Glyph Animals — recreation brief

Build a single-file, full-screen browser "new tab" page: a near-black grid on which a flock of animals made entirely of keyboard characters travels across the screen, with a frosted liquid-glass species switcher at the top, a centred greeting with a round avatar, a large glass AI composer box, a "Tweaks" panel of live sliders, and a tiny "click to scatter" hint. Seven species can be switched: Moth, Rabbit, Sea turtle, Squid, Owl, Flying fish, Eagle. Every animal is drawn procedurally on a 2D canvas each frame; there are no images, sprites, videos or external assets of any kind apart from two web fonts. The whole thing is one HTML file with inline CSS and one inline script (no libraries, no build step).

## 1. Assets and fonts

There are no image or video assets. The only external resources are two Google Fonts, which in the delivered file are embedded as base64 WOFF2 data URIs (latin subset) so the page makes zero network requests.

## 6. The canvas renderer (the ASCII grid)

The canvas is sized to its CSS box times devicePixelRatio (capped at 2) and redrawn every frame. It is a grid of character cells:

- Cell width cw = clamp(round(viewport width ÷ 124 ÷ detail), 5, 24) px, cell height ch = round(cw × 1.45). "detail" is the per-species "ASCII detail" tuning (1.3 by default; 1.7 for Rabbit and Eagle). At 1440 wide and detail 1.3 the cells are 9 × 13 px.
- Background layer (cached on an offscreen canvas, repainted only on resize, grid change or hue change): fill rgb(6,7,12), then 1px grid lines on every cell boundary in rgba(255,255,255, 0.055 × grid), where "grid" is a tuning (1.05 default).
- Each frame: copy the background, draw the trail layer, then draw every non-empty cell. Text is drawn centred in its cell with font "600 round(ch × 0.74)px" + the canvas font family, textBaseline middle, at y + ch/2 + 1.
- Cell states: empty, stroke (glyph only) and solid (a filled rectangle inset 1px — x+1, y+1, cw−1, ch−1 — plus a glyph on top). Solid cells win over strokes.

How an animal becomes cells: every animal is an implicit shape function of local coordinates (u along its heading, v across it, both in units of its "span" in pixels). For each cell inside a square of ± extent × span around the animal, the function is probed at the cell centre and at four sub-points (fractions .25/.30, .75/.30, .25/.72, .75/.72 of the cell). It returns false (outside) or a colour plus a "kind" and optional glyph set. Coverage = hits ÷ 5.

- If the centre is outside or coverage < 0.6 it is an edge cell: a stroke whose glyph is picked from ":;" (coverage ≥ .5) or ".',`" and whose colour is the cell colour faded toward the background by fog + .55 − .45 × coverage.
- Otherwise the cell is solid, with a fill and a glyph colour that depend on the kind:

| Kind | Fill | Glyph colour | Default glyphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | colour (with fog) | 0.42 × fill | ".:;+=*%#" chosen by inverse luminance ± 1 jitter |
| Shine | same as Plain, but brightness × (1 − .4 × shimmer + shimmer × sin(2.2t + 9u + 6v + tilt + 2 × heading)) | 0.42 × fill | same ramp |
| Dark | colour | fill × 1.7 + (34,30,30) | "#%@" |
| Light | colour | 0.4 × fill | "o*" |
| Fur | colour | fill × 1.6 + (44,40,36) | "8#@" |
| Soft | colour faded by min(1, .62 + .38 × fog) | colour | ".:;+=*%#" |
| Bright | 0.58 × colour | colour × 1.05 + 50 | ".:*" |
| Line | no fill (stroke only, never over a solid) | colour | ".:+*" by luminance |

- Glyph choice is stable per animal: a hash of the animal id and the cell's rounded local position picks a character from the set, so patterns stick to the body as it moves instead of flickering.
- Every cell's brightness gets a tiny ±3% flicker that re-rolls 6 times a second. Sparkle: a per-cell hash re-rolled ~2.4 times a second turns the glyph pure white, light ice blue or pale cyan when below the "sparkle" tuning (full rate on Shine, a third on Plain, also on Soft and Bright).
- Depth fog: fog = (1 − depth) × "Distance fade" tuning; colours are mixed toward the background by that amount.
- Hue shift: all colours are passed through a standard luminance-preserving hue-rotation matrix by the "Hue shift" degrees.
- Lines: segments between two points are rasterised every half a cell, each cell getting a stroke glyph chosen from the segment angle ("-", "\\", "|" or "/"), optionally ending in a custom glyph. Dots put one glyph in one cell. Spots are single solid cells with their own fill and glyph (used for eyes, written as "●").

Trails: a per-cell energy field. Animals "shed" energy into the cell under a point (amount × "Trail" tuning, capped at 1.6); taps and landings "stamp" a round blob of radius r cells (rows weighted 1.4×). Each frame the field is diffused (new = (4 × self + 4 neighbours) ÷ 8) and decays by exp(−dt × "Trail fade"). It is drawn as small squares (size max(2, round(0.19 × cw)) px, one larger above 0.6 energy) centred at 50%/60% of each cell, in six alpha steps of the species' trail colour (alpha 0.85 × step/6), with a gentle per-cell twinkle (× 0.75 + 0.25 sin(5t + hash × 40)). Trail squares never draw over solid cells.

## 7. The flock (shared motion system)

- Fixed-step simulation at 60 Hz (accumulator, at most 4 steps per frame, dt capped at 0.1 s). Drawing happens every requestAnimationFrame; the loop pauses when the canvas is not intersecting the viewport and never runs under reduced motion.
- base size = clamp(min(viewport w, h) × 0.2, 80, 190) × species scale. Each animal has a random "roll" 0–1; depth = farthest + (1 − farthest) × roll^farBias; span = base × depth × size. Animals are kept sorted by roll so near ones draw last (on top).
- Population: target = clamp(round(w × h ÷ (area × (base ÷ scale ÷ 160)²) × density), 1, 200). Extra animals are removed at random; new ones spawn off-screen on the upwind edge (or, on first load and half of later spawns, anywhere on screen).
- Course: the travel direction in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up) from the species' "Direction", or, if "Corner to corner" is on, the bottom-left-to-top-right diagonal of the window. The group heading sways: course + sway × (sin(0.13t) + 0.5 sin(0.31t + 1.7)). Each animal has a bias in −1..1 multiplied by "Spread".
- Steering: acceleration toward (cos aim, sin aim) × speed minus current velocity, times a gain; separation pushes apart animals within (spanA + spanB) × reach whose depths differ by less than 0.18, strength = "Separation"; speed is capped (plus 300 px/s while startled). cruise speed = species speed × (0.55 + 0.45 × depth) × "Speed". The heading turns toward the velocity at a limited rate.
- Wrapping: when an animal has passed the downwind edge by one span (or is three spans off-screen anywhere) it re-enters on the upwind edge, placed along the edges in proportion to their exposure to the course.
- Tap / click (pointerdown on the canvas only, ignored under reduced motion): stamps a 6-cell trail burst of 1.4 at the point and startles every animal within 240 px with strength k = 1 − distance/240 (each species reacts in its own way below), unless the species overrides taps (Sea turtle drops food instead).

Species that hide a control (Shimmer for Squid and Owl, Hold course for Flying fish) leave it out.
- Each row is a two-column grid: label and a Geist Mono 600 11px value (decimals from the step size), with the slider spanning beneath. Sliders: 18px tall, 4px track whose left part (up to the value, via a --fill percentage) is the accent colour and the rest --chip-edge; 14px white thumb with a faint border and shadow. Toggles: 30 × 18 px switch, accent when on, a 14px knob sliding 12px. Disabled rows fade to 40%.
- Hovering or focusing a row shows a tooltip to the left of the panel (max 240px, radius 12px, background #0e101aeb) with the hint text plus "Double-click the name to reset it." Double-clicking a label resets that value.
- Changes apply live. Detail triggers a resize; hue and grid repaint the cached background. Settings that differ from the species defaults are saved per species in localStorage under "wild-tab:tweaks:<species>" (tuning plus glass), and the open/closed state under "wild-tab:tweaks-open" (closed by default). Copy writes those changes as pretty JSON to the clipboard ("Copied", or "In console" if the clipboard is refused), reverting after 1.4 s. Reset asks "Reset all?" (red confirm styling) for 3 s and on a second click restores every default and clears storage. Another tab saving the same key reloads the page.
- Switching species rebuilds the flock with that species' defaults plus its saved tweaks, rebuilds the panel, clears the trail field and remembers the choice in localStorage "wild-tab:animal". A "?animal=<key>" URL parameter (moths, rabbits, turtles, squid, owls, flyingfish, eagles) picks the starting species, and "?count=N" fixes the number of animals.

## 10. Reduced motion and robustness

- Under prefers-reduced-motion the animation loop never starts: the flock is simulated silently for 4 s (240 steps) and one frame is drawn, re-drawn whenever a tweak changes, the window resizes or the preference flips; taps do nothing. Switching the preference off resumes animation.
- A ResizeObserver on the canvas re-sizes the grid and population; an IntersectionObserver pauses the loop when hidden. All localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch so the page works when storage is blocked.

## 11. Acceptance checklist

- One HTML file, no network requests beyond the embedded fonts, no console errors.
- At 1440×900: the species bar is centred at the top with Moth selected, the avatar, "Good … , Rosalie" and the 720px composer sit in the middle, Tweaks is top-right and the hint bottom-left; moths fill the grid flying toward the top-right.
- Each of the seven pills switches instantly to that species, with its own shape, colours, motion, direction and Tweaks group; the highlight slides to the chosen pill with a slight overshoot.
- Clicking empty space scatters animals (moths kick away, rabbits bolt, owls swoop, squid jet, flying fish leap away, eagles are pushed), drops food for the sea turtles, and leaves a trail burst.
- On a 375px phone and a 320px phone all seven pills are visible on two rows, nothing overlaps, nothing scrolls sideways; Tweaks opens as a bottom sheet. On a landscape phone the avatar hides and everything fits. With reduced motion a single still frame shows.

### Runtime clean-up of the cut sheets (required)

The background remover leaves white inside each hanger's triangle. On load, load the white-background sheet and its cut version with `crossOrigin="anonymous"` into two canvases (same size), then for each sprite, only in the zone from 60 px above the sprite's top to 34% of its height (and 30 px either side):

1. **Front sheet only (pockets):** flood-fill 4-connected components of pixels whose white-sheet RGB are all ≥ 253 and whose cut alpha > 0. Any component larger than `250·f²` px (f = loaded width / 3504) gets alpha 0.
2. **Both sheets (haze):** four passes over the same zone. A pixel with min(RGB) ≥ 232 in the white sheet and max−min ≤ 16 gets alpha 0 if its cut alpha < 225 or any 4-neighbour already has alpha 0.

Export the cleaned canvas with `toBlob(..., "image/webp", .92)`, put it on the root as CSS variables `--sheet` (front) and `--side` (side), and use `var(--sheet)` / `var(--side)` as each sprite's `background-image`. Start with the raw cut URLs and swap when ready. Wait for both (failsafe 10 s) before showing the dresses. Then preload both model sheets.

## 5. The dresses

Scale: sheet px × **S = 0.44** = stage px. The hook line is **HOOK_Y = 291**. The usable rail runs **RAIL_L = 347** for **RAIL_W = 970** px. **FLOOR = 838** is the lowest a pulled-forward hem may reach.

Each dress is a zero-size wrapper `.dress` at `left: cx (hook x), top: 291`, z-index = index + 1, `transition: left .34s var(--ease), opacity .22s linear`. It holds two layers (`.art`, absolute, background from the sheet):

- `.side`, from the side sheet with row top 54/1192:
  - placement: `left = −(hookX − x)·S`, `top = (y − rowTop)·S`
  - size: `w·S × h·S`
  - background: `background-size: 3504S × 2336S`, `background-position: −x·S −y·S`
  - `transform-origin: (hookX − x)·S  −(y − rowTop)·S`, which is the hook point
- `.front`, the same construction from the front sheet with row top 42/1202.

Both layers get `filter: drop-shadow(0 7px 9px rgba(96,52,38,.16))` and the transition `transform .22s var(--ease), opacity .18s linear, filter .22s var(--ease)`.

- **Rest:** `.side` opacity 1, no transform. `.front` opacity 0, `transform: scaleX(.58)`.
- **Hovered (`.on`):** wrapper z 40 (!important).
  - `.side` → opacity 0, `scale(var(--k)) scaleX(.55)` (it squeezes out).
  - `.front` → opacity 1, `scale(var(--k))` (it opens up into the front view and grows from the hook), shadow `drop-shadow(0 22px 24px rgba(96,52,38,.26))`.
  - Per-dress `--k = min(1.42, (838 − 291) / (frontH·S))`, so short dresses grow 1.42× and long gowns stop with the hem at y 838.

### Slots (`place()`)

The dresses still on the rail are laid out left to right in slots:

- **At rest:** every slot is `970/n`, and the dress sits in the slot centre: `cx = RAIL_L + (k + .5)·step`.
- **One dress hovered:** its slot is `G = min(frontW·S·k·0.8 + 28, 970·0.42)` and the others share `(970 − G)/(n − 1)`. This pushes the dresses on its left further left and the ones on its right further right; the `left` transition animates the push.
- The hit buttons take the same slots: `left = slot start, width = slot width`.

### Put in bag: the fly into the bag (as in the original reel)

1. The button turns to "In your bag ✓" (`#5E3A30`). After 380 ms the window closes, with the blur and scrim fading.
2. Disable the hit columns. Make sure the chosen dress is hovered: front-on, pulled forward, neighbours pushed. Hide the sticker. On phones, smooth-scroll the rail to `left: 0` so the bag is on screen.
3. Animate the dress wrapper with Web Animations: delay 420 ms, duration 820 ms, `cubic-bezier(.45,.05,.55,.95)`, fill forwards.
   - Distances: `dx = 186 − cx` and `dy = 712 − 291 − frontH·S·k·0.16·0.55`. The bag mouth is at stage (186, 712).

     - 0: `translate(0,0) scale(1)`

     - .48: `translate(.45dx, .2dy) scale(.6)`
     - .76: `translate(.85dx, .72dy) scale(.3)`

     - 1: `translate(dx, dy + 46px) scale(.144)`
   - At 55% of the flight add `.flying` (z 26, below the bag's z 30), so it drops in behind the bag's front.
4. **On finish:**
   - Bag dip-and-settle, 420 ms ease-out: `translateY(0) scale(1,1)` → (.35) `translateY(4px) scale(1.05,.95)` → (.7) `translateY(-2px) scale(.98,1.02)` → none.

# Letterbloom: poppy type garden (recreation brief)

Build a single, self-contained, full-screen web page called **Letterbloom**: a generative type toy where everything you type is set as one huge serif word in the centre of a flat dark field, and poppies grow out of every letter. Stems are drawn on like ink, weave over and under the letters, end in poppies that spring open petal by petal, in seed pods, feathery leaves or spiral curls. Space cuts the stems and makes the word finish with a little burst of blooms, Backspace withers the last letter, Enter clears the field. A white butterfly flies in when you click and perches on a poppy. Stems and poppies lean toward the cursor. A second mode, Poster, renders the same garden as a 1080 × 1080 looping animation with seven motion presets and exports MP4 or PNG frames.

Everything is drawn live on a 2D canvas with plain JavaScript: there are no images, no videos and no libraries. The only external assets are two Google Fonts.

## 1. Assets and fonts

| Asset | Source | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Playfair Display 600 (latin) | https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Playfair+Display:wght@600&display=swap | The typed word on the canvas, the "Poster" panel heading, the poster Words input, the "Aa" in palette cards |
| DM Mono 400 and 500 (latin) | https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=DM+Mono:wght@400;500&display=swap | All interface text: wordmark, mode toggle, hints, buttons, poster panel |

Self-host the latin WOFF2 files (or embed them as base64 data URIs) with font-display: swap. Canvas font string: weight 600, size S px, family "Playfair Display", Georgia, serif. When document.fonts finishes loading "600 100px Playfair Display", clear the glyph-width cache, re-run the layout and rebuild the poster garden. No other media: no image or video URLs are used anywhere.

Head: title "Letterbloom", meta description "Type, and poppies grow from your letters. Space cuts the stems, backspace withers them.", viewport width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content, theme-color set live to the current background, an empty data: favicon.

## 2. Palettes

## 4. Type layout

Letters are laid out by measuring each glyph at 100 px in the canvas font and caching width/100 per character (a space counts 1.4 × its measured width).

- Maximum line width maxW = 80% of the viewport width (68% when the viewport is narrower than 600 px). Base size S0 = 28% of the viewport height. Line height = 2.1 × size.
- Size S = min(S0, maxW ÷ total width at size 1). If there are two or more words and S would drop below 10% of the height (or below 14% if the text was already wrapped), wrap instead: binary-search (22 iterations) the largest size between 3% and 15% of the height where greedy word wrapping keeps every line within maxW and lines × 2.1 × size ≤ 82% of the height.
- Each line is centred horizontally (trailing spaces ignored). Baseline of line k of n: y = H/2 + (k − (n−1)/2) × lineHeight + 0.33 × S. Each letter stores its target centre x, baseline y and width.
- Every frame, the drawn size, each letter's position and the caret ease toward their targets with k = 1 − e^(−dt/80) (dt capped at 64 ms), so letters glide when the word grows, shrinks or wraps. On resize everything snaps.
- Letters are drawn with fillText, centred, alphabetic baseline, in the type colour.
- **Caret**: a bar 0.8 × S tall and max(2, 0.03 × S) wide in the type colour, centred at x = last letter's right edge + 0.07 × S and y = baseline − 0.33 × S (or the screen centre when empty). Its height grows in with ease-out cubic over 600 ms after load. It blinks with a 530 ms period but stays solid for 500 ms after any keystroke.

## 5. Input

- On desktop the hidden input is focused 50 ms after load and again on every pointerdown in the app, so typing works immediately. Ctrl/Cmd+S saves a PNG, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S saves an SVG.
- Printable key: add the letter. Space: cut (below). Backspace: wither the last live letter. Enter: clear all letters. Keys with Ctrl/Meta/Alt are ignored, as are Enter/Space while a button has focus.
- Phones: tapping the canvas focuses the input to open the keyboard. Because mobile keyboards often write into the field instead of firing key events, the field is mirrored: on each input event compare the field with its previous value, wither one letter per removed character, add each new character (a newline clears), then reset the field to the sentinel (during IME composition keep the composing text and diff when it ends). A keydown that was already handled sets a flag for one tick so the input event is ignored.
- Phones also track window.visualViewport: the app's top and height follow the visible area (CSS variables), and if the keyboard closes while the field still has focus the field is blurred so the next tap reopens it.

## 6. How a letter grows

All randomness uses a seeded mulberry32 generator. Each word gets a random word seed; every letter in a word shares it plus its index, so a word has one character. Per-word parameters (from the word seed): poppy chance 0.24–0.46, leafiness 0.6–1.4, lean −0.3…0.3, bloom scale 0.85–1.3, curviness 0.8–1.4, bridge chance 0.45–0.8 (capped 0.95). All geometry is in units of the type size S, relative to the letter's baseline centre (negative y is up). w = the letter's width in S units.

**Vine path**: 40 steps of equal length from a base point in a start direction; at step fraction u the heading is dir + bend × u + amp × sin(u × π × waves + phase) × min(1, 3u), with amp = (0.35–0.8) × curviness, waves 1–2.6, bend −0.6…0.6. A "curl" tip appends a 1.6-turn spiral (14 points, radius 0.05–0.10 shrinking to half) to either side.

**Weave**: each stem is split at 1–3 random points (between 15% and 85% of its length) into segments that alternate between behind the letters (layer 0) and in front (layer 1); 30% of the cuts leave a 2–5% gap. Leaves and tips take the layer of the segment they sit on.

**Per letter**:
- 1 upward stem (a second with probability 0.45): base x random within ±35% of the letter width, base y 0 to −0.3, direction straight up ± lean/2 ± 0.35 rad, length 0.6–1.1, delays 40 ms and 170 ms. The first letter of every word always ends its first stem in a poppy.
- 40% chance of a downward stem: base y −0.1 to −0.45, direction down ± 0.4 rad, length 0.35–0.7, delay 160 ms.
- If the letter follows another in the same word, with the bridge chance: a cubic Bézier from a point inside this letter to a point inside the previous one (both at y −0.05 to −0.6), bulging up or down by 0.4–0.8; 45% of the time it is cut short to 70–90% of its length. Delay 90 ms; its tip is a curl (50%), a leaf (25%) or a poppy (25%).
- The first letter of a word also grows a side curl pointing left (base x −0.3w, length 0.45–0.75, delay 120 ms).
- Every letter also keeps one hidden tendril curl (base x +0.25w, direction ±0.7 rad sideways, length 0.45–0.7). It is drawn only while the letter is the last letter of its word, growing in with ease-out cubic over 450 ms after a 150 ms delay. When a letter is followed by another, it disappears.

**Each stem** draws on from its base with ease-out cubic over max(320, length × 620) ms after its delay. Width 0.017 × S (82% for side branches). It carries 0–2 fine hairs (short strokes 0.035 × S long, 0.012 × S wide, angled 2.5 rad off the stem) that appear once the stroke passes them. 0–3 leaves sit along it (count floor(random × 2.8 × leafiness)) at 25–85% of its length, alternating sides, angled 0.55–1.05 rad off the stem, length 0.14–0.34 (×0.8 on branches), each appearing as the stem reaches it. 30% of top-level stems fork once into a side branch from 35–70% of their length (length 35–55% of the parent, starting in the parent's layer).

**Tips** (when not forced): poppy with the word's poppy chance, otherwise pod 45%, leaf 15% (of the remainder), else curl. Tips appear at 80% of the stem's draw time.
- **Poppy**: radius R = (0.17–0.33) × bloom scale (×0.75 on branches). A poppy whose centre sits over the letter body (y between −0.78 and 0.05 and within half the letter width) goes behind the letters 78% of the time; elsewhere it is in front 60% of the time. 10% of poppies get a smaller twin (60–90% size) beside them, 120 ms later.
- **Pod**: length 0.11–0.16, pointing along the stem.
- **Leaf**: length 0.16–0.32, pointing along the stem.

**Space** (cut): the last letter of the word gets 1–3 extra side stems (fanned around up-and-right, length 0.4–0.85), each tipped with a poppy (the first always, others 50%) or a pod, starting when the cut happens. Its tendril recoils: its drawn length shrinks over 150 ms by min(0.85, 20 px ÷ (0.6 × S)).

**Backspace** (wither): the last letter is marked dead; everything it grew scales down with ease-out cubic over 260 ms, then it is removed at 300 ms. The previous letter (if in the same word) loses its cut blooms and regrows its tendril.

## 7. Drawing

All shapes are filled or stroked smooth paths: closed shapes go through the midpoints of consecutive points with quadratic curves; open strokes use round caps and joins.

**Hand-drawn boil**: every 120 ms (frame index floor(t/120)) each element gets a new pseudo-random offset of up to ±max(0.8, 1% of S) px in x and y and up to ±0.035 rad rotation, hashed from its id and the frame index, so linework trembles like a stop-motion drawing.

**Birth sway**: for 2.5 s after a letter is typed, every point of its garden is pushed sideways by 0.07 × S × h × e^(−3.2t) × sin(11t) and vertically by 0.035 × S × h × e^(−3.2t) × sin(11t + 1.2), where h is the point's height above the baseline in S units and odd/even letters sway in opposite directions.

**Cursor lean**: for each live letter, measure from a point 0.6 × S above its baseline to the pointer. Within reach = max(260, 3.2 × S) px, the lean vector is the unit direction × smoothstep(1 − d/reach). Each letter eases its lean toward that at 0.07 per frame. A point at height h (clamped 0–2.5) moves by lean × (0.1 × S, 0.05 × S) × (0.5h² + 0.5h), so tops of stems bend the most. Poppies also turn to face the pointer: within 300 px the face vector is the direction × smoothstep × min(1, d/40), eased at 0.09 per frame; it squashes the flower along that direction (factor −0.28 × strength), shifts its inner layers toward the pointer, and adds 0.22 × x-component to its rotation. On touch, the lean relaxes when the finger lifts. Leaving the window clears the pointer.

**Feathery leaf**: a blade along its axis (with a slight bend of up to 0.6 × 0.15 × length), half-width = 0.3 × L × sin(π × u^0.8) × (0.28 + 0.72 × tooth), where tooth is a sawtooth with 5.5 teeth (rising for 70% of each tooth, dropping for 30%), the two sides offset by 0.09 so the teeth alternate; 44 points per side; filled in the stem colour; a centre vein from 5% to 85% of its length in the background colour, width max(0.7, 0.022 × L). Leaves spring in: scale = 1 − e^(−7t) cos(15t) (t in seconds from its delay).

**Seed pod** (length L = pod size × S × spring, same spring as leaves): an oval capsule from the stem tip outward (centre 0.55L, radii 0.55L along and 0.44L across), a flat crown disc at 1.12L (radii 0.1L by 0.36L), five short crown rays from 1.06L fanning out to 1.24L, all in the stem colour; three thin rib lines along the capsule in the background colour, width max(0.7, 0.045 × L).

**Poppy** (radius R in px, rotation −0.5…0.5 rad, two random phases): four petals, back to front: left-back (−0.42, −0.24; radii 0.6 × 0.56; −0.4 rad), right-back (0.44, −0.22; 0.6 × 0.56; +0.4 rad), left-front (−0.38, 0.24; 0.6 × 0.5; +0.3 rad; depth 0.12), right-front (0.4, 0.26; 0.6 × 0.5; −0.3 rad; depth 0.12), all in units of R. Each petal is a 34-point ellipse whose radius is crinkled by 1 + 0.045 sin(5θ + phase1 + i) + 0.03 sin(9θ + phase2) + 0.012 sin(15θ + 2i), filled in the flower colour.
- Each petal opens 85 ms after the previous with spring s = 1 − e^(−8t) cos(14t): it scales from the base point (0, 0.45R) by s and starts rotated 0.5 rad outward, settling as s reaches 1.
- Petal lines (only when R ≥ 10): once a petal's spring passes 0.4, three fine lines per petal draw on over the next half of the spring, radiating from the centre toward the petal at angle offsets −0.32, +0.05 and +0.36 rad, from 32% to 100% of a reach of (centre distance + 0.55–0.65 × petal radius), slightly bowed; flower-line colour, width 0.032R (middle line 0.9 ×, outer 0.75 ×).
- Centre: 80 ms after the last petal starts, a progress value grows with ease-out cubic over 520 ms. A dark core disc of radius 0.24R × progress (slightly wavy, 86% as tall as wide) at (0, −0.02R) in the core colour; when R ≥ 9 a ring of 11 stamen dots (radius 0.045R) at 0.33R from the centre pops in one after another; on top, a small seed-cap disc (0.085R × 0.075R) in the stem colour.
- Inner parts are lifted toward the pointer by depth (petals 0–0.12, core 0.3, cap 0.36) for the turning effect.

**Butterfly** (size s = max(14, 0.15 × S)): four wing ellipses per side (lower wing centre (0.46, 0.28), radii 0.36 × 0.3, tilted 0.5; upper wing centre (0.55, −0.32), radii 0.55 × 0.36, tilted −0.55), slightly wavy, filled in the type colour and compressed horizontally by 0.12 + 0.88 × open; when open > 0.3 each upper wing gets a flower-colour tip spot and two fine dark veins (background colour); a slim body ellipse (0.07 × 0.46) and two curved antennae in the stem colour.
- Clicking the canvas spawns one (max 6; the oldest leaves when a 7th comes). It enters from the nearer side edge at a random height and flies to the nearest free poppy that has been open for over 700 ms, landing 0.55R above its centre. Flight: steering speed min(0.34, 0.06 + 0.0016 × distance) px/ms, velocity eased at 0.06 per 16 ms, flutter wobble sin(7t) × 0.12 and cos(4.3t) × 0.1, vertical bob sin(13t) × 0.6 px, body tilt following horizontal velocity (±0.5 rad), wingbeat |cos(17t)|. Perched: it follows the poppy, wings mostly half closed (0.25 + 0.15 sin), with a short fast flapping burst whenever sin(0.9t + seed) > 0.75. If its poppy disappears it flies off up and out. With no poppy available it wanders around the click point for 3.5 s and leaves.

**Planted poppies**: double-clicking or double-tapping the canvas (two taps within 340 ms and 40 px, at most one plant per 1.8 s) plants a free-standing poppy (0.24 × S, random rotation) at that spot that blooms like the others and lasts 60 s, fading and sinking over its last 2.2 s. At most 14 at once.

**Draw order each frame**: fill the background; all layer-0 stems, leaves, pods and poppies; the letters; all layer-1 elements; butterflies; planted poppies; the caret.

## 8. Exports

- **PNG**: renders the current frame without the caret and downloads the canvas as letterbloom.png.
- **SVG**: re-runs the same drawing into SVG paths (fills and round-capped strokes, coordinates rounded to 0.01) over a background rect, with letters as text elements in Playfair Display 600, and downloads letterbloom.svg.

## 9. Poster mode

Clicking "Poster" switches to a two-column screen (background #111110, cursor default, DM Mono 12 px, letter-spacing 0.03em, text #EDEDED): a left panel minmax(280 px, 340 px) wide (#161615, 1 px right border #262624, padding 24 px 22 px 32 px, 26 px gaps, scrolls) and a stage that centres a 1080 × 1080 canvas shown at min(100%, 100vh − 104 px) with a 1 px #262624 border and 64 px top padding. The text typed in Type mode becomes the poster words (default "red poppy").

Panel, top to bottom:
- "Poster" in Playfair Display 600, 26 px, white; under it in #8C8C88 "1:1 · <loop seconds>s loop · 30 fps".
- Section label "WORDS" (11 px uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em, #8C8C88); an input in Playfair Display 600 22 px (bg #0E0E0D, 1 px #2E2E2C border, radius 10 px, padding 10 px 12 px, border white on focus) that rebuilds the garden on change (max 40 characters); a "Regrow garden" outline pill that picks a new random seed.
- "MOTION": a two-column grid of seven cards (radius 10 px, 1 px #2E2E2C border, padding 10 px 12 px; title 13 px, subtitle 11 px #8C8C88; selected = white border on #1E1E1C): Breathe "Slow sway · 3s", Grow & wither "Bloom, then back · 6s", Typed "Type, cut, repeat · 5s", Gust "Wind sweeps through · 4s", Reach "Stems follow a light · 6s", Scatter "Random bloom, fade · 6s", Visitor "Butterfly drops by · 7s".
- "PALETTE": a two-column grid of the ten palettes as cards (radius 12 px, padding 6 px 6 px 8 px), each with a 44 px preview strip in the palette background showing an 18 px flower dot, a 12 px stem dot overlapping it by 4 px, and "Aa" in Playfair 18 px in the type colour, with the name below; the selected card has a white border.
- "EXPORT · 1080 × 1080 LOOP" (1 px #262624 top border, 20 px padding): a white filled pill "Export MP4 loop" (or WebM, black 500-weight text, padding 12 px 14 px), an outline pill "PNG frames (.zip)", and a status line.

The poster garden is generated from the words with a seed (7 by default), laid out with the same rules on a 1080 square, then scaled (up to 1.25 ×) and centred on the type so the whole garden fits inside a 6% margin (half-size 0.44 × 1080). It loops continuously; time t runs modulo the preset length T. Letters are always shown in full.
- **Breathe (3 s)**: fully grown. Each point sways x by sin(φ + 0.004 x_letter + 1.1h) × 0.03 S × h and y by cos(φ + 0.003x) × 0.008 S × h, with φ = 2π t/T; leaves and poppies rotate sin(φ + 0.7 id) × 0.12 rad.
- **Grow & wither (6 s)**: letters are "typed" every min(110, 3000/n) ms starting at 200 ms, words are cut at spaces, and from 4.2 s letters wither one by one from the end (spacing min(60, 900/n) ms, 600 ms wither).
- **Typed (5 s)**: letters appear one by one every min(85, 3600/n) ms from 300 ms with a blinking caret (400 ms period); the frame goes blank after 4.4 s and restarts.
- **Gust (4 s)**: a wind front sweeps from x = −35% to 155% of the width; points ahead of it barely move, points behind it ring out (e^(2.2d) cos(9d)), with an idle sway of 0.012; displacement scales with height.
- **Reach (6 s)**: a small light disc (0.09 S, flower-line colour) travels a figure-eight (x = 540 + 430 sin φ, y = 540 + 260 sin 2φ) and stems within 560 px bend toward it.
- **Scatter (6 s)**: letters bloom at random times between 150 ms and 2.55 s and wither from 4.7 s.
- **Visitor (7 s)**: a gentle sway while a butterfly flies in from the left (1.8 s arc), perches on the poppy a quarter of the way across (until 3.4 s, a wing flap at 2.4–2.8 s), hops to the poppy three-quarters across (to 4.6 s), rests (flap at 5–5.3 s), and flies out to the top right.

**Export**: MP4 (avc1 if supported, else WebM) is recorded from an offscreen 1080 canvas with MediaRecorder at 14 Mbps, 30 frames per second of loop, frames drawn deterministically one per 1/30 s; the button shows progress and then "Saved MP4 · N frames". PNG frames renders the same frames to PNGs and downloads them as a stored (uncompressed) ZIP built in the browser, named letterbloom-<words>-<preset>-frames.zip.

Clicking "Type" returns to the live garden and refocuses the input.

With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the boil is turned off, every growth, spring, sway and wither is shown in its finished state (time is advanced past all animations), the caret appears at full height, and the swatch and button transitions are removed. Typing still adds and removes letters instantly.
